metadata.title: $K$-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs

extraction_notes.note: The unnumbered intro theorems 1-7 (thm environments) and intro Definition 1.3 restate Theorems 4.36, 6.5, 6.1, 6.11, 5.26, 5.5, Corollary 2.15 and Definition 3.12; only the body copies are nodes. Their \ref's occur only in intro prose.
Remark 2.14 is entirely an alternative proof of Lemma 2.5; typed proof (with a proves edge) rather than remark.

Non-standard environments: Constructions 3.18 and 4.5 typed definition (3.18 also asserts existence properties, could be a cited theorem), Construction 4.17 typed remark, Example 3.3 is a definition, Question typed open_problem, Variant typed definition.

Theorem 5.26 is proved in Corollary 5.32 except its p-torsion-freeness, deferred to Corollary 5.33, whose proof reads part (1) off Theorem 5.26's isomorphism; the parts sit in one sentence and cannot be separate claims, so this graph cycle is kept.
The sentence stating the Cartier isomorphism also defines 'ind-smooth'; it cannot be split, so 'ind-smooth' has no separate definition node.
The proof of Lemma 4.20 is one inline claim followed by two sentences; nesting (step rule 7) would leave a single top-level step, so the three sentences are flat steps.
Historical lists (special cases of Theorem 2 in the introduction, the seven known continuity cases in 5.1) and discursive motivation paragraphs are not nodes.

nodes.name: K^inv: fiber of the cyclotomic trace
nodes.statement: For a ring $R$, we write $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)$ for the homotopy fiber of the cyclotomic trace $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$.

nodes.name: Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy theorem
nodes.statement_short: K^inv is invariant under surjections with nilpotent kernel.
assumptions: Let $R \to R'$ be a map of rings which is a surjection with nilpotent kernel.
conclusions: the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R')$ is an equivalence
nodes.statement: Let $R \to R'$ be a map of rings which is a surjection with nilpotent kernel.\footnote{Or, more generally, a map of connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra such that $\pi_0R\rightarrow\pi_0R'$ is a surjection with nilpotent kernel} Then the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R')$ is an equivalence.
nodes.label: DGMthm

nodes.name: Gabber rigidity
nodes.statement_short: For a henselian pair with n invertible, K/n is unchanged by passing to R/I.
assumptions: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair.
Suppose $n$ is invertible in $R$.
conclusions: the map $K(R)/n \to K(R/I)/n$ is an equivalence of spectra
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair. Suppose $n$ is invertible in $R$. Then the map $K(R)/n \to K(R/I)/n$ is an equivalence of spectra.
nodes.label: gabberthm

nodes.name: Logarithmic forms
nodes.statement:
We let $\Omega^i_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ denote the subgroup of $\Omega^i_R$
consisting of elements which can be written as sums of products
of forms $dx/x$ for $x$ a unit.

nodes.name: Geisser--Levine theorem
nodes.statement_short: Mod p K-groups of a regular local F_p-algebra are the logarithmic forms.
conclusions: are identified with the logarithmic forms $\Omega^{i}_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ for $i \geq 0$
nodes.statement: The mod $p$ $K$-groups $K_i(R; \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}) = \pi_i( K(R)/p)$ are identified with the logarithmic forms $\Omega^{i}_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ for $i \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Category CAlg of commutative R-algebras
nodes.statement: The category of commutative algebras over a ring $R$ is denoted by $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/R}$.

nodes.name: The infinity-category of spectra Sp
nodes.statement:
We will let $\mathrm{Sp}$ denote the $\infty$-category of spectra, and write $\otimes$
for the smash product of spectra.

nodes.name: Sphere spectrum S^0
nodes.statement: The sphere spectrum will be denoted by $S^0\in\mathrm{Sp}$.

nodes.name: Mapping spectra Hom_C
nodes.statement:
In a stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$, we will write
$\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(\cdot, \cdot) \in \mathrm{Sp}$ for the mapping spectrum between any
two objects of $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: Connective and coconnective subcategories Sp_{>=r}, Sp_{<=r}
nodes.statement:
Given an integer $r$, we let $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq r}$ (resp.~$\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq r}$) for the
subcategory of $X \in\mathrm{Sp}$ such that $\pi_i(X) = 0$ for $i < r$ (resp.~$i>r$).

nodes.name: Truncation functors
nodes.statement:
We let 
$\tau_{\geq r}, \tau_{\leq r}$ denote the associated truncation functors.

nodes.name: Connective and nonconnective K-theory
nodes.statement:
We let $K$ denote connective $K$-theory and $\mathbb{K}$ denote its
nonconnective analog; $\mathrm{TC}$ denotes topological cyclic homology.

nodes.name: Relative K-theory K(R,I)
nodes.statement:
Given a ring $R$ and an ideal $I \subset R$, we let $K(R, I)$
(resp.~$\mathbb{K}(R, I)$) denote the relative $K$-theory (resp.~relative nonconnective
$K$-theory), defined  as $\mathrm{fib}(K(R) \to K(R/I))$ and
$\mathrm{fib}(\mathbb{K}(R) \to \mathbb{K}(R/I))$.

nodes.name: Relative K^inv and TC
nodes.statement:
We define $ K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R, I), \mathrm{TC}(R, I)$
similarly.

nodes.name: K-theory with mod p^r coefficients
nodes.statement:
Finally, following traditional practice in algebraic $K$-theory, we
will sometimes write $K_*(R; \mathbb{Z}/p^r \mathbb{Z})$ for the mod $p^r$
homotopy of the spectrum $K(R)$ (i.e., $\pi_*( K(R)/p^r)$) and similarly for
$\mathrm{TC}$.

nodes.name: Hochschild and topological Hochschild homology
nodes.statement:
Given a ring $R$, we can form both its Hochschild homology $\mathrm{HH}(R/\mathbb{Z})$
and its topological Hochschild homology spectrum $\mathrm{THH}(R)$.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement_short: A spectrum with S^1-action and S^1-equivariant Frobenius maps X -> X^{tC_p} for every prime p.
nodes.statement: A {\em cyclotomic spectrum} is a tuple $$ (X , \, \{\varphi_{X, p}: X \to X^{tC_p}\}_{p = 2, 3, 5, \dots }),$$ where $X \in \mathrm{Fun}(BS^1, \mathrm{Sp})$ is a spectrum with an $S^1$-action which is moreover equipped with a map $\varphi_p:X\to X^{tC_p}$ (the {\em cyclotomic Frobenius} at $p$), for each prime number $p$, which is required to be equivariant with respect to the $S^1$-action on $X$ and the $S^1\simeq S^1/C_p$-action on the Tate construction $X^{tC_p}$. By a standard abuse of notation we will occasionally denote a cyclotomic spectrum simply by the underlying spectrum $X$. For the precise definition of the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{CycSp}$ of cyclotomic spectra (whose objects are as above) as a lax equalizer, we refer the reader to \cite[II.1]{nikolaus-scholze}. See \cite[IV.2]{nikolaus-scholze} for a treatment of the symmetric monoidal structure.

nodes.name: Structure of the infinity-category of cyclotomic spectra
nodes.statement_short: CycSp is presentably symmetric monoidal and the forgetful functor to Sp is conservative, exact and colimit-preserving.
nodes.statement:
The $\infty$-category $\mathrm{CycSp}$ naturally has the structure of a presentably
symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category\footnote{Meaning, a presentable $\infty$-category with symmetric monoidal tensor product commuting with colimits in each variable separately; or in other words a commutative algebra object in $\operatorname{Pr}^L$ with respect to Lurie's tensor product.} and the tensor product recovers the smash
product on the level of underlying spectra with $S^1$-action. Moreover, the
forgetful functor $\mathrm{CycSp}\to \mathrm{Sp}$ reflects equivalences, is exact, and preserves
all colimits.

nodes.name: Topological cyclic homology (Nikolaus--Scholze)
nodes.statement_short: TC(X) is the mapping spectrum Hom_CycSp(1, X); TC^- and TP are homotopy fixed points and Tate construction.
nodes.statement: Given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, its \emph{topological cyclic homology} $\mathrm{TC}(X) $ is defined as the mapping spectrum $\mathrm{TC}(X) = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{CycSp}}(\mathbf{1}, X)$, where $\mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ is the unit (cf.~Definition \ref{cons_trivial}). We moreover write \[ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) = X^{hS^1}, \quad \mathrm{TP}(X) = X^{tS^1}\] for its {\em negative topological cyclic homology} and \emph{periodic topological cyclic homology}, the latter having been particularly studied by Hesselholt \cite{hesselholt-tp}.
nodes.label: definition_TC_via_NS

nodes.name: Bounded-below cyclotomic spectra CycSp_{>=n}
nodes.statement: Given $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Sp}$ consisting of those spectra $X$ that satisfy $\pi_i(X) = 0$ for $i < n$. Let $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathrm{CycSp}$ consisting of those cyclotomic spectra $(X, \{\varphi_{X,p}\}_{p = 2, 3, 5, \dots} )$ such that the underlying spectrum $X$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$.

nodes.name: Canonical map and Frobenius TC^- -> TP
nodes.statement:
Here $\mathrm{can}_X$ is the canonical map from homotopy fixed points to the Tate
construction, while $\varphi_X$ arises from taking $S^1$-homotopy-fixed points
in the cyclotomic structure map $X \to X^{tC_p}$ and using a version of the Tate orbit lemma
to identify 
$X^{tS^1} \simeq (X^{tC_p})^{h(S^1/C_p)}$ since $X$ is bounded below and $p$-complete \cite[Lem.~II.4.2]{nikolaus-scholze}.

nodes.name: Nikolaus--Scholze formula for TC
nodes.statement_short: For bounded-below p-complete X, TC(X) is the equalizer of can and phi from TC^- to TP.

nodes.name: Nikolaus--Scholze formula for TC
nodes.statement_short: TC(X) is the fiber of can - phi: TC^-(X) -> TP(X).
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X) = \mathrm{fib}( \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{can}_X - \varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X)),
nodes.label: keyformula

nodes.name: THH of a ring as a cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement: A key source of examples of cyclotomic spectra arises as follows. If $R$ is a ring (or, more generally, a structured ring spectrum), then one can form its topological Hochschild homology $\mathrm{THH}(R)$ as an object of $\mathrm{CycSp}$, following \cite[\S III.2]{nikolaus-scholze}. As usual, we will write $\mathrm{TC}(R), \mathrm{TC}^-(R), \mathrm{TP}(R)$ in place of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathrm{THH}(R)), \mathrm{TC}^-(\mathrm{THH}(R)), \mathrm{TP}(\mathrm{THH}(R))$.

nodes.name: Genuine fixed points TR^r with R, F, V
nodes.statement:
In particular, given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ which is $p$-complete, one extracts genuine fixed
point spectra $\mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p):=X^{C_{p^{r-1}}}$ for each $r\ge1$, which are related by Restriction ($R$), Frobenius ($F$), and Verschiebung ($V$) maps:
\[ R, F: \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \to \mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p) , \quad V: \mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p) \to
\mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p).\]

nodes.name: TR and the classical definition of TC
nodes.statement:
Setting $\mathrm{TR}(X;p):=\varprojlim_R\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p)$, then the topological cyclic
homology of $X$ is classically defined as \begin{equation} \mathrm{TC}(X)=\mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}(X;p)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}-F}\mathrm{TR}(X;p)).\end{equation}

nodes.name: Classical formula for TC
nodes.statement_short: TC(X) is the fiber of id - F on TR(X;p).
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X)=\mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}(X;p)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}-F}\mathrm{TR}(X;p)).
nodes.label: keyformulaclassical

nodes.name: Connectivity of TC
nodes.statement_short: TC lowers connectivity of a p-complete bounded-below cyclotomic spectrum by at most one.
assumptions: Suppose $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$ is $p$-complete.
conclusions: $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n-1}$
nodes.statement: Suppose $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$ is $p$-complete. Then $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n-1}$.
nodes.label: connectivity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement_short: Classical approach: reduce to TR via the formula and Milnor sequence, then induct with the isotropy cofiber sequence.
nodes.statement: Using formula (\ref{keyformulaclassical}), it suffices to show that $\mathrm{TR}(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$; using the Milnor sequence, it is therefore enough to prove that $\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$ and that the Restriction maps $R:\pi_n\mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \to \pi_n\mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p)$ are surjective for all $r\ge1$. But this inductively follows from the basic cofiber sequence (cf.~\cite[Th.~1.2]{Hesselholt}) \begin{equation} X_{hC_{p^r}} \to \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \stackrel{R}{\to} \mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \end{equation} and the observation that $X_{hC_{p^r}}\in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$.

nodes.name: Isotropy separation cofiber sequence
nodes.statement: X_{hC_{p^r}} \to \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \stackrel{R}{\to} \mathrm{TR}^r(X;p)
nodes.label: isotropysep

nodes.name: TC/p commutes with geometric realizations
conclusions: commutes with geometric realizations
nodes.statement: The functor $ \mathrm{TC}/p:\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ commutes with geometric realizations.
nodes.label: geometricreal

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.6
nodes.statement_short: Partial geometric realizations are finite colimits; connectivity from Lemma 2.5 bounds the error.
nodes.statement: A geometric realization of connective spectra agrees with its $n^{th}$ partial geometric realization in degrees $<n$. Since $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p=\mathrm{TC}(X/p)$ decreases connectivity at most by one by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, to show that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations it therefore suffices to show that it commutes with $n^{th}$ partial geometric realizations for all $n$. But these are finite colimits, and are thus preserved by $\mathrm{TC}/p$ since the latter is an exact functor.

nodes.name: Cocontinuity of TC/p
nodes.statement_short: TC/p commutes with all colimits on connective cyclotomic spectra.
conclusions: commutes with all colimits
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{TC}/p: \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, commutes with all colimits.
nodes.label: TCcommutes

nodes.name: TC commutes with inverse limits of towers
nodes.statement_short: For towers of connective cyclotomic spectra, limits exist in CycSp, are preserved by the forgetful functor, and TC commutes with them.
nodes.statement: There is also a dual assertion which is significantly easier. Suppose we have a tower $\dots \to X_3 \to X_2 \to X_1$ in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Then the inverse limit of the tower $\left\{X_i\right\}$ exists in $\mathrm{CycSp}$ (in fact, in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq -1}$) and is preserved by the forgetful functor $\mathrm{CycSp} \to \mathrm{Sp}$. Indeed, we have $(\varprojlim X_i)^{tC_p} \simeq \varprojlim X_i^{tC_p}$ because the $X_i$'s are uniformly bounded-below, and taking $C_p$-homotopy orbits behaves as a finite colimit in any range of degrees. Then we can appeal to the description of $\mathrm{CycSp}$ as a lax equalizer and \cite[Prop. II.1.5]{nikolaus-scholze}. In particular, it follows that if $X = \varprojlim X_i$ on the level of underlying spectra, then $\mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X_i)$.
nodes.label: TCinvlim

nodes.name: Trivial cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement_short: The symmetric monoidal cocontinuous functor Sp -> CycSp, X -> X^triv (trivial action, Frobenius X -> X^{hC_p} -> X^{tC_p}), right adjoint to TC.
nodes.statement: We have a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathrm{CycSp}$, so it receives a unique symmetric monoidal, cocontinuous functor \[ \mathrm{Sp} \to \mathrm{CycSp},\quad X \mapsto X^{\mathrm{triv}} \] whose right adjoint is the functor $\mathrm{TC}: \mathrm{CycSp} \to \mathrm{Sp}$. More explicitly, this functor $X \mapsto X^{\mathrm{triv}}$ can be identified as follows: $X^\sub{triv}$ has underlying spectrum $X$ equipped with the trivial $S^1$-action; there is therefore a resulting $S^1$-equivariant map $X \to X^{hC_p} = F(BC_{p+}, X)$, and the cyclotomic Frobenius at $p$ for $X^\sub{triv}$ is the composition $\varphi_{X,p}:X\to X^{hC_p} \to X^{tC_p}$. (Notation: when $X$ is a $p$-complete spectrum for a particular prime number $p$, we will tend to drop the $p$ from $\varphi_{X,p}$.) Compare the discussion on \cite[p. 126]{nikolaus-scholze}. For example, taking $X$ to be the sphere spectrum $S^0 \in \mathrm{Sp}$ obtains the {\em cyclotomic sphere spectrum}, which is moreover the unit $\mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$.
nodes.label: cons_trivial

nodes.name: TC^- and TP of HF_p^triv
nodes.statement_short: TC^-_*(HF_p^triv) = F_p[x] and TP_* = F_p[x^{+-1}] with |x| = -2, and can inverts x.
nodes.statement:
Calculating the $S^1$-homotopy fixed points and Tate construction of
$\mathbb{F}_p$, we find that
\[ \mathrm{TC}^-_*( H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) = \mathbb{F}_p[x], 
\quad \quad
\mathrm{TP}_*( H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) = \mathbb{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}], \quad \quad
\text{where}  \ |x|
= -2.
\]
The canonical map $\mathrm{TC}^-( H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}(
H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$ carries $x$ to $x$ (i.e., it is the localization inverting $x$).

nodes.name: Frobenius of HF_p^triv annihilates x
conclusions: annihilates $x$
nodes.statement: The Frobenius map $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}:\mathrm{TC}^-_*( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}_*(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$ annihilates $x$.
nodes.label: Frobvanish

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.10
nodes.statement_short: Compare with the Frobenius of HF_p via the Tate orbit lemma; degree -2 classes must vanish.
nodes.statement: There is a commutative diagram of spectra \[ \xymatrix{ \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]^-{\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}} \ar[d]& \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[d] \\ H\mathbb{F}_p \ar[r]_{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}} & H \mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p} }\] where the top row is obtained by taking $S^1$-homotopy fixed points on the bottom row via the Tate orbit lemma, \cite[Lem.~II.4.2]{nikolaus-scholze}. The right vertical map $\mathrm{TP}(H\mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})\to H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p}$ is an isomorphism in degree $-2$: indeed, the degree $-2$ generator is invertible in the source by the above calculation of $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})$, and therefore necessarily maps to a generator of $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p})$ by multiplicativity. Going both ways around the diagram and noting that of course $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb F_p)=0$, we find that $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}$ must be zero on $\pi_{-2}( \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}))$.

nodes.name: Cofiber sequences for circle actions on HZ-modules
nodes.statement_short: Three functorial cofiber sequences relating X^{hS^1}, X^{tS^1}, X_{hS^1} and X via multiplication by x.
assumptions: Let $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{Z}}(\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^1})$ be an $H \mathbb{Z}$-module spectrum equipped with an $S^1$-action.
nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{Z}}(\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^1})$ be an $H \mathbb{Z}$-module spectrum equipped with an $S^1$-action. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \stackrel{x}{\longrightarrow} X^{hS^1} \longrightarrow X, \] where the first map is given by multiplication by the generator $x \in \pi_{-2}(H \mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}) = H^2( \mathbb{CP}^\infty; \mathbb{Z})$. \item There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H \mathbb{Z}$-modules \[ X \to X_{hS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1} . \] \item There is moreover a functorial cofiber sequence \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x \mathrm{can}_X} X^{tS^1} \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}, \] where $\mathrm{can}_X: X^{hS^1} \to X^{tS^1}$ is the canonical map. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: cofiberofx

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.11
nodes.statement_short: Each sequence comes from module structures over HZ^{hS^1} and standard cofiber sequences.
nodes.statement: Assertion (1) is \cite[Lemma~IV.4.12]{nikolaus-scholze}, in view of the cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $\Sigma^{-2} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}$. For assertion (2), by \emph{loc.~cit.}, we have functorial equivalences $X^{tS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1} = X^{hS^1}[1/x]$. The fiber sequences $\Sigma (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1}$ and $\Sigma X_{hS^1} \to X^{hS^1} \to X^{tS^1}$ make $(H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$ into an $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} $-module and yield a natural equivalence $X_{hS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$. Using the fiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $H\mathbb{Z} \to (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} \Sigma^2 (H \mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$, we obtain the assertion (2). Assertion (3) follows from assertion (1) and from the cofiber sequence $X^{hS^1} \stackrel{\mathrm{can}_X}{\to} X^{tS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1}$, where we use that multiplication by $x$ is an equivalence on $X^{tS^1}$.

nodes.name: Fiber sequence TC(X) -> X -> X_{hS^1} for HF_p^triv-modules
assumptions: For $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}( \mathrm{CycSp})$
conclusions: there exists a functorial fiber sequence
nodes.statement: For $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}( \mathrm{CycSp})$, there exists a functorial fiber sequence \begin{equation} \mathrm{TC}(X) \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: functorialfibseq

nodes.name: Fiber sequence TC(X) -> X -> X_{hS^1}
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X) \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.12
nodes.statement_short: Linearity over the Frobenius of HF_p^triv and Lemma 2.10 kill phi after multiplication by x; compare cofibers.
nodes.statement: We show first that, for $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) $, the composition \begin{equation} \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X) \end{equation} is functorially nullhomotopic. In fact, since $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, we find that $\mathrm{TC}^-(X)$ is an $\mathrm{TC}^-( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, $\mathrm{TP}(X)$ is a $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, and the map $\varphi_X$ is $\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}$-linear. We obtain a resulting functorial commutative diagram, where the base-changes are along $\varphi_{ H \mathbb F_p}: \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$, \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .\end{equation} However $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}(x)$ vanishes, by Lemma~\ref{Frobvanish}, and so the composite \eqref{th} is functorially nullhomotopic as desired. It now follows that there is a functorial commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]_{x} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{id}} &\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)\ar[d]^{x \mathrm{can}_X} \\ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]_{\mathrm{can}_X-\varphi_X} & \mathrm{TP}(X) } \end{equation} in which the fiber of the bottom arrow is $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ by formula \eqref{keyformula}. Therefore $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ is also the fiber of the natural map $X \to X_{hS^1}$ between the cofibers of the vertical arrows in the above diagram, where we identify the cofibers using Lemma~\ref{cofiberofx}.

nodes.name: Composite Sigma^{-2}TC^- -> TC^- -> TP
nodes.statement: \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X)
nodes.label: th

nodes.name: Base-change diagram for the Frobenius
nodes.statement: \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .
nodes.label: cycdiag

nodes.name: Square comparing x and can - phi
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]_{x} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{id}} &\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)\ar[d]^{x \mathrm{can}_X} \\ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]_{\mathrm{can}_X-\varphi_X} & \mathrm{TP}(X) }
nodes.label: cyc2

nodes.name: TC commutes with colimits on HF_p^triv-modules
conclusions: commutes with all colimits
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) \to \mathrm{Sp}$ given by $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)$ commutes with all colimits. That is, the unit of the presentably symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp})$ is compact.
nodes.label: Fpcommutecolimit

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.13
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy orbits commute with colimits; apply Proposition 2.12.
nodes.statement: Since passage to homotopy orbits commutes with all colimits, this follows from Proposition \ref{functorialfibseq}.

nodes.name: Alternative proof of Lemma 2.5 via Nikolaus--Scholze
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to HF_p^triv-modules via Proposition 2.12, then HZ^triv-modules by p-completeness, then a general X via the Adams tower and the Milnor sequence.
nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$ be $p$-complete. Using the functorial fiber sequence of Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}, we can give an independent proof of Lemma~\ref{connectivity} (and thus of Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}) which is independent of the classical approach to $\mathrm{TC}$ (i.e., based entirely on the formula \eqref{keyformula}). Namely, we argue that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$. First, suppose that $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module. In this case, we find that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ thanks to Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}. More generally, if $X$ is a $p$-complete $H \mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, then we find that $X/p$ is an $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module so that $\mathrm{TC}(X/p) \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$; by $p$-completeness we deduce that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$. In general, let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ be an arbitrary $p$-complete object. Then, we consider the Adams tower for $X$ with respect to the commutative algebra object $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, i.e., the tower for the totalization of the cosimplicial object $X \otimes (H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}})^{\otimes \bullet + 1}$ (cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.1]{MNN17} for a reference in this generality). That is, we consider the tower $\left\{X_n\right\} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ defined inductively such that $X_0 = X$ and $X_{n+1}$ is the fiber of the map $X_{n} \to X_n \otimes H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$. One sees easily that $X_n \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$, and that $X_n$ is $p$-complete since $\pi_i(S^0)$ is finite for $i>0$. Since $X_{n}/X_{n+1}$ is a $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, it follows from the previous analysis that $\mathrm{TC}(X_n/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq (n-1)}$ for each $n$. Inductively, it follows now that $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) = \mathrm{TC}(X_0/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for each $n$ and that the maps $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) \to \mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n})$ are surjective on $\pi_{-1}$. Since $X \to X/X_{n+1}$ is an equivalence in degrees $\leq n$, it follows (as in \cite[Lem.~I.2.6]{nikolaus-scholze}) that \[ X^{hS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n )^{hS^1}, \quad X^{tS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n)^{tS^1} \] and therefore by \eqref{keyformula} \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X/X_n). \] Using the Milnor exact sequence and the connectivity properties of $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1})$, one concludes that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.label: rem:TCconnectivity

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.7
nodes.statement_short: Assembly map TC(X) tensor (-) -> TC(X tensor (-)^triv) is an equivalence on HF_p; then reduce to HF_p^triv-modules and use boundedness.
nodes.statement: Consider an $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete. Since $\mathrm{TC}(X\otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}})$ is an exact functor from spectra to spectra with value $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ on $S^0$, we get a natural transformation \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes (-) \to \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}}),\] uniquely characterized by being an equivalence on $S^0$, hence on any finite spectrum.\footnote{This is a standard ``assembly map". To construct it rigorously, note that left Kan extension of the restriction of the right hand side to finite spectra is uniquely characterized by its value on $S^0$, by the universal property of spectra among presentable stable $\infty$-categories, and therefore identifies with the left hand side.} By Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}, it is also an equivalence on any geometric realization of finite connective spectra, i.e., for any connective spectrum whose homology groups are finitely generated, e.g., $H \mathbb F_p$. So we have shown that, for any $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete, there is a natural equivalence $$\mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}).$$ Replacing $X$ with $X/p$, the same conclusion follows for an arbitrary $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Then from Corollary~\ref{Fpcommutecolimit} we deduce that the functor $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p$ commutes with colimits in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Hence, given a diagram $I\to\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$, the induced map of spectra \begin{equation} \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X) \end{equation} becomes an equivalence after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$. Since both sides are bounded below mod $p$ by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, it follows that \eqref{TCcolim} is an equivalence after smashing with $S^0/p$.

nodes.name: Colimit comparison map for TC
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X)
nodes.label: TCcolim

nodes.name: Connective associative ring spectra
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})$ be the $\infty$-category of connective
associative ring spectra.

nodes.name: TC/p of connective ring spectra commutes with sifted colimits
conclusions: commutes with sifted colimits
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with sifted colimits.
nodes.label: TCring

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.15
nodes.statement_short: THH commutes with sifted colimits; apply Theorem 2.7.
nodes.statement: This follows from Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes} since $\mathrm{TC}(R) = \mathrm{TC}( \mathrm{THH}(R))$, where we note that the topological Hochschild homology functor $\mathrm{THH}: \mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}) \to \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ commutes with sifted colimits (as geometric realizations and tensor products do).

nodes.name: TC/p finitary for F_p-algebras via de Rham--Witt
nodes.statement: For commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, Corollary~\ref{TCring} can be deduced using the description of Hesselholt \cite{Hesselholt} of $\mathrm{THH}$ of smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in terms of the de Rham--Witt complex; we detail this in subsection~\ref{dRWapproach} below.

nodes.name: p-limit axiom for square-zero extensions (McCarthy)
nodes.statement: In the case of square-zero extensions, the verification (called the \emph{$p$-limit axiom}) of Corollary~\ref{TCring} plays an important role in the proof that relative $K$-theory and $\mathrm{TC}$ with finite coefficients agree for nilimmersions of rings in McCarthy \cite{mccarthy}.

nodes.name: TC/p of spherical monoid rings
nodes.statement_short: For spherical monoid rings the Frobenius lift simplifies TC, giving another route to Corollary 2.15.
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an $\mathbb{E}_1$-monoid in the $\infty$-category of spaces, so that one can form the spherical monoid ring $\Sigma^\infty_+ M$. The formula for $\mathrm{TC}$ of spherical monoid rings \cite[Lemma IV.3.1]{nikolaus-scholze} (preceded by the formula for spherical group rings appearing already in \cite[Eq. (0.3)]{BHM}) shows that for any such $R$, the cyclotomic structure map $\mathrm{THH}(R) \to \mathrm{THH}(R)^{tC_p}$ factors $S^1$-equivariantly through $\mathrm{THH}(R)^{hC_p}$, which is called a \emph{Frobenius lift} in \cite{nikolaus-scholze}. For cyclotomic spectrum $X$ with a Frobenius lift, the construction of ($p$-complete) $\mathrm{TC}$ simplifies: one has a fiber square \cite[Prop. IV-3.4]{nikolaus-scholze} relating $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ to $\Sigma X_{hS^1}$ and two copies of $X$. It follows from this that the construction $M \mapsto \mathrm{TC}( \Sigma^\infty_+ M)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits in $M$. Since the free associative algebra is a spherical monoid ring, and since $\mathrm{TC}$ is already known to commute with geometric realizations, one can also deduce Corollary~\ref{TCring} in this way.

nodes.name: Functor category Fun(CycSp_{>=0}, Sp)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ denote the $\infty$-category of functors $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$.

nodes.name: Approximation of TC/p by homotopy-orbit functors
nodes.statement_short: In any range, TC/p agrees with a functor in the thick subcategory generated by X -> (X tensor HF_p^triv)_{hS^1}.
assumptions: For any given integer $n$
conclusions: there exists a functor $F \in \mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ with the following properties
nodes.statement: For any given integer $n$, there exists a functor $F \in \mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item $F$ belongs to the thick subcategory of $\mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ generated by the functor $X \mapsto (X\otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^\sub{triv})_{hS^1}$; \item There exists an equivalence $\tau_{\leq n} F(X) \simeq \tau_{\leq n}(\mathrm{TC}(X)/p)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: strong:finiteness

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.19
nodes.statement_short: Take F = TC(X tensor tau_{<=n+1}(S^0/p)^triv) and use Proposition 2.12, Lemma 2.11, Lemma 2.5.
nodes.statement: We claim that for each $n$, the functor $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X\otimes \tau_{\leq n+1}(S^0/p)^\sub{triv})$ has the desired properties. Indeed, it belongs to the thick subcategory generated by $X \mapsto (X\otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^\sub{triv})_{hS^1}$ thanks to Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq} and assertion~(\ref{hS1cofib}) of Lemma~\ref{cofiberofx}, while the connectivity assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{connectivity}.

nodes.name: Finite stages TC^r(X;p)
nodes.statement:
Given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq
0}$, the classical approach to topological cyclic homology (cf.~subsection \ref{subsection_reminders}) involves the spectra
\[ \mathrm{TC}^r(X;p) = \mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \xrightarrow{R-F} \mathrm{TR}^{r-1}(X;p)) \]
for all $r\ge1$.

nodes.name: Connectivity and cocontinuity of TC^r
nodes.statement_short: Each TC^r(X;p) is (-1)-connective and X -> TC^r(X;p) commutes with all colimits.
nodes.statement:
Note that $\mathrm{TC}^r(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for all $r\ge1$ (by the proof of Lemma \ref{connectivity}), and that each functor $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $X
\mapsto \mathrm{TC}^r(X;p)$ commutes with all colimits (by induction using (\ref{isotropysep})).

nodes.name: Pro-zero criterion for towers of Ab-valued functors
nodes.statement_short: A tower of coproduct-preserving functors to Ab with vanishing lim and lim^1 is pro-zero.
assumptions: For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r F_r(X) = 0$.
For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts.
conclusions: the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category admitting countable coproducts, and consider a tower of functors $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}$, say $\ldots \rightarrow F_r\rightarrow F_{r-1}\rightarrow \ldots \rightarrow F_1$. Suppose that: \begin{enumerate} \item For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r F_r(X) = 0$. \item For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts. \end{enumerate} Then the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero, i.e.\ it is zero as an object of $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab}))$; or, equivalently, for all $r\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $s>r$ such that the morphism $F_s\rightarrow F_r$ is $0$.
nodes.label: invlimmzero

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.20
nodes.statement_short: Objectwise Mittag-Leffler argument, then a coproduct of witnesses gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement: First we show the weaker claim that for all $X\in\mathcal{C}$, the tower $\{F_r(X)\}_r$ of abelian groups is pro-zero. Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity. From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower $\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes. If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero. Now, suppose the claim of the lemma does not hold, i.e., that $\{F_r\}_r$ is not pro-zero. Then for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $s>r$, we can find an $Y\in\mathcal{C}$ such that $F_s(Y)\rightarrow F_r(Y)$ is nonzero. Let $X$ denote the coproduct over all pairs $s>r$ of a choice of such a $Y$. Then for every $s>r$ the map $F_s(X)\rightarrow F_r(X)$ is nonzero, so we deduce that the tower $\{F_r(X)\}$ is not pro-zero, in contradiction to what was established above.

nodes.name: Pro-zero criterion for towers of spectrum-valued functors
assumptions: For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = 0$.
For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts.
The homotopy groups of each $F_r(X)$ are zero outside some fixed interval $[a,b]$, independent of $X$ and $r$.
conclusions: the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $\infty$-category admitting countable coproducts, and consider a tower of functors $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \operatorname{Sp}$, say $\ldots \rightarrow F_r\rightarrow F_{r-1}\ldots \rightarrow F_1$. Suppose that: \begin{enumerate} \item For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = 0$. \item For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts. \item The homotopy groups of each $F_r(X)$ are zero outside some fixed interval $[a,b]$, independent of $X$ and $r$. \end{enumerate} Then the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero, i.e.\ it is zero as an object of $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp}))$.
nodes.label: invlim02

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.21
nodes.statement_short: Pass to homotopy groups, apply Lemma 2.20, and devissage up the finite Postnikov tower.
nodes.statement: The Milnor sequence and induction up the Postnikov tower show that (1) implies $\varprojlim_r \pi_i F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r \pi_i F_r(X) = 0$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$. Since $\pi_i$ commutes with coproducts, we can apply the previous lemma to $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ and conclude that each tower $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero. Thus each Postnikov section of $\{F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero, and therefore so is $\{F_r\}_r$ itself, by devissage up the (finite) Postnikov tower.

nodes.name: Pro-constancy of the tower TC^r/p
nodes.statement_short: Truncated, the tower {TC^r(-)/p} is pro-constant with value TC(-)/p.
assumptions: Fix an integer $k$.
conclusions: is pro-constant with value $\tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $k$. Then the tower of objects of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0},\operatorname{Sp})$ given by $ \left\{ \tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p)\right\}_{r}$ is pro-constant with value $\tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$.
nodes.label: prop_pro_constant

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.22
nodes.statement_short: Show the truncated cofiber tower is pro-zero via Theorem 2.7 and Lemma 2.21.
nodes.statement: Setting $F_{r}(X) \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} \tau_{\leq k+1}\mathrm{cofib}( \mathrm{TC}(X)/p \to \mathrm{TC}^r(X)/p)$, we will show that the tower $\{F_{r}(-)\}_r$ is pro-zero. As $k$ varies, this shows that the map $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(-)/p\right\} \to \left\{\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p\right\}_r$ is a pro-isomorphism on each homotopy group in degrees $\leq k$ (in the pro-category of functors $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Ab}$), which is enough to conclude. Certainly $\varprojlim_r F_{r}(X) = 0$, and $F_r$ commutes with arbitrary coproducts by Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes}, so the desired claim follows from Lemma~\ref{invlim02}.

nodes.name: Differential forms and de Rham complex
nodes.statement: We let $\Omega^n_R$ denote the $n$-forms of $R$ (over $\mathbb{F}_p$) and let $\Omega_R^{\ast}$ denote the algebraic de Rham complex of $R$.

nodes.name: Inverse Cartier operator
nodes.statement_short: The multiplicative operator C^{-1}: Omega^n -> H^n(Omega^*) with C^{-1}(a)=a^p, C^{-1}(db)=b^{p-1}db.
nodes.statement: The \emph{inverse Cartier operator} $C^{-1}: \Omega^n_R \to H^n(\Omega^{\ast}_R) \subset \Omega^n_R/d \Omega^{n-1}_R$ is the multiplicative operator uniquely characterized by the formulas \( C^{-1}(a) = a^p, \quad C^{-1}(db) = b^{p-1} db, \) for $a, b \in R$. See \cite{Cartier1957}, also \cite[Prop.~3.3.4]{BLM}, for a construction of this map.
nodes.label: cartier

nodes.name: Cartier isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: For ind-smooth F_p-algebras, C^{-1} is a Frobenius-semilinear isomorphism from Omega^n onto de Rham cohomology H^n.
assumptions: if we further assume that $R$ is ind-smooth
nodes.statement:
It has image in the
cohomology of the de Rham complex; if we further assume that $R$ is ind-smooth,
i.e., can be written as a filtered colimit of smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras\footnote{Since smooth algebras are finitely presented, it follows that the category of ind-smooth algebras indeed identifies with $\operatorname{Ind}$ of the category of smooth algebras.}, then $C^{-1}$ provides a natural (Frobenius
semi-linear) isomorphism 
between $\Omega^n_R$ and $H^n( \Omega_R^{\ast})$ by the classical
\emph{Cartier isomorphism}, cf.~\cite[Th.~7.2]{Katz70}.

nodes.name: de Rham--Witt complex
nodes.statement_short: The Bloch--Deligne--Illusie de Rham--Witt complexes W_r Omega^*_R with R and F, and their limit W Omega^*_R.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra. For $r\ge 1$, we denote as usual by \[W_r(R)\xrightarrow{d}W_r\Omega^1_R\xrightarrow{d}W_r\Omega^2_R\xrightarrow{d}\cdots\] the classical de Rham--Witt complex (more precisely, differential graded algebras) of Bloch--Deligne--Illusie \cite{illusie-derham-witt}; this is the usual de Rham complex $\Omega^\bullet_R$ in the case $r=1$. We recall that the individual de Rham--Witt groups are equipped with Restriction and Frobenius maps $R,F:W_r\Omega^n_R\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_R$. We let $W \Omega_R^{\ast}$ denote the inverse limit of the tower $\left\{W_r \Omega^{\ast}_R\right\}$ under the Restriction maps.
nodes.label: dRW1

nodes.name: F lifts the inverse Cartier operator
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ W\Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[d] \ar[r]^F & W \Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[d] \\ \Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[r]^-{C^{-1}} & \Omega_R^{\ast}/d \Omega^{\ast-1}_R. }

nodes.name: Hesselholt's HKR theorem for TR
nodes.statement_short: For smooth F_p-algebras, TR^s_* is W_s Omega^* tensor a polynomial ring, so TR_* is W Omega^*.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.
conclusions: for each $s\ge1$, we have an isomorphism of graded rings
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. Then, for each $s\ge1$, we have an isomorphism of graded rings \begin{equation} \mathrm{TR}^s_*(R; p) \simeq W_s \Omega^{\ast}_R \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/p^s} \mathbb{Z}/p^s [ \sigma_s], \quad |\sigma_s| = 2. \end{equation} The Restriction maps are determined by the Restriction maps on the de Rham--Witt complex and send $\sigma_s \mapsto p \sigma_{s-1}$. Therefore, we have an isomorphism \begin{equation} \mathrm{TR}_*(R; p) \simeq W \Omega^{\ast}_R, \end{equation} and the $F$ map on $\mathrm{TR}(R; p)$ induces the $F$ map on $W \Omega_R^{\ast}$.

nodes.name: HKR isomorphism for TR^s
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TR}^s_*(R; p) \simeq W_s \Omega^{\ast}_R \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/p^s} \mathbb{Z}/p^s [ \sigma_s], \quad |\sigma_s| = 2.
nodes.label: HHKR1

nodes.name: HKR isomorphism for TR
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TR}_*(R; p) \simeq W \Omega^{\ast}_R,
nodes.label: HHKR2

nodes.name: TC/p commutes with filtered colimits of F_p-algebras
conclusions: commutes with filtered colimits
nodes.statement: The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/\mathbb F_p}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R\mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.26
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to ind-smooth algebras and use Hesselholt's HKR theorem; show F-1 on W Omega/p and C^{-1}-1 have isomorphic kernels and cokernels. The key step is that F-1 is bijective on the images of V and dV.
nodes.statement: Let $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ be a filtered colimit of $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. By functorially picking simplicial resolutions of all the terms by ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebras, and recalling that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations of rings, we reduce to the case in which all the $R_i$ (hence also $R$ itself) are ind-smooth over $\mathbb F_p$. Next we use Hesselholt's HKR theorem. Since each $\mathrm{TR}^s(-;p)$ commutes with filtered colimits (induction on (\ref{keyformulaclassical})), as does $W_s\Omega^n_{-}$, the formula \eqref{HHKR1} remains valid for ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. By taking the inverse limit over $s$, we deduce that $\pi_*(\mathrm{TR}(R;p)) \simeq W\Omega_R^*$ for any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$, i.e., \eqref{HHKR2} is valid in the ind-smooth case as well. Note here that each $W\Omega_R^n$ is $p$-torsion-free, by a basic property of the de Rham--Witt complex for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras \cite[Cor.~I.3.6]{illusie-derham-witt} which can easily be extended to the ind-smooth case as it derives from the stronger assertion that each Restriction map $W_s \Omega_R^{\ast} \to W_{s-1} \Omega_R^{\ast}$ annihilates every element $x \in W_s \Omega_R^{\ast}$ with $px = 0$. As a result, we also conclude that $\pi_* ( \mathrm{TR}(R; p)/p) \simeq W \Omega_R^{\ast}/p$. Taking fixed points for the Frobenius, we find that $\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)$ fits into an exact sequence \[W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\longrightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)\longrightarrow W\Omega^{n}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n}_R/p,\] and similarly for each $R_i$. To complete the proof it is enough to show, for each $n\ge0$, that the kernel and cokernel of $F-1:W\Omega^{n}_-/p\to W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ commutes with our filtered colimit $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$; we stress that $W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ does not commute with filtered colimits. For any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$, consider the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[r]^{F-1}\ar[d] & W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[d]\\ \Omega^n_R\ar[r]_{C^{-1}-1}&\Omega^n_R/d\Omega^{n-1}_R }. \end{equation} Here $C^{-1}$ is the inverse Cartier operator. To complete the proof we will show that the two horizontal arrows have isomorphic kernels (resp.\ cokernels), i.e., the square is both cartesian and cocartesian. To see this, it suffices to show that the map induced between the kernels of the vertical maps (which are surjective) is an isomorphism. The kernel of the map $W \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R$ is generated by the images of $V, dV$ by \cite[Proposition I.3.18]{illusie-derham-witt}. Note that the citation is for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, but the statement clearly passes to an ind-smooth algebra as the terms $W_s \Omega^n_{-}$ commute with filtered colimits and $W \Omega^n_{-} = \varprojlim W_s \Omega^n_{-}$. It follows that the kernel of the first vertical map in \eqref{thisdiag} is spanned by the images of $V, dV$ while the kernel of the second vertical map is spanned by the images of $V, d$. Thus, we need to show that the map \begin{equation} F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \end{equation} is an isomorphism. First, we show that $F-1$ is surjective. We record the following identities in $W \Omega_R^n/p$, \[(F-1)V=-V,\qquad (F-1)d\sum_{i>0}V^i=d;\] using it, we see immediately that $F - 1$ is surjective in \eqref{mapFminusone}. To see injectivity, we will use an important property of the de Rham--Witt complex: the image of $F$ on $W \Omega_R^n$ consists precisely of those elements $w$ with $dw$ divisible by $p$, thanks to \cite[(I.3.21.1.5)]{illusie-derham-witt}. Again, the reference is stated in the smooth case, but it also passes to the ind-smooth case;\footnote{Since the passage to the ind-smooth case is not completely immediate, we provide the argument. Firstly, the quasi-isomorphisms $W_s \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^{\bullet}$ for $s\ge1$ in the smooth case \cite[Corol.~I.3.15]{illusie-derham-witt} extend at once to the ind-smooth case, and taking the limit then shows $W \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^\bullet$ (to take the limit recall again that the $p$-torsion in $W_s\Omega^n_R$ is annihilated by $R:W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_R$). Secondly, the identity $\ker(d \colon \Omega^n_R\to\Omega^{n+1}_R)=\mathrm{Im}( F \colon W_2\Omega^n_R\to \Omega^n_R)$ also extends at once from the smooth \cite[Prop.~I.3.21]{illusie-derham-witt} to the ind-smooth case. Therefore, given $w\in W\Omega^n_R$ satisfying $dw\in pW\Omega^n_R$, we may write $w=Fx+y$ for some $x,y\in W\Omega^n_R$ such that $y$ vanishes in $\Omega^n_R$. But then $dy=dw-pFdx\in pW\Omega^n_R$, so $y$ defines a class in $H^n(W\Omega^\bullet/p)$ which vanishes in $H^n(\Omega^\bullet_R)$; by the first claim, we deduce that the initial class was zero, in other words that $y=dz+pz'$ for some $z\in W\Omega^{n-1}_R$, $z'\in W\Omega^n_R$. So $w= Fx+FdVz+FVz'$, as required.} for more on this point cf.~\cite[Sec.~2]{BLM}. Suppose $x \in W \Omega^n_R$ can be written as $x = Vy + dVz$ and $(F -1 )x $ is divisible by $p$; we show that $x $ is divisible by $p$ in $ W \Omega^n_R$. This will hold if $y, z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. First, $-dx \equiv d((F-1) x)$ modulo $p$, so $dx$ is divisible by $p$. It follows that $d Vy$, and hence $dy = FdVy$ is divisible by $p$, so that $y$ belongs to the image of $F$. In particular, modulo $p$, we have $x \equiv dV z$ and $(F-1) d Vz = d (z - Vz)$ is divisible by $p$. Therefore, $z - Vz$ belongs to the image of $F$. Since the operator $V$ is topologically nilpotent on $W \Omega^n_R$, we find that $(1 - V)$ is invertible and $z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. Therefore, $x$ is divisible by $p$ as desired.

nodes.name: Square comparing F-1 and C^{-1}-1
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[r]^{F-1}\ar[d] & W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[d]\\ \Omega^n_R\ar[r]_{C^{-1}-1}&\Omega^n_R/d\Omega^{n-1}_R }.
nodes.label: thisdiag

nodes.name: F-1 on images of V and dV
nodes.statement: F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right)
nodes.label: mapFminusone

nodes.name: Saturated Dieudonne complex
nodes.statement:
A \emph{saturated} Dieudonn\'e complex 
$(X^{\ast}, d, F)$ is a  $p$-torsion-free cochain complex
equipped with an operator $F: X^{\ast} \to X^{\ast}$ such that $dF = pFd$, the
opeartor $F: X^n \to X^n$ is injective, and the image of $F$ consists
precisely of those $x \in X^n$ such that $p $ divides $dx$; this implies that one
can define uniquely an operator $V$ such that $FV = VF = p$.

nodes.name: Strict Dieudonne complex
nodes.statement:
A saturated Dieudonn\'e complex $(X^{\ast}, d, F)$ is called \emph{strict} if 
$X^{\ast}$ is in addition complete for the filtration defined by
$\{\mathrm{im}(V^n, d V^n)\}$.

nodes.name: de Rham--Witt complexes are strict Dieudonne complexes
nodes.statement:
The de Rham--Witt complex of an ind-smooth
algebra is a strict Dieudonn\'e complex, and the functor $A \mapsto W
\Omega_A^{\ast}$ commutes with filtered colimits from ind-smooth
$\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras to the category of strict Dieudonn\'e complexes (where
colimits in the latter involve a completion process).

nodes.name: Kernel and cokernel of F-1 on strict Dieudonne complexes commute with filtered colimits
conclusions: commute with filtered colimits
nodes.statement: The functors from the category of strict Dieudonn\'e complexes to graded abelian groups given by $$(X^{\ast}, d, F)\mapsto \mathrm{ker}(F-1: X^{\ast}/p \to X^{\ast}/p), \quad \mathrm{coker}( F-1 : X^{\ast}/p \to X^{\ast}/p) $$ commute with filtered colimits.
nodes.label: strictDieudonne

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.27
nodes.statement_short: Analogous to the proof of Proposition 2.26.
nodes.statement:
Proposition~\ref{strictDieudonne} can be proved in an entirely analogous manner
as above.

nodes.name: Nonunital R-algebra
nodes.statement: Given a commutative base ring $R$, a \emph{nonunital $R$-algebra} is an $R$-module $I$ equipped with a multiplication map $I \otimes_R I \to I$ which is commutative and associative. We denote the category of nonunital $R$-algebras by $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. By contrast, when we say ``$R$-algebra,'' we assume the existence of a unit.

nodes.name: Unitalization R semidirect J
nodes.statement:
Conversely, given a nonunital $R$-algebra $J$, we can adjoin to it a unit and thus form the $R$-algebra $S = R
\ltimes J$, in which $J$ is embedded as an ideal.

nodes.name: Nonunital algebras are augmented algebras
nodes.statement: This latter construction establishes an equivalence between the category of nonunital $R$-algebras and the category of augmented $R$-algebras.

nodes.name: Free nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$ denote the ideal $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \subset R[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in the polynomial ring $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]$. Then $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$ is the free object of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ on $n$ generators.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence of nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: We say that a sequence $I' \to I \to \overline{I}$ in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ is a \emph{short exact sequence} if it is a short exact sequence of underlying abelian groups. That is, $I \to \overline{I}$ is surjective, and we can recover $I'$ as the pullback $0 \times_{\overline{I}} I$ in the category $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$.

nodes.name: Local nonunital algebra
nodes.statement_short: I is local if every x has a quasi-inverse y with x+y+xy=0, equivalently I lies in the Jacobson radical of any unitalization.
nodes.statement: A non-unital $R$-algebra $I$ is \emph{local} if the following equivalent conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For any $x \in I$, there exists $y \in I$ (necessarily unique) such that $x + y + xy = 0$. \item Whenever $I$ embeds as an ideal in an $R$-algebra $S$, then $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $S$. \item $I \subset R \ltimes I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $R \ltimes I$. \end{enumerate} The equivalence of the above conditions follows because, given an ideal $I \subset S$ in a commutative ring $S$, then $I$ belongs to the Jacobson radical of $S$ if and only if $1 + I$ consists of units of $S$. We let $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ denote the full subcategory of nonunital local $R$-algebras.

nodes.name: Localization of nonunital algebras is a left adjoint
conclusions: the inclusion $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ admits a left adjoint
nodes.statement: To describe all colimits, we need to localize further by observing that the inclusion $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ admits a left adjoint.

nodes.name: Localization I[(1+I)^{-1}]
nodes.statement_short: Base change of I along the group completion of the multiplicative monoid 1+I.

nodes.name: Free local nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+_{(x_1, \dots, x_n)}\in\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R$ be the image of $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+\in\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ under the left adjoint explained above. In other words, $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+_{(x_1, \dots, x_n)}$ is the ideal $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of the localization $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]_{1 + (x_1, \dots, x_n)}$ of the polynomial ring $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ at its multiplicative subset $1 + (x_1, \dots, x_n)$. It follows that $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+_{(x_1, \dots, x_n)}$ is a local nonunital $R$-algebra, and it is the free object on $n$ generators.

nodes.name: Local nonunital algebras form a localization
nodes.statement: Stated more formally, the preceding discussion shows that the inclusion $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ is the right adjoint of a \emph{localization} functor on the category $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. Specifically, $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R$ consists of those objects in $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ which are orthogonal \cite[Sec. 5.4]{Borceux1} to the map $R[x]^+ \to R[x]^+_{1 + (x)}$, in the sense that such that any map $R[x]^+ \to I$ extends uniquely over $R[x]^+_{1 + (x)}$. Moreover, one sees easily from the construction of the localization \eqref{loccons} that it is independent of the ground ring $R$. Analogous statements will be true when we restrict further to the subcategory of henselian nonunital rings; see the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma_nuh}.

nodes.name: Henselian nonunital algebra
nodes.statement_short: I is henselian if every equation x(1+x)^{n-1}+g(x)=0 with g in I[x] has a solution in I.
nodes.statement: A nonunital $R$-algebra $I$ is \emph{henselian} if for every $n \geq 1$ and every polynomial $g(x) \in I[x]$, the equation \begin{equation} x(1 + x)^{n-1} + g(x) = 0 \end{equation} has a solution in $I$. We let $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ denote the full subcategory of henselian nonunital $R$-algebras.
nodes.label: def_hens_nu

nodes.name: Henselian nonunital algebras are local with unique roots
nodes.statement: We note that if $I$ is a henselian nonunital $R$-algebra then: \begin{enumerate} \item Considering the equation $x + xy + y = 0$ for $y \in I$, we find that $I$ is local, i.e., $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R$. \item The root of the equation \eqref{henseq} is necessarily unique: denoting the equation by $f(x)=0$ for simplicity, if $\alpha, \alpha' \in I$ are both roots then we have $f'(\alpha) \in 1 + I$ and so the Taylor expansion shows that $$0 = f(\alpha) - f(\alpha') \in \alpha - \alpha' + I(\alpha - \alpha'),$$ whence $\alpha = \alpha'$ since $I$ is local. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Limits and sifted colimits of henselian nonunital rings
conclusions: the category of henselian nonunital rings has all limits and sifted colimits
nodes.statement: Since the solution of \eqref{henseq} is unique if it exists, the category of henselian nonunital rings has all limits and sifted colimits, both of which are computed at the level of underlying sets.

nodes.name: Quotients of henselian nonunital rings are henselian
assumptions:
if $I \twoheadrightarrow I'$ is a surjection in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$
and $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$
conclusions: $I' \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ too
nodes.statement:
Moreover, if $I \twoheadrightarrow I'$ is a surjection in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$
and $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$, then $I' \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ too.

nodes.name: Henselianity is independent of the base ring
nodes.statement:
Finally, the condition that a nonunital $R$-algebra be henselian does
not depend on the base ring $R$, i.e., we might as well take $R = \mathbb{Z}$ in
the definition.

nodes.name: Henselization of nonunital algebras
nodes.statement:
Now we prove the existence of a left adjoint $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R \to \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$, which will be
called \emph{henselization}.

nodes.name: Presentability and existence of henselization of nonunital algebras
conclusions: The category $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is presentable and the inclusion $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ admits a left adjoint.
nodes.statement: The category $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is presentable and the inclusion $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \subset \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ admits a left adjoint.
nodes.label: lemma_nuh

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.9
nodes.statement_short: Henselian nonunital algebras are an orthogonality class; presentability and the left adjoint follow formally.
nodes.statement: It follows from the above discussion that $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is the orthogonal \cite[Sec.~5.4]{Borceux1} of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ with respect to the maps \[ f_{n,t}: R[x_0, \dots, x_t]^+ \to R[x_0, \dots, x_t, y]^+/( y(1 + y)^{n-1} + x_0 + x_1 y + \dots + x_t y^t ),\] for $n, t \geq 1$. That is, a given object $X \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ belongs to $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ if and only \begin{equation} \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}( R[x_0, \dots, x_t, y]^+/( y(1 + y)^{n-1} + x_0 + x_1 y + \dots + x_t y^t ), X) \xrightarrow{\cdot\circ f_{n,t}} \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}(R[x_0, \dots, x_t]^+ , X) \end{equation} is an isomorphism for all $n,t\ge1$. It now follows formally that $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is presentable and the desired left adjoint exists \cite[Cor. 5.4.8]{Borceux1}. Alternatively, one can appeal to the theory of henselian pairs and define the left adjoint directly by taking the henselization of the pair $(R \ltimes I, I)$; see the forthcoming Construction \ref{construction_henselization}.

nodes.name: Orthogonality condition for henselian nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}( R[x_0, \dots, x_t, y]^+/( y(1 + y)^{n-1} + x_0 + x_1 y + \dots + x_t y^t ), X) \xrightarrow{\cdot\circ f_{n,t}} \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}(R[x_0, \dots, x_t]^+ , X)
nodes.label: hommap

nodes.name: Free henselian nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+\in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ denote the henselization of $R[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+ \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. By construction, $R\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is the free object on $n$ generators.
nodes.label: freeobjs

nodes.name: Nonunital rings as models of Lawvere theories
nodes.statement: The categories $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$, $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,loc}}_R$ and $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ are all examples of models for a {\em Lawvere} or {\em algebraic theory} \cite[Ch.~3]{ARloc} \cite[Ch.~3]{Borceux}. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category satisfying the following conditions: \begin{itemize} \item[(Law)] $\mathcal C$ has all limits and colimits, and is equipped with a functor $U \colon \mathcal C\to \mathrm{Sets}$ which is conservative, preserves sifted colimits, and admits a left adjoint $F \colon \mathrm{Sets}\to\mathcal C$. \end{itemize} For example, $\mathcal C$ might be the category of rings, nonunital rings, groups, etc. In this case, one takes for $U$ the forgetful functor taking the underlying set, and its right adjoint $F$ is the free ring, nonunital ring, group, etc.~on the given set. Denoting by $\{1\}$ a one-point set, the element $F(\{1\})$ is therefore both compact projective (i.e., $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(\{1\}), \cdot)$ commutes with sifted colimits) and a strong generator (i.e., $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(\{1\}), \cdot)$ is faithful and conservative). The {\em free object of $\mathcal C$ on $n$ generators} is by definition $\bigsqcup_nF(\{1\})\simeq F(\{1,\dots,n\})$. By the monadicity theorem, $\mathcal{C}$ is monadic over $\mathrm{Sets}$, via a monad that preserves sifted colimits. Let $\mathcal C'\subset \mathcal C$ be a full subcategory, and assume that $\mathcal C'$ is closed under limits and sifted colimits (in $\mathcal C$) and that the inclusion $\mathcal C'\subset\mathcal C$ is a right adjoint. Then clearly $\mathcal C'$ also satisfies conditions (Law), with $U'$ given by the restriction of $U$ to $\mathcal C'$. Moreover, the free objects of $\mathcal C'$ are given by applying the left adjoint $\mathcal C\to \mathcal C'$ to the free objects of $\mathcal C$. In practice, this is how the ``free objects'' in the above categories are constructed. According to general results of Lawvere theory \cite[Thm.~3.9.1]{Borceux} (in fact, we do not use the results in this paragraph, but the point of view may be helpful), the full subcategory $\mathcal{C}_{\Sigma} \subset \mathcal{C}$ of compact projective objects of $\mathcal{C}$ is the idempotent completion of the full subcategory consisting of the free objects $\left\{\bigsqcup_{n} F(\{1\}) : n \geq 0\right\}$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{C}$ can be identified with the category of presheaves on $\mathcal{C}_\Sigma$ which commute with finite products. In particular, objects of $\mathcal{C}$ can be identified with sets equipped with various ``operations'' arising from maps between the free objects satisfying various relations.
nodes.label: remark_Lawvere

nodes.name: Henselian pair
nodes.statement_short: A pair (S,I) is henselian if simple roots mod I lift, equivalently I in the Jacobson radical with monic lifting, equivalently lifting against etale maps.
nodes.statement: A \emph{pair} is the data $(S, I)$ where $S$ is a commutative ring and $I \subset S$ is an ideal. The collection of pairs forms a category in the obvious manner. The pair $(S, I)$ is said to be \emph{henselian} if the following equivalent (cf.~\cite[Tag 09XD]{stacks-project} for the equivalence) conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item Given a polynomial $f(x) \in S[x]$ and a root $\overline{\alpha} \in S/I$ of $\overline{f} \in (S/I)[x]$ with $\overline{f}'(\alpha)$ being a unit of $S/I$, then $\overline \alpha$ lifts to a root $\alpha \in S$ of $f$. Note that the lifted root $\alpha \in S$ is necessarily unique by the same argument as we gave after Definition \ref{def_hens_nu}. \item The ideal $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $S$, and the same condition as (1) holds for \emph{monic} polynomials $f(x) \in S[x]$. \item Given any commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ A \ar[d] \ar[r] & S \ar[d] \\ B \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & S/I\ }\end{equation} with $A \to B$ \'etale, there exists a lift as in the dotted arrow. \end{enumerate} We may also say that the surjective map $S \to S/I$ is a henselian pair, if there is no risk of confusion. If $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\frak m$, then $S$ is said to be a \emph{henselian local ring} if $(S, \frak m)$ is a henselian pair.
nodes.label: def:henspair

nodes.name: Lifting diagram for henselian pairs
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ A \ar[d] \ar[r] & S \ar[d] \\ B \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & S/I\ }
nodes.label: lifthens

nodes.name: Uniqueness in the lifting property
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a henselian pair and consider a diagram as in \eqref{lifthens} with $A \to B$ \'etale. Then the lifting is unique. Indeed, given two liftings $f_1, f_2: B \to S$ in \eqref{lifthens}, we have a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ B \otimes_A B \ar[d]^m \ar[r]^{f_1 \otimes f_2} & S \ar[d] \\ B \ar[r] & S/I, }\] for $m \colon B \otimes_A B \to B$ the multiplication map. Since $m$ is also \'etale (in fact, the projection on a direct factor), the lifting property again shows that $f_1 \otimes f_2$ factors through $m$, so $f_1 = f_2$.
nodes.label: uniquenessinliftingproperty

nodes.name: Subideals of henselian ideals are henselian
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair and let $J \subset I$ be a subideal. Then $(R, J)$ remains a henselian pair.
nodes.label: subideal:henspair

nodes.name: Elkik's lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Henselian pairs have the right lifting property against smooth maps.
assumptions: Let $(S, I)$ be a henselian pair.
conclusions: $S \to S/I$ has the right lifting property with respect to smooth maps
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a henselian pair. Then $S \to S/I$ has the right lifting property with respect to smooth maps. That is, any diagram as in \eqref{lifthens} with $A \to B$ smooth (rather than \'etale) admits a lift as in the dotted arrow.
nodes.label: elkikthm

nodes.name: Gabber's criterion: henselian pairs depend only on the ideal
nodes.statement_short: A pair (S,I) is henselian iff I is henselian as a nonunital ring.
assumptions: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair.
conclusions: $(S, I)$ is a henselian pair if and only if $I$ is henselian as a nonunital ring
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair. Then $(S, I)$ is a henselian pair if and only if $I$ is henselian as a nonunital ring.
nodes.label: checkhensnonunital

nodes.name: Henselianity of (S,I) versus (Z semidirect I, I)
assumptions: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair.
conclusions: $(S, I)$ is a henselian pair if and only if $(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I, I)$ is a henselian pair
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair. Then $(S, I)$ is a henselian pair if and only if $(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I, I)$ is a henselian pair.

nodes.name: Henselization of a pair
nodes.statement_short: The initial henselian pair under (S,I): an ind-etale S-algebra with I^h = I S^h and the same quotient.
nodes.statement: Given a pair $(S, I)$, there is a pair $(S^h, I^h)$ and a map $(S, I) \to (S^h, I^h)$, called the \emph{henselization} of the original pair, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item $(S^h, I^h)$ is a henselian pair and is the initial henselian pair receiving a map from $(S, I)$. That is, the construction $(S, I) \mapsto (S^h, I^h)$ is the left adjoint to the forgetful functor from henselian pairs to pairs. \item $S^h$ is a filtered colimit of \'etale $S$-algebras and $I^h = I S^h = I \otimes_S S^h$. \item The map $S/I \to S^h/I^h$ is an isomorphism. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: construction_henselization

nodes.name: Recognizing the henselization
nodes.statement_short: An ind-etale factorization S -> S~ -> S/I with S~ -> S/I henselian is the henselization.
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair. Suppose given a factorization $S \to \widetilde{S} \to S/I$ such that $\widetilde{S}$ is a filtered colimit of \'etale $S$-algebras and such that $\widetilde{S} \to S/I$ has the right lifting property with respect to \'etale morphisms (i.e., the surjection $\widetilde{S} \to S/I$ is a henselian pair). Then $(\widetilde{S}, I \widetilde{S})$ is the henselization of $(S, I)$. To see this, consider a henselian pair $(A, J)$ and a map $(S, I) \to (A, J)$. Considering the commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ S \ar[d] \ar[r] & \widetilde{S} \ar@{-->}[ld] \ar[r] & S/I \ar[d] \\ A \ar[rr] & & A/J },\] the ind-\'etaleness of $S \to \widetilde{S}$ implies the existence of a \emph{unique} dotted arrow $\widetilde{S} \to A$ making the diagram commute (cf.~Remark~\ref{uniquenessinliftingproperty}). This verifies the universal property of the henselization. In particular, one can construct $(S^h, I^h)$ by appealing to Quillen's small object argument \cite[Th. 2.1.14]{Hovey} to factor $S \to S/I$ as the composite of a filtered colimit of \'etale morphisms and a morphism that has the right lifting property with respect to \'etale morphisms; the universal property of the henselization then constructs it as a functor. Note that in \eqref{lifthens}, it suffices to take $A, B$ finitely generated over $\mathbb{Z}$, by the structure theory for \'etale morphisms.
nodes.label: hensfact

nodes.name: Milnor square
differentia: the diagram is both cartesian and cocartesian in the category of commutative rings
nodes.statement: A \emph{Milnor square} of commutative rings is a diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ S \ar[d] \ar[r]& T \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r] & T' } \end{equation} such that the vertical arrows are surjective and such that the diagram is both cartesian and cocartesian in the category of commutative rings. It follows in particular that if $I \subset S$, $J \subset T$ are the respective kernels of the vertical maps $S \to S'$, $T \to T'$, then $f|_I : I \stackrel{\simeq}{\to} J$ establishes an isomorphism of the ideals $I$, $J$.
nodes.label: milnorsquare

nodes.name: Milnor square diagram
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ S \ar[d] \ar[r]& T \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r] & T' }
nodes.label: milnsquare

nodes.name: Henselization preserves Milnor squares
assumptions: Consider a Milnor square as in \eqref{milnsquare} with respect to the ideals $I \subset S$, $J \subset T$.
conclusions: the henselizations $S^h$, $T^h$ of $S$, $T$ along $I$, $J$ fit into a Milnor square
$T^h \simeq S^h \otimes_S T$
nodes.statement: Consider a Milnor square as in \eqref{milnsquare} with respect to the ideals $I \subset S$, $J \subset T$. Then the henselizations $S^h$, $T^h$ of $S$, $T$ along $I$, $J$ fit into a Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ S^h \ar[d] \ar[r] & T^h \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r] & T' }.\] Furthermore, $T^h \simeq S^h \otimes_S T$.
nodes.label: milnsquarehens

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.21
nodes.statement_short: Base change the Milnor square along the flat map S -> S^h and recognize the henselization via Remark 3.19.
nodes.statement: Since $S^h$ is flat over $S$, we can base-change \eqref{milnsquare} along $S \to S^h$ to obtain a new Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ S^h \ar[d] \ar[r] & T \otimes_S S^h \ar[d] \\ S' \otimes_S S^h \ar[r] & T' \otimes_S S^h }. \] Note that $S' \otimes_S S^h \simeq S'$ by the properties of the henselization, and similarly for $T$. Therefore the bottom arrow can be rewritten as $S' \to T'$. Since this is a Milnor square and the left vertical arrow is a henselian pair, so is the right vertical arrow thanks to Proposition~\ref{checkhensnonunital}. We have a factorization $T \to T \otimes_S S^h \to T'$ as the composite of an ind-\'etale map and a map having the right lifting property with respect to \'etale maps. Thus, the result follows in view of Remark~\ref{hensfact}.

nodes.name: Henselization of nonunital rings is independent of the base
assumptions: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair and let $(S^h, I^h)$ be its henselization.
Let $R$ be any ring mapping to $S$.
conclusions: $I^h$ is the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair and let $(S^h, I^h)$ be its henselization. Let $R$ be any ring mapping to $S$. Then $I^h$ is the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. In particular, the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ does not depend on the base ring $R$.
nodes.label: corollary_hens_ind_of_base

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.22
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.21 to the Milnor square relating R semidirect I and S.
nodes.statement: To distinguish the possible henselizations which a priori might not coincide, we temporarily write $I^{nuh}$ to denote the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. The equivalence between $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ and augmented $R$-algebras easily implies that $(R\ltimes I^{nuh},I^{nuh})$ is the henselization of the pair $(R \ltimes I, I)$. Applying Proposition~\ref{milnsquarehens} to the Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ R\ltimes I \ar[d] \ar[r] & S \ar[d] \\ R \ar[r] & S/I }\] then reveals that the square \[ \xymatrix{ R\ltimes I^{nuh} \ar[d] \ar[r] & S^h \ar[d] \\ R \ar[r] & S^h/I^h }\] is also Milnor, i.e., that $I^{nuh}\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} I^h$, as desired.

nodes.name: Multiplication-by-N endomorphism [N]
nodes.statement:
For each $N>0$, denote by \[[N]: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_n\right\}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_n\right\}^+\] the endomorphism in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_{\mathbb Z}$ which sends $x_i \mapsto Nx_i$.

nodes.name: Free henselian nonunital Q-algebras as colimits
nodes.statement_short: Q{x_1..x_n}^+ is the filtered colimit of the multiplication-by-N maps on Z{x_1..x_n}^+.
assumptions: Let $n > 0$.
conclusions: is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$
nodes.statement: Let $n > 0$. The filtered colimit of the endomorphisms $[N]$ on $\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$, indexed over natural numbers $N$ ordered by divisibility, is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$.
nodes.label: rationalhens

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.23
nodes.statement_short: Henselization commutes with filtered colimits and is independent of the base.
nodes.statement: Henselization commutes with filtered colimits, and the filtered colimit of the analogous maps $[N]: \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$ is given by $\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$. We now use Corollary \ref{corollary_hens_ind_of_base} that henselization does not depend on the base ring.
nodes.label: sec:kanext

nodes.name: Finitely generated functor
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category and $F: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ a functor. We say that $F$ is \emph{finitely generated} if there exist finitely many objects $X_1, \dots, X_n \in \mathcal{C}$ and a surjection of functors \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(X_i, \cdot)] \twoheadrightarrow F. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Surjection from corepresentables
nodes.statement: \bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(X_i, \cdot)] \twoheadrightarrow F.
nodes.label: fingenfun

nodes.name: Perfect and pseudocoherent functors
nodes.statement_short: F is perfect if in the thick subcategory generated by corepresentables, pseudocoherent if approximable by perfect functors in every truncation.
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category and $F: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Sp}$ a functor. \begin{enumerate} \item We say that $F$ is \emph{perfect} if $F$ belongs to the thick subcategory of $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathrm{Sp})$ generated by the functors $\Sigma^\infty_+ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(C, \cdot)$ for $C \in \mathcal{C}$ (or equivalently is a compact object of $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp})$, by a thick subcategory argument). \item We say that $F$ is \emph{pseudocoherent} if, for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ such that $\tau_{\le n}F'(C)\to\tau_{\le n}F(C)$ is an equivalence for all $C\in \mathcal C$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Characterizations of pseudocoherence
nodes.statement_short: For bounded-below F: pseudocoherent iff truncations are compact iff F has a cell filtration by shifted corepresentables.
assumptions: Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$.
conclusions: The following conditions on a functor $F \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq d}) \subset \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp})$ are equivalent
nodes.statement: Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$.
