nodes.statement: We say that a tower $\left\{X_i\right\}$ of spectra is \emph{almost nilpotent} if for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the truncated tower $\left\{\tau_{\leq n} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, or equivalently if each tower $\left\{\pi_n (X_i)\right\}$ of abelian groups is nilpotent. We say that a tower is \emph{almost quickly converging} if for each $n$, the tower $\left\{\tau_{\leq n} X_i\right\}$ is quickly converging. If the tower is uniformly bounded below, then it is almost quickly converging if and only if each tower $\left\{\pi_n (X_i)\right\}$ of abelian groups is quickly convergent.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.15
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of Mathew's Lemma 3.11.
nodes.statement: The following then is a direct consequence of \cite[Lemma 3.11]{Mthick}.

nodes.name: Thickness of almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers
conclusions: form thick subcategories
nodes.statement: The almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers form thick subcategories of $\mathrm{Tow}( \mathrm{Sp})$ including the nilpotent and quickly converging towers respectively.

nodes.name: Geometric realization of almost quickly converging towers
assumptions: Suppose each tower $\dots \to X_{j,2} \to X_{j, 1}$ is almost quickly convergent, with limit $X_j$.
conclusions: is almost quickly converging and has limit $\vert X_\bullet \vert$ via the natural comparison map
nodes.statement: Let $X_{\bullet, \ast}$ be a simplicial object in the $\infty$-category of towers of connective spectra. Suppose each tower $\dots \to X_{j,2} \to X_{j, 1}$ is almost quickly convergent, with limit $X_j$. Then the geometric realization $\dots \to |X_{\bullet, 2}| \to |X_{\bullet, 1}|$ is almost quickly converging and has limit $\vert X_\bullet \vert$ via the natural comparison map.
nodes.label: simplicialalmostquickconv

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.16
nodes.statement_short: Approximate by finite skeletal realizations.
nodes.statement: This follows from approximating the geometric realization with an $n$-skeletal geometric realization in any range of degrees.

nodes.name: TC/p preserves almost quick convergence
assumptions: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}$ be a tower in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$.
Suppose that the underlying tower of spectra $\left\{X_i/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging.
conclusions: the tower of spectra $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(X_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}$ be a tower in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$. Suppose that the underlying tower of spectra $\left\{X_i/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging. Then the tower of spectra $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(X_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging.
nodes.label: TCalmostquickconv

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.17
nodes.statement_short: As for Proposition 2.19.
nodes.statement: This follows in a similar fashion as Proposition~\ref{strong:finiteness}. See also Remark \ref{TCinvlim} for the identification of the inverse limit of the above tower in $\mathrm{CycSp}$.

nodes.name: Smash products of almost quickly converging towers
assumptions: If $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ are almost quickly converging with inverse limits $X$ and $Y$
conclusions: $\left\{X_i\otimes Y_i\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with inverse limit $X\otimes Y$
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ be two towers of connective spectra. If $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ are almost quickly converging with inverse limits $X$ and $Y$, then $\left\{X_i\otimes Y_i\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with inverse limit $X\otimes Y$.
nodes.label: transfernilp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.18
nodes.statement_short: Truncation reduces to nilpotent or constant factors; thick subcategory argument.
nodes.statement: Note that $\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i) \simeq \tau_{\leq m} ( \tau_{\leq m} X_i \otimes Y_i)$. So if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, then so is $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i)\right\}$, and the limit is zero. Symmetrically, we get the same if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}Y_i\right\}$ is nilpotent. On the other hand, if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} Y_i\right\}$ are both constant, we see that $\tau_{\leq m} (X_i\otimes Y_i)$ is constant, and the map from $X\otimes Y$ to the limit is an isomorphism degrees $\leq m-1$. A thick subcategory argument lets us conclude.

nodes.name: Continuity of TC for almost quickly converging towers of ring spectra
assumptions: If this comparison map is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower of spectra $\{R_i/p\}$ is almost quickly converging
conclusions: is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower $\{\mathrm{TC}(R_i)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\{R_i\}_{i\ge1}$ is a tower of connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra, and $R$ is another connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectrum with a comparison map $R\rightarrow \varprojlim_i R_i$. If this comparison map is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower of spectra $\{R_i/p\}$ is almost quickly converging, then the comparison map $$\mathrm{TC}(R)\rightarrow\varprojlim_i \mathrm{TC}(R_i)$$ is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower $\{\mathrm{TC}(R_i)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging.
nodes.label: THHmodp

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.19
nodes.statement_short: Tensor powers, then the cyclic bar construction, then TC preserve almost quick convergence.
nodes.statement: Note that a tower is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ if and only if it is almost quickly converging after smashing with $X$, for any choice of spectrum $X$ generating the same thick subcategory as $S^0/p$. For example one can take $X=S^0/p\otimes S^0/p$.\footnote{This is the cone of multiplcation by $p$ on $S^0/p$, hence lies in the thick subcategory generated by $S^0/p$. For the converse, note that $p^2$ kills $S^0/p$, so $S^0/p$ is a retract of $(S^0/p \otimes S^0/p)/p$.} Keeping this in mind, an inductive application of Lemma \ref{transfernilp} shows that $\left\{(HR_i)^{\otimes n}\right\}_i$ is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ for any $n\geq 0$, and has mod~$p$ limit $(HR)^{\otimes n}/p$. Then by Lemma \ref{simplicialalmostquickconv} we deduce that $\left\{\mathrm{THH}(R_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with limit $\mathrm{THH}(R)/p$. From this, Lemma \ref{TCalmostquickconv} lets us conclude.

nodes.name: HZ-module spectra
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category of $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra, or equivalently the derived $\infty$-category of $\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Derived p-adic continuity of TC
assumptions: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$.
conclusions: is a $p$-adic equivalence
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$. Then the map \[ \mathrm{TC}(R) \to \varprojlim_i \mathrm{TC}( R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i) \] is a $p$-adic equivalence. Moreover the tower on the right-hand-side is almost quickly converging modulo $p$.
nodes.label: TCderpcontinuous

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.20
nodes.statement_short: The fiber tower has transition maps multiplication by p; apply Theorem 5.19.
nodes.statement: It suffices to remark that the transition maps in the tower of fibers $\{\operatorname{fib}(R\rightarrow R\otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z})\}_n$ identify with multiplication by $p$ maps, hence are zero modulo $p$, so that Proposition \ref{THHmodp} applies.

nodes.name: Derived p-adic continuity of K-theory
assumptions: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $\pi_0(R)$ is commutative and henselian along $(p)$.
conclusions: is an equivalence modulo $p$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $\pi_0(R)$ is commutative and henselian along $(p)$. Then the tower $\{K(R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}) / p\}_{i \geq 1}$ is almost quickly converging, and $$K(R)\rightarrow \varprojlim_i K(R\otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}}H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z})$$ is an equivalence modulo $p$.
nodes.label: derivedpadiccont

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.21
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem reduces to Theorem 5.20.
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} we see $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) = K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i \mathbb{Z})$ for each $i$. This reduces us to the analogous result for $\mathrm{TC}$, which is Theorem~\ref{TCderpcontinuous}.

nodes.name: p-adic continuity of K-theory with bounded p-power torsion
assumptions: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$, and suppose the $p$-power-torsion in $R$ is bounded.
conclusions: $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$
the tower $\{K(R/p^iR)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$, and suppose the $p$-power-torsion in $R$ is bounded. Then $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$. Moreover, the tower $\{K(R/p^iR)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.22
nodes.statement_short: The fiber tower is almost nilpotent mod p under bounded torsion; argue as in Theorems 5.20, 5.21.
nodes.statement: The map of towers $\{HR\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}\}\rightarrow \{H(R/p^iR)\}$ has fiber $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ with transition maps multiplication by $p$. Because of the bounded $p$-power torsion hypothesis, this tower $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ is almost nilpotent modulo $p$. So we deduce $p$-adic continuity for $\mathrm{TC}$ as in Proposition \ref{TCderpcontinuous}, and then $p$-adic continuity for $K$-theory as in Proposition \ref{derivedpadiccont}.

nodes.name: Variant without Z-linear structure
nodes.statement: Without assuming $\mathbb{Z}$-linear structure, one can get similar results by replacing $-\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}$ with $-\otimes S_i$ for any reasonable tower of $E_\infty$-algebras $\left\{S_i\right\}$ of which $p$-adically approximates the sphere spectrum, for example the tower coming from the usual cosimplicial Adams resolution associated to $S^0\rightarrow H\mathbb{F}_p$.

nodes.name: Logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement_short: W_r Omega^n_{R,log} is the image of the dlog map on units, for R local.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra. We recall the de Rham-Witt complex $\{W_r \Omega_R^{\ast}\}$ as in \cite{illusie-derham-witt} (see also Definition~\ref{dRW1}). Letting $[\cdot]:R\to W_r(R)$ denote the Teichm\"uller lift, there is a resulting group homomorphism $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:R^\times\to W_r\Omega^1_R$, $\alpha\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha]=\tfrac{d[\alpha]}{[\alpha]}$, and more generally \[\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:R^{\times\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{R}^n,\quad \alpha_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\alpha_n\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_n].\] When $R$ is local, the image of this map will be denoted by $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$.
nodes.label: definition_dRW

nodes.name: Globalization of (logarithmic) de Rham--Witt sheaves
nodes.statement: Given an $\mathbb F_p$-scheme $X$, one defines $W_r\Omega^n_X$ to be the Zariski (or \'etale, depending on the context) sheaf obtained by sheafifying $U\mapsto W_r\Omega^n_{\mathcal O_X(U)}$. When $X=\mathrm{Spec} R$ is affine, this sheaf (in either topology) has no higher cohomology and has global sections $W_r\Omega_R^n$: this follows from flat descent and the facts that if $R\to S$ is \'etale then so is $W_r(R)\to W_r(S)$ \cite[Thm.~2.4]{vanderKallen1986} and moreover the canonical map $W_r\Omega_R^n\otimes_{W_r(R)}W_r(S)\to W_r\Omega_S^n$ is an isomorphism \cite[Prop.~1.7]{LangerZink2004}. We define $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ to be the subgroup of $W_r\Omega^n_R$ consisting of elements which can be written Zariski locally as sums of dlog forms, i.e., $H^0(\mathrm{Spec} R,-)$ of the image (as a Zariski sheaf) of \[\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,\mathrm{Spec} R}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{\mathrm{Spec} R}^n,\quad \alpha_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\alpha_n\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_n].\] We note that $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ would be unchanged if we were to replace Zariski by \'etale in the previous sentence, by \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}; in particular, $W_1\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ really is the same as $\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ as defined at the start of the subsection. Similarly, if $X$ is a scheme, we let $W_r \Omega_{X, \sub{log}}^n$ denote the sheaf $\mathrm{Spec} R \mapsto W_r \Omega^n_{R, \sub{log}}$.

nodes.name: Geisser--Levine theorem with mod p^r coefficients
nodes.statement_short: For ind-smooth local F_p-algebras, K_n mod p^r is W_r Omega^n_log via dlog, and K_n is p-torsion-free.
assumptions: In the case that $R$ is an ind-smooth local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra
nodes.statement:
In the case that $R$ is an ind-smooth local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, Geisser--Levine
\cite{GL} established isomorphisms $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\cong W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ (given by the map $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols) for all $n\ge0$, $r\ge1$, and proved that each group $K_n(R)$ is $p$-torsion-free.

nodes.name: Pro Geisser--Levine theorem
nodes.statement_short: For F-finite regular local F_p-algebras, pro K-groups of R/I^s mod p^r are pro logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups, and p-torsion-free.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, local noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal; fix $n,r\ge 0$.
conclusions: the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s $ is $p$-torsion-free
there is a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, local noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal; fix $n,r\ge 0$. Then the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s $ is $p$-torsion-free and there is a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups \[\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}\}_s\] given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols.
nodes.label: theorem_pro_GL

nodes.name: Relative K-theory mod p of ind-smooth henselian pairs
assumptions: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras.
Suppose that $R$ and $R/I$ are ind-smooth.
conclusions: we have a natural isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. Suppose that $R$ and $R/I$ are ind-smooth. Then we have a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} K_n(R, I; \mathbb{Z}/p) \simeq \Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}},.\end{equation} where $\Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}}:=\operatorname{ker}(\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}\rightarrow \Omega^n_{R/I,\sub{log}})$.

nodes.name: Relative K mod p as relative log forms
nodes.statement: K_n(R, I; \mathbb{Z}/p) \simeq \Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}},.
nodes.label: relhensmodp

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.27
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem plus the Geisser--Hesselholt sequence and Proposition 4.31.
nodes.statement: Indeed, this follows from our main result (which identifies the relative $K$-theory with relative $\mathrm{TC}$), together with the Geisser--Hesselholt calculations of relative $\mathrm{TC}$. We have the short exact sequence \[ 0 \to \widetilde{\nu}^{n+1}(R) \to \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p) \to \nu^n(R) \to 0 \] as in Theorem~\ref{GHGL} (see also \eqref{thisdiag}). Using Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}, the result follows.

nodes.name: Relative logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: Given an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$ and ideal $I\subseteq R$, we set $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{R/I,\sub{log}})$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of R - F on relative de Rham--Witt groups
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$.
conclusions: $R-F:W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)}$ is surjective
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$. Then $R-F:W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)}$ is surjective.
nodes.label: lemma_drw1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.29
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the complete F-finite case of Morrow via Neron--Popescu and split injections.
nodes.statement: If $R$ is $F$-finite, noetherian, and $I$-adically complete then this was proved in \cite[Prop.~2.20]{Morrow-HW}, and we will reduce the general case to this one. Firstly, by taking a filtered colimit we may suppose that $R$ is the henselization of a finite type $\mathbb F_p$-algebra along some ideal, and in particular that $R$ is $F$-finite and excellent \cite[Tag 07QS]{stacks-project}. Then the $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is geometrically regular over $R$ by \cite[7.8.3(v)]{EGA_IV_2}, whence it is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras $A$ by N\'eron--Popescu. But each structure map $R\to A$ admits a splitting as in Remark~\ref{henspairequivtocontinuity}. Therefore, taking a filtered colimit shows that \[\operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)})\] is injective. Since the right side vanishes by the first sentence of the paragraph, the proof is complete.

nodes.name: Illusie's exact sequence for logarithmic de Rham--Witt sheaves
nodes.statement_short: On smooth varieties, W_s Omega_log / p^r = W_r Omega_log, giving a short exact sequence of pro etale sheaves.
assumptions:
if $X$ is a smooth variety over a
perfect field of characteristic $p$
nodes.statement:
A important result of Illusie states that if $X$ is a smooth variety over a
perfect field of characteristic $p$, then the canonical map of \'etale sheaves
$W_{s}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}/p^r\to W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ is an isomorphism
whenever $s\ge r$ and $n\ge0$, and therefore \[0\longrightarrow
\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}
\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{s-r}\}_s}W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\longrightarrow
0\] is an exact sequence of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$ \cite[\S
I.5.7]{illusie-derham-witt}.

nodes.name: Pro exact sequence for relative logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n\ge0$.
conclusions: is exact for any $r\ge1$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n\ge0$. Then the sequence of pro abelian groups \[0\longrightarrow\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{s-r}\}_s}\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow 0\] is exact for any $r\ge1$.
nodes.label: lemma_drw2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.30
nodes.statement_short: Etale-sheaf argument: relative log de Rham--Witt sheaves have no H^1, and Illusie's sequence passes to relative terms.
nodes.statement: We will need to argue via the \'etale topology, so we begin by introducing the necessary sheaves. Let $X:=\mathrm{Spec} R$, with closed subschemes $Y_s:=\mathrm{Spec} R/I^s$ for $s\ge1$; let $W_r\Omega^n_X$, $W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s)}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_X\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s})$ be the corresponding \'etale sheaves on $X$. As explained in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, these sheaves have no higher \'etale cohomology (since $X$ is affine) and their global sections are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_R$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$. Next let $W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ be the image in the \'etale topology of $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,X}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{X}^n$, and similarly for each $Y_s$, and set $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}})$. As we already mentioned in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, the subgroup of dlog forms may be defined using either the Zariski or \'etale topology by \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}, and therefore the global sections of these sheaves are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}$. We claim that $\{H^1_\sub{\'et}(X,W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}})\}_r=0$ for each $s\ge 1$. After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$. Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms \begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0\end{equation} Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}. Finally, appealing to Illusie's result recalled immediately before the lemma (which has been extended to arbitrary regular $\mathbb F_p$-schemes by A.~Shiho \cite[Cor.~2.13]{Shiho2007}) and to an analogous pro version for the formal completion of $X$ along along $Y_1$ \cite[Cor.~4.8]{Morrow-HW} gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are again surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}\ar[d]&\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\ar[d]&W_{r}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}&\{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}&\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking kernels gives a short exact sequence of relative terms \[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow0.\] Taking global sections completes the proof since the previous paragraph showed that the left term has no $H^1_\sub{\'et}$.

nodes.name: R - F sequence of relative pro sheaves
nodes.statement: 0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0
nodes.label: equation_R-F

nodes.name: Relative pro Geisser--Levine theorem for henselian ideals
nodes.statement_short: The trace identifies pro relative K-groups mod p^r with pro relative log de Rham--Witt groups.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n,r\ge 0$.
conclusions: the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n,r\ge 0$. Then the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups \[\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s.\]
nodes.label: theorem_pro_GL_relative

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.31
nodes.statement_short: Pro HKR identifies relative TR with relative de Rham--Witt; surjectivity of R-F gives relative TC as log forms; main theorem transfers to K.
nodes.statement: The proof is similar to the techniques of \cite[\S5.1]{Morrow-HW}, but we repeat the necessary details here. In particular, we begin with the same recollections on Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg theorems for the spectra $\mathrm{TR}^s$. If $R$ is any $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, then the pro graded ring $\{\mathrm{TR}^s_*(R;p)\}_s$ is a $p$-typical Witt complex with respect to its operators $F,V,R$; by universality of the de Rham--Witt complex, there are therefore natural maps of graded $W_s(R)$-algebras \cite[Prop.~1.5.8]{Hesselholt} $\lambda_{s,R}:W_s\Omega_R^*\to \mathrm{TR}_*^s(R;p)$ for $s\ge0$, which are compatible with the Frobenius, Verschiebung, and Restriction maps (in other words, a morphism of $p$-typical Witt complexes). From now on in the proof assume that $R$ is regular, noetherian, and $F$-finite, and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. Hesselholt's HKR theorem \cite[Thm.~B]{Hesselholt} implies that the resulting map of pro abelian groups \[\lambda_R:\{W_s\Omega_R^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R;p)\}_s\] is an isomorphism for each $n\ge 1$; similarly, the pro HKR theorem of Dundas--Morrow \cite[Cor.~4.15]{DundasMorrow} implies that \[\lambda_{R/I^\infty}: \{W_s\Omega_{R/I^s}^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s \tag{pro-HKR}\] is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups for each $n\ge0$. Since $W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_s\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$ is surjective for all $s,n\ge0$, it follows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exact sequences and there are therefore natural induced isomorphisms of relative theories \[\{W_s\Omega_{(R,I^s)}^n\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\] for all $n\ge0$. Now assume that $R$ is henselian along $I$. By Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}, the map $R-F:W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$ is surjective for all $n,s\ge0$, and therefore the previous isomorphism shows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\xrightarrow{R-F}\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exacts and thereby induces natural isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;p)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\ker(W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)})\}_s\] The right side of the previous line is precisely $\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by applying \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} to $R$ and $R/I^s$ for each $s\ge1$ (in fact, we have already made this argument: just take global sections in line (\ref{equation_R-F}) for each $Y_s$ and then pass to the resulting diagonal of the $\mathbb N^2$-indexed pro abelian group); moreover, this latter pro abelian group is $p$-torsion-free by the injectivity in Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2} (this is anyway easy: the pro abelian group is contained in $\{W_s\Omega^n_R\}_s$, which is $p$-torsion-free thanks to the equality of the $p$- and canonical-filtrations on the de Rham--Witt groups of any regular $\mathbb F_p$-algebra: see \cite[Prop.~I.3.2 \& I.3.4]{illusie-derham-witt} for the case of a smooth algebra over a perfect field, then apply N\'eron--Popescu), so passing to finite coefficients gives us isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}/p^r\}_s\] for each fixed $r\ge1$. The right side is $\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by (the hard part of) Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2}. Finally, pro-constancy of $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(-;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ (Proposition \ref{prop_pro_constant}) implies that the left side of the previous line is $\{\mathrm{TC}_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$, which by Theorem \ref{mainthm} identifies with $\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ via the trace map.

nodes.name: Proof of the pro Geisser--Levine theorem
conclusions: Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL} is true.
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL} is true.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.32 (and Theorem 5.26)
nodes.statement_short: Combine Theorem 5.31 with Geisser--Levine for R.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be as in the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}. Without loss of generality $R$ is henselian along $I$, whence $R$ is also local, and so the result follows by combining Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL_relative} with the isomorphism $K_n(R; \mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ of Geisser--Levine \cite{GL}. Note that the two results are compatible since the trace map is given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols by \cite[Lem.~4.2.3 \& Cor.~6.4.1]{GH}. We establish the $p$-torsion-freeness of $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ in the next corollary.

nodes.name: Comparison to Milnor K-theory; p-torsion-freeness
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that $R/I$ is local.
conclusions: the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ is $p$-torsion-free
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that $R/I$ is local. Then, for all $n,r\ge0$: \begin{enumerate} \item the canonical map $\{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\to\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ is surjective and has the same kernel as $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\to \{W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}\}_s$; \item the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ is $p$-torsion-free. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corollary_Milnor

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.33
nodes.statement_short: Read off from the diagram of Theorem 5.26; surjectivity of dlog.
nodes.statement: We can replace $R$ by its $I$-adic completion and thereby assume $R$ itself is local. Part (1) is an immediate consequence of the commutative diagram \[\xymatrix{ \{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\ar[r]\ar@/_1cm/[rr]_{\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]}& \{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\ar[r]^{\cong}&\{W_r\Omega_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}^n\}_s }\] which summarises the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}, since the bendy arrow is surjective. Part (1) clearly implies that $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s\to \{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is surjective, whence the usual exact sequence implies it is an isomorphism and that $\{K_{n-1}(R/I^s)[p]\}_s=0$.

nodes.name: Lifting classes
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then, for all $n,r\ge0$: \begin{enumerate} \item the sequences \[0\longrightarrow \{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\longrightarrow K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\longrightarrow 0\] are short exact; \item there exists $s\ge 1$ with the following property: if an element of $K_n(R/I;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)$ lifts to $K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)$, then it is symbolic and hence lifts to $K_n(R)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corollary_lifting

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.34
nodes.statement_short: Pro K-groups are symbolic and units lift, so relative sequences split into short exact sequences.
nodes.statement: As we have just seen in Corollary \ref{corollary_Milnor}, $\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is entirely symbolic; since $R\to R/I$ is surjective on units (using the assumption $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$), we deduce that $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\to \{K_n(R/I^s;p^r\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is surjective for all $n\ge0$. Therefore the long exact relative sequences breaks into the desired short exact sequences. Part (2) is a consequence of the surjectivity arguments of the previous paragraph, unravelling what it means for a map of pro abelian groups to be surjective.

nodes.name: Relative pro Geisser--Levine for local rings
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal.
conclusions: the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then, for all $n,r\ge0$, the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups $\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.35
nodes.statement_short: Short exact sequence of Corollary 5.34 with Geisser--Levine and Theorem 5.26.
nodes.statement: This follows from the short exact sequence of Corollary \ref{corollary_lifting}(1) by applying usual Geisser--Levine to the middle term and Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL} to the right term.

nodes.name: Strictly henselian local ring
nodes.statement:
Recall that a 
local ring is called \emph{strictly henselian} if it is henselian local and its
residue field is separably closed.

nodes.name: Etale K-theory is TC at points of characteristic p
nodes.statement_short: For strictly henselian local rings of residue characteristic p, K -> TC is a p-adic equivalence.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring of residue characteristic $p$.
conclusions: $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)/p =0$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring of residue characteristic $p$. Then $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)/p =0$, i.e., the map $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence.
nodes.label: etalekthm

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem reduces to a separably closed field; nu~ vanishes as Artin--Schreier type equations are solvable.
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we may assume that $R=k$ is a field itself, which is then separably closed. Thus we need to show that if $k$ is a separably closed field of characteristic $p > 0$, then the map $K(k) \to \mathrm{TC}(k)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence. As $\mathbb{F}_p$ is perfect, $k$ is an ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra (e.g., choose a transcendence basis for $k$). Thus it suffices to show that the terms $\widetilde{\nu}^n(k)$ vanish by Theorem~\ref{GHGL}. That is, we need to show that the map \[ 1 - C^{-1}: \Omega^n_k \to \Omega^n_k/ d \Omega^{n-1}_k \] is surjective. Given a form $\omega = a dx_1 \dots dx_n \in \Omega^n_k$, we have $(1 - C^{-1})(u \omega) = (u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1}) \omega$. Since $k$ is separably closed, we can solve the equation $ u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1} = 1$ in $k$. This implies that $1 - C^{-1}$ is surjective as desired and completes the proof.

nodes.name: Suslin's invariance under extensions of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: A finitary rigid functor takes the same value on separably closed fields related by an extension.
assumptions: Suppose that $F$ commutes with filtered colimits and satisfies rigidity, i.e., for a henselian pair $(R, I)$ we have $F(R) \simeq F(R/I)$.
conclusions: for an extension $K \to L$ of separably closed fields, we have $F(K) \simeq F(L)$
nodes.statement: Let $F: \mathrm{Ring} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ be a functor from rings to abelian groups. Suppose that $F$ commutes with filtered colimits and satisfies rigidity, i.e., for a henselian pair $(R, I)$ we have $F(R) \simeq F(R/I)$. Then for an extension $K \to L$ of separably closed fields, we have $F(K) \simeq F(L)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement_short: Suslin's rigidity argument: pullbacks along sections of smooth connected schemes agree; injectivity via retractions, surjectivity via two maps to L.
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field. The crux of Suslin's argument is to show that if $q:X\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k)$ is a connected smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type, then for any class $\alpha \in F(X)$ and section $x: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$, the pullback $x^* \alpha \in F(k)$ is independent of the choice of $x$. It suffices to fix a section $x_0: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$, and show (by connectedness, in view of the Zariski density of $k$-points in $X$, cf., e.g., \cite[Tag 04QM]{stacks-project}) that there exists a Zariski neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$ such that $x_0^\ast\alpha = x^\ast\alpha$ for all sections $x:\mathrm{Spec}(k)\rightarrow U$. Replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha-q^\ast x_0^\ast \alpha$, we can assume $x^\ast\alpha=0$. Then by the assumption of rigidity, applied to the henselization of $X$ at $x_0$, and the commutation of $F$ with filtered colimits, we deduce that there is an \'etale neighborhood $Y\rightarrow X$ of $x_0$ such that $\alpha$ pulls back to $0$ on $Y$. Then we can take $U$ to be the image of $Y\rightarrow X$: as $k$ is separably closed, every $k$-point of $U$ lifts to $Y$. Now we prove the proposition. It suffices to consider the case where $K$ is the separable closure of a prime field, and so is in particular perfect. Therefore, the extension $K \to L$ is ind-smooth, i.e., $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $K$-algebras $A_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ running over a filtered poset. Then each map $K \to A_\alpha$ admits a retraction, as $K$ is separably closed. It follows that $F(K) \to F(A_\alpha)$ is injective for each $\alpha$, so that $F(K) \to F(L)$ is injective. We now argue surjectivity. Let $u \in F(A_\alpha)$; we show that the image of $u$ in $F(L)$ belongs to the image of $F(K)$. Passing to a component if necessary, we can assume $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha)$ is connected. Then $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha\otimes_K L)$ is connected as well, since $K$ is algebraically closed. Now consider the two maps \[ f_1, f_2:A_\alpha \rightrightarrows L, \] where the first map is the colimit structure map and where where the second map is $A_\alpha \stackrel{s}{\to} K \to L$. By the first paragraph of the argument applied to the $L$-algebra $A_\alpha \otimes_K L$, we conclude that these two maps have the same effect on $u$, verifying the claim.

nodes.name: Etale homotopy sheaves of K/p and TC/p
nodes.statement:
Let
$\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ denote the \'etale sheafification of the functor $\pi_n
(K(-)/p)$ over an arbitrary scheme $X$, and let $\pi_n( \mathcal{TC}/p)$ denote the same for $\pi_n (\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$.

nodes.name: Sheaf-theoretic reformulation of Theorem 6.1
nodes.statement_short: pi_n(TC/p) is pushed forward from its restriction to the characteristic-p locus, where it agrees with pi_n(K/p).
nodes.statement:
Then if $i$ denotes the closed inclusion $(X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{F}_p))_{et}\rightarrow X_{et}$, Theorem \ref{etalekthm} (plus the trivial fact that $\mathrm{TC} /p$ vanishes on rings where $p$ is invertible) is equivalent to the statement that for all $n$, there is an equivalence
\begin{equation} \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)\simeq i_\ast i^\ast
\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)\end{equation}
adjoint to the map $i^\ast\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)\rightarrow i^\ast \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$ (also an equivalence) given by the restriction of the cyclotomic trace.

nodes.name: Stalkwise description of TC/p sheaves
nodes.statement: \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)\simeq i_\ast i^\ast \pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)
nodes.label: stalkK

nodes.name: p-adic etale K-theory is TC for proper schemes over henselian bases
assumptions: Let $X$ be a scheme proper over $\mathrm{Spec} R$ for a ring $R$ henselian along $(p)$.
conclusions: is an equivalence
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme proper over $\mathrm{Spec} R$ for a ring $R$ henselian along $(p)$. Denote by $\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(-)$ the \'etale Postnikov sheafification of the $K$-theory presheaf, meaning the limit over the \'etale sheafified Postnikov tower of $K(-)$.\footnote{This is what Thomason's \'etale hypercohomology construction implements. By \cite[Thm.~1.3]{CM18} it agrees with the more basic sheafification for the etale site as considered in \cite{HTT} under very mild finiteness assumptions on $X$. We refer also to \cite[Sec.~1.3]{SAG} as a source for sheaves of spectra and the associated $t$-structure.} Then the natural map $$\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)/p\rightarrow \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$$ is an equivalence.
nodes.label: padicetaleKthy

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.3
nodes.statement_short: Proper base change reduces to the special fiber, where the etale homotopy sheaves agree.
nodes.statement: The comparison map is induced by the cyclotomic trace, given that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ is an \'etale Postnikov sheaf (see \cite[Thm 5.16]{CM18} in full generality; for affines, see \cite[Sec.~3]{GH}; in the semi-separated case see \cite{BMloc} for the conclusion of Nisnevich descent). Now assume $X$ is proper over $\mathrm{Spec}(R)$ henselian along $(p)$. Then the proper base change theorem together with Gabber's affine analog of the proper base change theorem \cite{Gabberaffine} combine to show $H^j_\sub{\'et}(X, \mathcal{F})\simeq H^j_\sub{\'et}(X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR), i^*\mathcal{F})$ for all torsion abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_{et}$. In particular, $X_{et}$ has finite $p$-cohomological dimension by induction on an affine cover and the following Lemma~\ref{finiteetale}, so by comparing descent spectral sequences for $\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)$ and $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ it suffices to show that $\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ and $\pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$ have the same cohomology on $X_\sub{\'et}$. But by the same base change results, this follows from the fact (see above) that they have the same restriction to $X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR)$.

nodes.name: Mod p etale cohomological dimension of F_p-algebras
assumptions: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.
conclusions: the mod $p$ \'etale cohomological dimension of $R$ is $\leq 1$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. Then the mod $p$ \'etale cohomological dimension of $R$ is $\leq 1$.
nodes.label: finiteetale

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement_short: Artin--Schreier sequence in the noetherian case; filtered colimits in general.
nodes.statement: This is classical in the noetherian case from the Artin-Schreier sequence (see \cite[Exp.~X, Thm.~5.1]{SGA4}). To obtain the non-noetherian case, we use the criterion from \cite[Exp. IX, Prop.~5.5]{SGA4} together with the fact that cohomology commutes with filtered colimits \cite[Tag 03Q4]{stacks-project}.

nodes.name: Asymptotic comparison of K and TC
nodes.statement_short: For R henselian along p with finite-dimensional R/p and residue fields of p-degree at most d, K/p^r = TC/p^r in degrees >= d.
assumptions: $R$ is henselian along $(p)$.
The ring $R/p$ has finite Krull dimension.
For any $x \in \mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$, the residue field $k(x)$ has the property that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$.
conclusions: The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for any $r$.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $p$ be a prime number. Suppose that $d \geq 1$ and: \begin{enumerate} \item $R$ is henselian along $(p)$. \item The ring $R/p$ has finite Krull dimension. \item For any $x \in \mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$, the residue field $k(x)$ has the property that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$. \end{enumerate} The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for any $r$.
nodes.label: KTCasymptotic

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.5
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to F_p-algebras via the main theorem, use Nisnevich descent with finite homotopy dimension, and check stalks via Geisser--Levine/Geisser--Hesselholt and p-bases.
nodes.statement: We use throughout the following basic observation: if $T \to T'$ is a map of spectra which is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$, then for any spectrum $T''$ with a map $T'' \to T'$, the map $T \times_{T'} T'' \to T''$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$. Using the pullback square from Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (involving the spectra $K(R)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r, K(R/p)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R/p)/p^r$), we reduce to the case where $R$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. It now suffices to see that $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$. Note also that the result is clearly equivalent if we replace $K(R)/p$ with $\mathbb{K}(R)/p$. By the theorems of Thomason--Trobaugh \cite{TT90} and Blumberg--Mandell \cite{BMloc} respectively, $\mathbb{K}(-)/p^r$ and $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ are Nisnevich sheaves on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ with values in the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sp}$. By \cite[Th.~3.17]{CM18}, the finiteness of Krull dimension implies that the Nisnevich topos of $\mathrm{Spec} R$ has \emph{finite homotopy dimension} in the sense of \cite[Def. 7.2.2.1]{HTT}. In the case where $R$ is noetherian, the finiteness of homotopy dimension appears in \cite[Thm.~3.7.7.1]{SAG}. As a consequence, Postnikov towers in the $\infty$-category of Nisnevich sheaves of spectra on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ are convergent and one has a descent spectral sequence. Therefore, it suffices to see that the maps on stalks induce isomorphisms in degrees $\geq d$. The maps on stalks are \[ \mathbb{K}(A)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p^r, \] as $A$ ranges over the connected finite \'etale algebras over henselizations of $R$ at prime ideals. Since the map $K(A)/p \to \mathbb{K}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 1$, it suffices to see that $K(A)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for each such $A$. This in turn follows from the fiber square of Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (applied to the henselian local ring $A$) and the fact that if $k$ is a field of characteristic $p$, then the map $K(k)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(k)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq \log_p [k: k^p]$ (which follows from Theorem~\ref{GHGL} and the theory of $p$-bases, which implies $\dim \Omega^1_k \leq d$ and so $\Omega^n_k = 0$ for $n > d$ \cite[Thm.~26.5]{Matsumura}). Note also that the invariant $\log_p [k:k^p] = \dim \Omega^1_k$ is invariant under finite separable extensions of fields of characteristic $p$.

nodes.name: p-adic Lichtenbaum--Quillen isomorphism
assumptions: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$ with $\mathrm{Spec}(R/p)$ of finite Krull dimension
conclusions: the map $K(R)/p^r\to \widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\ge d$ for any $r$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$ with $\mathrm{Spec}(R/p)$ of finite Krull dimension, and suppose that $d\ge1$ is such that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$ for all $x\in\mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$. Then the map $K(R)/p^r\to \widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\ge d$ for any $r$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic comparison for F-finite noetherian F_p-algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a noetherian $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra which is \emph{$F$-finite,} i.e., the Frobenius map is finite (Definition~\ref{Ffinite}). Then $R$ has finite Krull dimension \cite[Prop. 1.1]{Kunz}. Moreover, if $R$ is generated as a module by $p^d$ elements over the Frobenius, this passes to any localization. It follows that if $k$ is any residue field of $R$, then $[k: k^p] \leq p^d$. Therefore, the map $K(R)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p $ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ thanks to Theorem~\ref{KTCasymptotic}. Note that Theorem~\ref{KTCasymptotic} assumes that $d \geq 1$, but if $d = 0$ then $R$ is a finite product of perfect fields, so that the result follows from Example~\ref{perfex} below.

nodes.name: K and TC of perfect F_p-algebras
nodes.statement_short: For perfect F_p-algebras, K/p^r -> TC/p^r is an equivalence on connective covers.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra, i.e., such that the Frobenius is an isomorphism. Then the map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence on connective covers for each $r \geq 0$. In fact, $\mathrm{TC}_i(R)$ vanishes for $i > 0$. This follows as in the calculation of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ in \cite[Sec.~IV-4]{nikolaus-scholze}. Indeed, by a variant of B\"okstedt's calculation, one finds $\mathrm{THH}(R)_* \simeq R[\sigma]$ for $|\sigma| = 2$ and $$ \mathrm{TC}^-_*(R) = W(R)[x, \sigma]/(x \sigma - p), \quad \mathrm{TP}_*(R) \simeq W(R)[x^{\pm 1}], \quad |x| = -2.$$ If $R$ has no nontrivial idempotents, it follows that $\pi_0(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r) = \mathbb{Z}/p^r \mathbb{Z}$ and that $\pi_{-1}(\mathrm{TC}_{}(R)/p^r)$ is the cokernel of $F -1 $ on $W_r(R)$. We refer to the work of Bhatt--Morrow--Scholze \cite{BMS2} for more details. Moreover, $K_i(R)$ is a $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$-module for $i > 0$. This follows from the existence of Adams operations in higher $K$-theory and the fact that $\psi^p$ is the Frobenius, cf.~\cite{Hiller, Kratzer}. If $R$ has no nontrivial idempotents, it follows by Zariski descent that the kernel of the map $K_0(R) \to \mathbb{Z}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$-module, so that $K_0(R)/p \simeq \mathbb{Z}/p$. Combining all these observations, the claim for $R$ follows provided $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is connected. To reduce the general case to that one, note that everything commutes with filtered colimits, so we can assume $R$ is the perfection of a finite type $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is noetherian, hence a finite disjoint union of connected affines, giving the reduction.
nodes.label: perfex

nodes.name: K and TC agree in nonnegative degrees for semiperfect reductions
assumptions: Let $R$ be a ring henselian along $(p)$.
Suppose $R/p$ is a \emph{semiperfect} ring
conclusions: The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$ for any $r$.
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a ring henselian along $(p)$. Suppose $R/p$ is a \emph{semiperfect} ring, i.e., an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra such that the Frobenius map on $R/p$ is a surjection. The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$ for any $r$.
nodes.label: Kpfd

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.9
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem reduces to semiperfect F_p-algebras, then to the perfect quotient by the nilradical.
nodes.statement: Using Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we immediately reduce to the case where $R$ itself is a semiperfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. In this case, let $I \subset R$ be the nilradical. It follows that $R/I$ is perfect and that $I$ is locally nilpotent, so that $(R, I)$ is a henselian pair. By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} and Example~\ref{perfex}, it follows that the map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$.

nodes.name: K-theory of rings of integers in complete nonarchimedean fields
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be a complete nonarchimedean field whose residue field is perfect of characteristic $p$. Let $\mathcal{O}_C \subset C$ be the ring of integers, and let $\pi \in \mathcal{O}_C$ be a nonzero element of positive valuation. Then $\mathcal{O}_C$ is $\pi$-adically complete, and the image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_C \subset \mathcal{O}_C$ is a locally nilpotent ideal in $\mathcal{O}_C/\pi$: in particular, $\mathfrak{m}_C \subset \mathcal{O}_C$ is henselian. We conclude that the map $K( \mathcal{O}_C)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}( \mathcal{O}_C)/p^r$ exhibits the former as the connective cover of the latter for $r \geq 0$ since we know the analogous statement for the residue field (as in Example~\ref{perfex}). Given a perfectoid field $C$ (in the sense of \cite{Scholze}), the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_C$ has perfect residue field, so the above conclusion holds. When $C = \mathbb{C}_p$ is the completed algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic $K$-theory of $\mathcal{O}_C$ was calculated by Nizio\l, cf.~\cite[Lem~3.1]{Niziol-crystalline} which shows that $K(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p) \simeq K(C; \mathbb{C}_p)$, which in turn is $p$-adic connective topological $K$-theory by \cite{Suslinalgclosed, Suslinlocal}. Similarly, $\mathrm{TC}(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p)$ was calculated by Hesselholt \cite{HesselholtOC} and shown to agree with the $K$-theory. A description of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p)$ in general has been given in \cite{BMS2}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.12
nodes.statement_short: pi - Fbar is etale-locally surjective with rigid cokernel; compute the etale H^1 on R' and pass to R by rigidity.
nodes.statement: We claim that the map $\pi - \overline{F}$ is surjective locally in the \'etale topology and the cokernel satisfies rigidity for henselian pairs. The first claim follows because the composite map \[ W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \stackrel{R}{\to} W_r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \] actually lifts to the map $W_{r+1}\Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{R - F} W_r \Omega_R^{m}$, which is a surjection in the \'etale topology thanks to \cite[Cor. 4.1(ii)]{Morrow-HW}. Second, let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. To see that $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ is rigid, we can imitate the strategy of Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}. Namely, we let $L$ denote the kernel of the surjection $W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_{R/I}^{m}/d V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ and contemplate the commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ & & W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \ar[rru]^{R - F} \ar[r]^R & W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \ar[r]^{\psi} & L \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \ar[d] \ar[r]^R & W_r \Omega_R^{m}\ar[d] \ar[r]^-{\pi - \overline{F}} & W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^R & W_{r} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^-{\pi - \overline{F}} & W_r \Omega_{R/I}^{m}/ d V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} }.\] To prove rigidity, it suffices by the snake lemma to show that $\psi:W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \to L$ is a surjection. Note that the kernel $L$ is surjected upon by the relative forms $W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m}$; this follows easily from the fact that $\Omega_R^{m} \to \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ is a surjection. Thus, the surjectivity of $\psi$ now follows from the surjectivity of $R - F: W_{r+1} \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)} \to W_r \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)}$ given by Lemma~\ref{lemma_drw1}. Now we prove the proposition. Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra and recall that, by definition, $$\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R) = H^1( \mathrm{Spec}(R')_{\mathrm{et}}; \pi_m ( \mathcal{TC}/p^r)),$$ where $R'\rightarrow R$ is a surjective map from an ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra with henselian kernel. Since $\pi_m ( \mathcal{TC}/p^r) \simeq W_r \Omega^{m}_{\mathrm{log}}$ (as \'etale sheaves) over the ind-smooth $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ by the results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, we can use the resolution of \eqref{piminusF2} in the \'etale topology and the fact that the two terms of \eqref{piminusF2} have no higher cohomology on affines to calculate this etale cohomology group. It follows that $\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R)$ identifies with $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ on $R'$. Since we have just seen this cokernel satisfies rigidity, we can replace $R'$ by $R$, whence the claim.

nodes.name: Composite of x and phi is null

We show first that, for $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) $,

\begin{equation} \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)
\xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X)  \end{equation}
is functorially nullhomotopic. 
In fact, since
$X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, we find that
$\mathrm{TC}^-(X)$ is an $\mathrm{TC}^-( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, $\mathrm{TP}(X)$ is a
$\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, and 
the map $\varphi_X$ is $\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}$-linear.
We obtain a resulting functorial commutative diagram,
where the base-changes are along $\varphi_{ H \mathbb F_p}:
\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to
\mathrm{TP}( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$,
\begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=1cm{
\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] &  \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]
\ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\
\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})}
\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})
\ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X)
\otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})}
\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & 
 \mathrm{TP}(X)  
} .\end{equation}
 However $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}(x)$ vanishes, by
Lemma~\ref{Frobvanish}, and so the composite 
\eqref{th} is functorially nullhomotopic as desired.

can give an independent proof 
of Lemma~\ref{connectivity} (and thus of Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}) which is independent of the classical approach to
$\mathrm{TC}$ (i.e., based entirely on the formula \eqref{keyformula}).

nodes.name: Case of HF_p^triv- and p-complete HZ^triv-modules
nodes.statement:
First, suppose that $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module. In this
case, we find that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ thanks to
Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}. More generally, if $X$ is a
$p$-complete $H \mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, then we find that $X/p$ is an
$H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module so that $\mathrm{TC}(X/p) \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ belongs
to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$; by $p$-completeness we deduce that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq
-1}$.

nodes.name: General case: Adams tower with respect to HZ^triv
nodes.statement:
In general, let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ be an arbitrary $p$-complete object. 
Then, we consider the Adams tower for $X$ with respect to the commutative
algebra object $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, i.e., the tower for
the totalization of the cosimplicial object $X \otimes
(H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}})^{\otimes \bullet + 1}$ (cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.1]{MNN17} for a reference in this generality). 
That is, we consider the tower $\left\{X_n\right\} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ defined
inductively such that
$X_0 = X$ and $X_{n+1}$ is the fiber of the map $X_{n} \to X_n \otimes
H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$. 
One sees easily that $X_n \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$, and that $X_n$ is $p$-complete since $\pi_i(S^0)$ is finite for $i>0$.
nodes.statement_short: General case: Adams tower with respect to HZ^triv

nodes.name: Induct up the tower and pass to the limit by Milnor
nodes.statement:
Since $X_{n}/X_{n+1}$ is a $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, it follows from
the previous analysis that $\mathrm{TC}(X_n/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq (n-1)}$ for each $n$. 
Inductively, 
it follows now that $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) = \mathrm{TC}(X_0/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for
each $n$ and that the maps $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) \to \mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n})$ are surjective
on $\pi_{-1}$. 
Since $X \to X/X_{n+1}$ is an equivalence in degrees $\leq n$, it follows (as in \cite[Lem.~I.2.6]{nikolaus-scholze}) that
\[ X^{hS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n )^{hS^1}, \quad 
X^{tS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n)^{tS^1}
\]
and therefore by \eqref{keyformula}
\[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X/X_n).  \]
Using the Milnor exact sequence 
and the connectivity properties of $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1})$, 
one concludes that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Induct up the tower and pass to the limit by Milnor

nodes.name: Assembly map TC(X) tensor (-) -> TC(X tensor (-)^triv)
nodes.statement_short: Assembly map TC(X) tensor (-) -> TC(X tensor (-)^triv)

nodes.name: Equivalence on HF_p by Corollary 2.6
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}, it is also an equivalence on any geometric realization of finite connective spectra, i.e.,
for any connective spectrum whose homology groups are finitely generated, e.g.,
$H \mathbb F_p$.
So we have shown that, for any $X \in
\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete, there is a natural equivalence
$$\mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes
H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence on HF_p by Corollary 2.6

nodes.name: Remove p-completeness
nodes.statement:
Replacing $X$ with $X/p$, the same conclusion follows for an arbitrary
$X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remove p-completeness

nodes.name: TC tensor HF_p commutes with colimits by Corollary 2.13
nodes.statement:
Then from Corollary~\ref{Fpcommutecolimit} we deduce that the functor $X
\mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p$ commutes
with colimits in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. 
Hence, given a diagram $I\to\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq
0}$, the induced map of spectra
\begin{equation} \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X) \end{equation} 
becomes an equivalence after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$.
nodes.statement_short: TC tensor HF_p commutes with colimits by Corollary 2.13

nodes.name: Boundedness lets HF_p detect mod p equivalences
nodes.statement_short: Boundedness lets HF_p detect mod p equivalences

nodes.name: Objectwise pro-zero
nodes.statement:
First we show the weaker claim that for all $X\in\mathcal{C}$, the tower
$\{F_r(X)\}_r$ of abelian groups is pro-zero.  Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity.
From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower
$\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies
that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes.  If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis.  Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Objectwise pro-zero

nodes.name: Emmanouil: vanishing lim^1 of sums gives Mittag-Leffler
nodes.statement:
Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity.
From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower
$\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies
that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes.
nodes.statement_short: Emmanouil: vanishing lim^1 of sums gives Mittag-Leffler

nodes.name: Nonzero stable image would give a nonzero limit
nodes.statement: If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Nonzero stable image would give a nonzero limit

nodes.name: Stable images vanish: pro-zero
nodes.statement: Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Stable images vanish: pro-zero

nodes.name: Assume not pro-zero; witnesses Y for each s > r
nodes.statement: Now, suppose the claim of the lemma does not hold, i.e., that $\{F_r\}_r$ is not pro-zero.  Then for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $s>r$, we can find an $Y\in\mathcal{C}$ such that $F_s(Y)\rightarrow F_r(Y)$ is nonzero.
nodes.statement_short: Assume not pro-zero; witnesses Y for each s > r

nodes.name: Coproduct of witnesses contradicts the objectwise claim
nodes.statement: Let $X$ denote the coproduct over all pairs $s>r$ of a choice of such a $Y$.  Then for every $s>r$ the map $F_s(X)\rightarrow F_r(X)$ is nonzero, so we deduce that the tower $\{F_r(X)\}$ is not pro-zero, in contradiction to what was established above.
nodes.statement_short: Coproduct of witnesses contradicts the objectwise claim

nodes.name: lim and lim^1 vanish on each homotopy group
nodes.statement:
The Milnor sequence and induction up the Postnikov tower show that (1) implies
$\varprojlim_r \pi_i F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r \pi_i F_r(X) = 0$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: lim and lim^1 vanish on each homotopy group

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.20 to each pi_i F_r
nodes.statement: Since $\pi_i$ commutes with coproducts, we can apply the previous lemma to $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ and conclude that each tower $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 2.20 to each pi_i F_r

nodes.name: Devissage up the finite Postnikov tower
nodes.statement: Thus each Postnikov section of $\{F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero, and therefore so is $\{F_r\}_r$ itself, by devissage up the (finite) Postnikov tower.
nodes.statement_short: Devissage up the finite Postnikov tower

nodes.name: Truncated cofibers F_r; aim to show pro-zero
nodes.statement:
Setting $F_{r}(X) \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} \tau_{\leq k+1}\mathrm{cofib}( \mathrm{TC}(X)/p \to
\mathrm{TC}^r(X)/p)$, we will show that the tower $\{F_{r}(-)\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Truncated cofibers F_r; aim to show pro-zero

nodes.name: Pro-zero cofibers suffice
nodes.statement:
As $k$ varies, this shows that the map 
$\left\{\mathrm{TC}(-)/p\right\} \to \left\{\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p\right\}_r$ is a pro-isomorphism
on each homotopy group in degrees $\leq k$ (in the pro-category of functors $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Ab}$), which
is enough to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Pro-zero cofibers suffice

nodes.name: Theorem 2.7 and Lemma 2.21
nodes.statement:
Certainly $\varprojlim_r F_{r}(X) = 0$, and $F_r$ commutes with arbitrary
coproducts by Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes}, so the desired claim follows from
Lemma~\ref{invlim02}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2.7 and Lemma 2.21

nodes.name: Reduce to ind-smooth F_p-algebras by simplicial resolutions
nodes.statement: Let $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ be a filtered colimit of $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. By functorially picking simplicial resolutions of all the terms by ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebras, and recalling that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations of rings, we reduce to the case in which all the $R_i$ (hence also $R$ itself) are ind-smooth over $\mathbb F_p$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to ind-smooth F_p-algebras by simplicial resolutions

nodes.name: HKR identifies TR(R;p)/p with W Omega/p for ind-smooth R
nodes.statement:
Next we use Hesselholt's HKR theorem. Since each $\mathrm{TR}^s(-;p)$
commutes with filtered colimits (induction on (\ref{keyformulaclassical})), as
does $W_s\Omega^n_{-}$, the formula \eqref{HHKR1} remains valid for ind-smooth $\mathbb
F_p$-algebras. By taking the inverse limit over $s$,  we deduce that
$\pi_*(\mathrm{TR}(R;p)) \simeq W\Omega_R^*$ for any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$,
i.e., \eqref{HHKR2} is valid in the ind-smooth case as well.
Note here that each $W\Omega_R^n$ is $p$-torsion-free, by a basic property of
the de Rham--Witt complex for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras \cite[Cor.~I.3.6]{illusie-derham-witt} which can easily be extended to the ind-smooth case as it
derives from the stronger assertion that each Restriction map $W_s \Omega_R^{\ast} \to
W_{s-1} \Omega_R^{\ast}$ annihilates every element $x \in W_s \Omega_R^{\ast}$
with $px  = 0$.
As a result, we also conclude that 
$\pi_* ( \mathrm{TR}(R; p)/p) \simeq W \Omega_R^{\ast}/p$.
nodes.statement_short: HKR identifies TR(R;p)/p with W Omega/p for ind-smooth R

nodes.name: Exact sequence for pi_n(TC/p); reduce to ker/coker of F-1
nodes.statement:
Taking fixed points for the Frobenius, 
we find that $\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)$ fits into an exact sequence
\[W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\longrightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)\longrightarrow
W\Omega^{n}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n}_R/p,\] and similarly for each $R_i$. To complete the proof it is enough to show, for each $n\ge0$, that the kernel and cokernel of $F-1:W\Omega^{n}_-/p\to W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ commutes with our filtered colimit $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$; we stress that $W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ does not commute with filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: Exact sequence for pi_n(TC/p); reduce to ker/coker of F-1

nodes.name: Compare F-1 with C^{-1}-1 by a square
nodes.statement_short: Compare F-1 with C^{-1}-1 by a square

nodes.name: Reduce to kernels of vertical maps, spanned by images of V, dV
nodes.statement:
To see this, it suffices to show that the map induced between the kernels of
the vertical maps (which are surjective) is an isomorphism. 
The kernel of the map $W \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R$ is generated by the images
of $V, dV$ by \cite[Proposition
I.3.18]{illusie-derham-witt}.  Note that the citation is for smooth
$\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, but the statement clearly passes to an ind-smooth
algebra as the terms $W_s \Omega^n_{-}$ commute with filtered colimits and $W
\Omega^n_{-} = \varprojlim W_s \Omega^n_{-}$. 
It follows that 
the kernel of the first vertical map in \eqref{thisdiag} is spanned by the
images of $V, dV$ while the kernel of the second vertical map is spanned by the
images of $V, d$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to kernels of vertical maps, spanned by images of V, dV

nodes.name: Need F-1 bijective on images of V and dV
nodes.statement:
Thus, we need to show that the map
\begin{equation} F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to 
\mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right)
\end{equation} 
 is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Need F-1 bijective on images of V and dV

nodes.name: Surjectivity from identities (F-1)V = -V etc.
nodes.statement:
First, we show that $F-1$ is surjective. 
We record the following identities in $W \Omega_R^n/p$,
\[(F-1)V=-V,\qquad (F-1)d\sum_{i>0}V^i=d;\]
using it, we see immediately that $F - 1$ is surjective in \eqref{mapFminusone}.
nodes.statement_short: Surjectivity from identities (F-1)V = -V etc.

nodes.name: Image of F = forms with dw divisible by p (Illusie), extended to ind-smooth
nodes.statement:
To see injectivity, 
we will use an important property of the de Rham--Witt complex: the image of $F$ on
$W \Omega_R^n$ consists precisely of those elements $w$ with $dw$ divisible by
$p$, thanks to \cite[(I.3.21.1.5)]{illusie-derham-witt}. Again, the reference is stated in
the smooth case, but it also passes to the ind-smooth case;\footnote{Since the
passage to the ind-smooth case is not completely immediate, we provide the
argument. Firstly, the quasi-isomorphisms $W_s \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq
\Omega_R^{\bullet}$ for $s\ge1$ in the smooth case
\cite[Corol.~I.3.15]{illusie-derham-witt} extend at once to the ind-smooth case,
and taking the limit then shows $W \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^\bullet$
(to take the limit recall again that the $p$-torsion in $W_s\Omega^n_R$ is
annihilated by $R:W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_R$). Secondly, the identity
$\ker(d \colon \Omega^n_R\to\Omega^{n+1}_R)=\mathrm{Im}( F \colon
W_2\Omega^n_R\to \Omega^n_R)$ also extends at once from the smooth
\cite[Prop.~I.3.21]{illusie-derham-witt} to the ind-smooth case. Therefore,
given $w\in W\Omega^n_R$ satisfying $dw\in pW\Omega^n_R$, we may write $w=Fx+y$
for some $x,y\in W\Omega^n_R$ such that $y$ vanishes in $\Omega^n_R$. But then
$dy=dw-pFdx\in pW\Omega^n_R$, so $y$ defines a class in $H^n(W\Omega^\bullet/p)$
which vanishes in $H^n(\Omega^\bullet_R)$; by the first claim, we deduce that
the initial class was zero, in other words that $y=dz+pz'$ for some $z\in
W\Omega^{n-1}_R$, $z'\in W\Omega^n_R$. So $w= Fx+FdVz+FVz'$, as required.} for more on this
point cf.~\cite[Sec.~2]{BLM}.
nodes.statement_short: Image of F = forms with dw divisible by p (Illusie), extended to ind-smooth

nodes.name: Injectivity: show x divisible by p
nodes.statement:
Suppose $x \in W \Omega^n_R$
can be written as $x = Vy + dVz$ and $(F -1 )x $ is divisible by $p$; we show
that $x $ is divisible by $p$ in $ W \Omega^n_R$. This will hold if $y, z \in
\mathrm{im}(F)$. 
First, $-dx \equiv d((F-1) x)$ modulo $p$, so $dx$ is divisible by $p$. 
It follows that 
$d Vy$, and hence $dy = FdVy$ is divisible by $p$, so that $y$ belongs to the
image of $F$. In particular, modulo $p$, we have $x \equiv dV z$ and 
$(F-1) d Vz  = d (z - Vz)$ is divisible by $p$. 
Therefore, $z - Vz$ belongs to the image of $F$. Since the operator $V$ is
topologically nilpotent on $W \Omega^n_R$, we find that $(1 - V)$ is invertible
and $z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. 
Therefore, $x$ is divisible by $p$ as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity: show x divisible by p

nodes.name: Suffices y, z in im(F)
nodes.statement:
This will hold if $y, z \in
\mathrm{im}(F)$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices y, z in im(F)

nodes.name: dx divisible by p, so y in im(F)
nodes.statement:
First, $-dx \equiv d((F-1) x)$ modulo $p$, so $dx$ is divisible by $p$. 
It follows that 
$d Vy$, and hence $dy = FdVy$ is divisible by $p$, so that $y$ belongs to the
image of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: dx divisible by p, so y in im(F)

nodes.name: z - Vz in im(F)
nodes.statement:
In particular, modulo $p$, we have $x \equiv dV z$ and 
$(F-1) d Vz  = d (z - Vz)$ is divisible by $p$. 
Therefore, $z - Vz$ belongs to the image of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: z - Vz in im(F)

nodes.name: Topological nilpotence of V gives z in im(F)
nodes.statement:
Since the operator $V$ is
topologically nilpotent on $W \Omega^n_R$, we find that $(1 - V)$ is invertible
and $z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$.
nodes.statement_short: Topological nilpotence of V gives z in im(F)

nodes.name: x divisible by p
nodes.statement: Therefore, $x$ is divisible by $p$ as desired.
nodes.statement_short: x divisible by p

nodes.name: Henselian nonunital algebras are an orthogonality class
nodes.statement:
It follows from the above discussion that $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is the orthogonal \cite[Sec.~5.4]{Borceux1} of $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$
with respect to the maps
\[ f_{n,t}: R[x_0, \dots, x_t]^+  \to 
R[x_0, \dots, x_t, y]^+/( y(1 + y)^{n-1} + x_0 + x_1 y + \dots + x_t y^t ),\]
for $n, t \geq 1$. 
That is, a given object $X \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ belongs to $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ if and only
\begin{equation} \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}(
R[x_0, \dots, x_t, y]^+/( y(1 + y)^{n-1} + x_0 + x_1 y + \dots + x_t y^t ), X)
\xrightarrow{\cdot\circ f_{n,t}}
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R}(R[x_0, \dots, x_t]^+ , X)
\end{equation}
is an isomorphism for all $n,t\ge1$.
nodes.statement_short: Henselian nonunital algebras are an orthogonality class

nodes.name: Orthogonality classes are presentable reflective subcategories
nodes.statement:
It now follows formally that $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ is presentable and the
desired left adjoint exists \cite[Cor. 5.4.8]{Borceux1}.
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality classes are presentable reflective subcategories

nodes.name: Alternative: henselize the pair (R semidirect I, I)
nodes.statement:
Alternatively, one can appeal to the theory of henselian pairs and define the
left adjoint directly by taking the henselization of the pair $(R \ltimes I, I)$; see the forthcoming Construction \ref{construction_henselization}.
nodes.statement_short: Alternative: henselize the pair (R semidirect I, I)

nodes.name: Base change the Milnor square along S -> S^h
nodes.statement:
Since $S^h$ is flat over $S$, we can base-change \eqref{milnsquare} along $S \to
S^h$ to obtain a
new Milnor square
\[  \xymatrix{
S^h \ar[d]  \ar[r] & T \otimes_S S^h    \ar[d]  \\
S' \otimes_S S^h \ar[r] &  T' \otimes_S S^h
}.  \]
Note that $S' \otimes_S S^h  \simeq S'$ by the properties of the henselization, and similarly for $T$. Therefore the bottom arrow can be rewritten as $S' \to T'$.
nodes.statement_short: Base change the Milnor square along S -> S^h

nodes.name: Right vertical map is henselian by Proposition 3.16
nodes.statement:
Since this is a Milnor square and the left vertical arrow is a henselian pair,
so is the right vertical arrow thanks to Proposition~\ref{checkhensnonunital}.
nodes.statement_short: Right vertical map is henselian by Proposition 3.16

nodes.name: Recognize T^h via Remark 3.19
nodes.statement:
We have a factorization  $T \to T \otimes_S S^h \to  T'$ as the composite of an
ind-\'etale map and a map having the right lifting property with respect to
\'etale maps. Thus, the result follows in view of Remark~\ref{hensfact}.
nodes.statement_short: Recognize T^h via Remark 3.19

nodes.name: Notation I^{nuh}
nodes.statement:
To distinguish the possible henselizations which a priori might not coincide, we
temporarily write $I^{nuh}$ to denote the henselization of $I$ as an object of
$\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$. The equivalence between $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu}}_R$ and augmented $R$-algebras easily implies
that $(R\ltimes I^{nuh},I^{nuh})$ is the henselization of the pair $(R \ltimes I, I)$.
nodes.statement_short: Notation I^{nuh}

nodes.name: Lemma 3.21 on a Milnor square identifies I^{nuh} with I^h
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.21 on a Milnor square identifies I^{nuh} with I^h

nodes.name: WLOG d = 0
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we can assume $d =0 $ by shifting.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG d = 0

nodes.name: (1)=>(2): truncation preserves compact objects
nodes.statement:
For (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), suppose that $F\in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp})$ (we do not
need $F$ connective) is pseudocoherent and let $n\in\mathbb Z$. Then by definition there is a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to
F$ inducing an equivalence $\tau_{\leq n} F' \simeq \tau_{\leq n} F$. Since
$\tau_{\leq n}: \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp}) \to \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, 
\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n})$ preserves compact objects (as its right adjoint preserves filtered
colimits), it follows that $\tau_{\leq n} F  \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, 
\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n})$ is compact.
nodes.statement_short: (1)=>(2): truncation preserves compact objects

nodes.name: (2)=>(3): build cell filtration killing homotopy degree by degree
nodes.statement:
For (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3), suppose that $F \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C},
\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})$ and $\tau_{\leq n} F  \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, 
\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$.  Then, by assumption $\tau_{\leq 0} F  \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Ab})
\subset \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp}_{\leq 0})$ is
a compact object and thus $\pi_0 F$ is a finitely generated functor. 
We can thus find a functor $G \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})$ which is a
direct sum of $\Sigma^\infty_+
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)$, for finitely many
$X\in\mathcal C$, and a map $G \to F$ which is a surjection on
$\pi_0$. Let $F_1 $ be the resulting cofiber and observe that $F_1$
has the same property as $F$ (namely $\tau_{\leq n} F_1 \in \mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, 
\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$, since compact objects are closed under pushouts) and that $F_1 $ is connected.  
Continuing in this way, we find a sequence of functors $F \to F_1 \to F_2 \to
\dots $ such that 
$F_n$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq n$ and such that the cofiber of each $F_n \to F_{n+1}$ is
a finite direct sum of shifts of representables.  We obtain the desired sequence $G_n$ by setting $G_n=\operatorname{Fib}(F\to F_{n+1})$.
nodes.statement_short: (2)=>(3): build cell filtration killing homotopy degree by degree

nodes.name: (3)=>(1): finite stages are perfect approximations
nodes.statement:
For (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1), note that each $G_n$ is perfect by induction on $n$,
and that $G_{n+1}\rightarrow F$ is an equivalence on $\tau_{\leq n}$.
nodes.statement_short: (3)=>(1): finite stages are perfect approximations

nodes.name: D-perfect functors are left Kan extended
nodes.statement:
The functor $\Sigma^\infty_+ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot) \in
\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Sp})$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$ is left Kan extended from
$\mathcal{D}$, so a thick subcategory argument shows that any
$\mathcal{D}$-perfect functor is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: D-perfect functors are left Kan extended

nodes.name: Truncations detect left Kan extension
nodes.statement:
To get
the same for any $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functor, note that the
truncations $\mathrm{Sp}\rightarrow \mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n}$ are a conservative family of
colimit-preserving functors, so a functor to $\mathrm{Sp}$ is left Kan extended if and
only if its image in each $\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n}$ is.
nodes.statement_short: Truncations detect left Kan extension

nodes.name: Converse: Kan extend perfect approximations
nodes.statement:
Conversely, suppose that $F$ is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ and $F|_{\mathcal{D}}: \mathcal{D}
