\to \mathrm{Sp}$ is pseudocoherent.  Then $\tau_{\leq n}F\mid_\mathcal{D}\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G\mid_\mathcal{D}$ for some $G:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathrm{Sp}$ in the thick subcategory generated by the $\Sigma^\infty_+ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$, and we deduce $\tau_{\leq n}F\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G$ by left Kan extension.
nodes.statement_short: Converse: Kan extend perfect approximations

nodes.name: WLOG C = D and d = 0
nodes.statement:
Thanks to Lemma~\ref{lkanpscoh}, 
 we may assume without loss of generality that $\mathcal{C} =
\mathcal{D}$, since the property of being left Kan extended is preserved under
all colimits. We may also take $d = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG C = D and d = 0

nodes.name: Thickness from compactness (Lemma 4.3)
nodes.statement:
Claim (1) follows from 
Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} because
compact objects (of any $\infty$-category) are closed under finite colimits and
retracts.
nodes.statement_short: Thickness from compactness (Lemma 4.3)

nodes.name: Colimits over skeletally finite K are finite in each range
nodes.statement:
For (2), 
it suffices by Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} to show that
$\tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_K f )$ is compact as an object of $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{C},
\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq n})$ for each $n$. 
But $\tau_{\leq n} f = \tau_{\leq n}  ( \varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f)$
and
$\varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f$ is a finite colimit of pseudocoherent
functors, hence pseudocoherent itself by (1); this implies the desired compactness
assertion.
nodes.statement_short: Colimits over skeletally finite K are finite in each range

nodes.name: Geometric realizations: truncated realizations are finite
nodes.statement:
Claim (3) is handled similarly, because
$\tau_{\leq n} ( |F_\bullet|) \simeq \tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_{\Delta_{\leq
n+1} }F)$ can be computed as a truncated geometric realization, and this is a
finite colimit, cf.~\cite[Lemma~1.2.4.17]{HA}.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric realizations: truncated realizations are finite

nodes.name: Bottom homotopy finitely generated from the filtration
nodes.statement: Claim (4) follows from the filtration Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact}.
nodes.statement_short: Bottom homotopy finitely generated from the filtration

nodes.name: Smash products of corepresentables are corepresentable
nodes.statement:
For (5), it suffices to observe that the smash products of functors of the form
$\{\Sigma^\infty_+ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)\}_{X \in \mathcal{D}}$ are still of this form under the
assumption that $\mathcal{C}$ has finite coproducts and $\mathcal{D} \subset
\mathcal{C}$ is closed under them. It then follows
by a thick subcategory argument that the subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functors is
closed under smash products, which implies the analogous assertion for
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors.
nodes.statement_short: Smash products of corepresentables are corepresentable

nodes.name: (2) iff (3): constant functor is corepresentable
nodes.statement:
The equivalence of (2) and (3) follows because $\Sigma^\infty, \Sigma^\infty_+$
differ by the constant functor at $S^0$, which is corepresentable since
$\mathcal{C}$ has an initial object in $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: (2) iff (3): constant functor is corepresentable

nodes.name: (1)=>(2) via the Goodwillie tower
nodes.statement:
Suppose $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. 
Using Proposition~\ref{goodwilliefilt}, 
we conclude that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is the homotopy limit of a
tower whose associated graded is given by $F, (F^{\otimes 2})_{h
\Sigma_2}, (F^{\otimes 3})_{h \Sigma_3 }, \dots $. 
Since $F$ takes values in $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 1}$, the connectivity of the associated graded terms
tends to $\infty$, so this tower stabilizes in any given finite range. As $F$
is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so are all the graded terms in
view of Proposition~\ref{general:pscoh}. It follows that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: (1)=>(2) via the Goodwillie tower

nodes.name: Tower with layers (F^{tensor n})_{h Sigma_n}
nodes.statement:
Using Proposition~\ref{goodwilliefilt}, 
we conclude that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is the homotopy limit of a
tower whose associated graded is given by $F, (F^{\otimes 2})_{h
\Sigma_2}, (F^{\otimes 3})_{h \Sigma_3 }, \dots $.
nodes.statement_short: Tower with layers (F^{tensor n})_{h Sigma_n}

nodes.name: Layers grow in connectivity; tower stabilizes
nodes.statement:
Since $F$ takes values in $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 1}$, the connectivity of the associated graded terms
tends to $\infty$, so this tower stabilizes in any given finite range.
nodes.statement_short: Layers grow in connectivity; tower stabilizes

nodes.name: Layers are D-pseudocoherent by Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement:
As $F$
is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so are all the graded terms in
view of Proposition~\ref{general:pscoh}.
nodes.statement_short: Layers are D-pseudocoherent by Proposition 4.8

nodes.name: Sigma^infty Omega^infty F is D-pseudocoherent
nodes.statement:
It follows that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Sigma^infty Omega^infty F is D-pseudocoherent

nodes.name: (2)=>(1) via the monadic bar resolution
nodes.statement:
Conversely, suppose $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. 
First, recall that the adjunction $(\Sigma^\infty, \Omega^\infty)$
between the $\infty$-categories of pointed spaces and connective spectra is monadic since
$\Omega^\infty|_{\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}}$ commutes with sifted colimits \cite[Prop.~1.4.3.9]{HA} and in view of the $\infty$-categorical monadicity theorem
\cite[Sec.~4.7.3]{HA}; 
alternatively, this follows explicitly from delooping
machinery going back to \cite{Maygeom}.  
As a result of monadicity, for any $X \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}$, one has a natural simplicial spectrum
(the bar resolution) $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^{\bullet + 1} X$ whose
geometric realization is equivalent to $X$.  
Therefore, in our case, we can
resolve $F$ via the iterates $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^k F$ for $k \geq 1$.
By the previous direction and our assumption, each of these is
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
Thus we have written $F$ as a geometric realization of
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent
functors $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 1}$,
so $F$ itself is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: (2)=>(1) via the monadic bar resolution

nodes.name: Sigma^infty / Omega^infty adjunction is monadic
nodes.statement:
First, recall that the adjunction $(\Sigma^\infty, \Omega^\infty)$
between the $\infty$-categories of pointed spaces and connective spectra is monadic since
$\Omega^\infty|_{\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}}$ commutes with sifted colimits \cite[Prop.~1.4.3.9]{HA} and in view of the $\infty$-categorical monadicity theorem
\cite[Sec.~4.7.3]{HA}; 
alternatively, this follows explicitly from delooping
machinery going back to \cite{Maygeom}.
nodes.statement_short: Sigma^infty / Omega^infty adjunction is monadic

nodes.name: Bar resolution of X
nodes.statement:
As a result of monadicity, for any $X \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}$, one has a natural simplicial spectrum
(the bar resolution) $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^{\bullet + 1} X$ whose
geometric realization is equivalent to $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Bar resolution of X

nodes.name: Resolve F by iterates
nodes.statement:
Therefore, in our case, we can
resolve $F$ via the iterates $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^k F$ for $k \geq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Resolve F by iterates

nodes.name: Each iterate is D-pseudocoherent
nodes.statement:
By the previous direction and our assumption, each of these is
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Each iterate is D-pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Geometric realization of D-pseudocoherent functors
nodes.statement:
Thus we have written $F$ as a geometric realization of
$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent
functors $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 1}$,
so $F$ itself is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric realization of D-pseudocoherent functors

nodes.name: Reduce to: one N kills F_0(NI) -> F_0(I) for all I
nodes.statement:
We will prove the following claim: there exists $N\ge1$ such that, for any $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$, the inclusion map $i_N:NI\to I$ induces the zero map $0=(i_N)_*: F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$.
Once this is done, the statement of the lemma will follow by applying (1) and (3) to the short exact sequence $NI\to I\to I/NI$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to: one N kills F_0(NI) -> F_0(I) for all I

nodes.name: Each element of F_0 on a free algebra is killed by some [N]
nodes.statement:
As in Corollary~\ref{rationalhens}, let $[N]: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \to
\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$ be the operator that multiplies each
$x_i$ by $N$, so that the colimit of the $[N]$, indexed over $N\ge1$ ordered by divisibility, is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$. 
By assumption $F_0$ commutes with filtered colimits
and annihilates any
nonunital henselian 
$\mathbb{Q}$-algebra; so, given any element 
$u \in F_0(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+)$, it follows that there
exists $N > 0$ such that $[N]_*(u) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Each element of F_0 on a free algebra is killed by some [N]

nodes.name: Generators g_i of F_0
nodes.statement:
Now we use that $F_0$ is projectively finitely generated. This means that there exists a surjection 
\[ \bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}}(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+, \cdot)] \to F_0\] of functors for some $n_1,\dots,n_t\ge1$. For each $i=1,\dots,t$, let $g_i\in F_0(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+)$ be the image of $\mathrm{id}\in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}}(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+, \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+)$. Then the above surjection concretely means the following: given any $I\in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$ and any element $y\in F_0(I)$, then $y$ is a finite sum of elements of $F_0(I)$ obtained by pushing forward the $g_i$ along various maps $\phi:\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1,
\dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+ \to I$.
nodes.statement_short: Generators g_i of F_0

nodes.name: One N kills all generators, hence the claim
nodes.statement:
By the second paragraph, there exists an integer $N > 0$ such that $[N]_*(g_i)=0$ for all the generators $g_i$. From this we can easily complete the proof of the claim, as follows. Given any $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$, every map $\phi: \mathbb{Z}\{ x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\}^+ \to  N I 
$ has the property that the composite
$i_N \circ \phi: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+ \to
I$ factors through $[N]$, i.e., one has
a commutative diagram
in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$
\[ \xymatrix{
\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \ar[r]_-{\phi}\ar[d]^{[N]} &  NI
\ar[d]^{i_N}  \\
\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \ar[r] &  I
}.\]
By choice of $N$ it follows that the composite
\[ \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}}( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots,
x_{n_i}\right\}^+, NI)] \to 
F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)
\]
is zero.  But we have shown that every element of $F_0(NI)$ is a finite sum of 
elements of the form $\phi_*(g_i)$ for various maps $\phi$. Since $g_i
\in F_0( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+)$ is annihilated by $[N]$,
it follows that $(i_N)_*: F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$ is zero, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: One N kills all generators, hence the claim

nodes.name: Maps into NI factor through [N]
nodes.statement:
Given any $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$, every map $\phi: \mathbb{Z}\{ x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\}^+ \to  N I 
$ has the property that the composite
$i_N \circ \phi: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+ \to
I$ factors through $[N]$, i.e., one has
a commutative diagram
in $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$
\[ \xymatrix{
\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \ar[r]_-{\phi}\ar[d]^{[N]} &  NI
\ar[d]^{i_N}  \\
\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \ar[r] &  I
}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Maps into NI factor through [N]

nodes.name: Composite from corepresentables is zero
nodes.statement:
By choice of $N$ it follows that the composite
\[ \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}}( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots,
x_{n_i}\right\}^+, NI)] \to 
F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)
\]
is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Composite from corepresentables is zero

nodes.name: (i_N)_* is zero
nodes.statement:
But we have shown that every element of $F_0(NI)$ is a finite sum of 
elements of the form $\phi_*(g_i)$ for various maps $\phi$. Since $g_i
\in F_0( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\right\}^+)$ is annihilated by $[N]$,
it follows that $(i_N)_*: F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$ is zero, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: (i_N)_* is zero

nodes.name: Restrict F to algebras over a prime field
nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be a prime field  and
restrict $F$ to $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$ to obtain a functor $F_R: \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \to \mathrm{Sp}$. 
We observe first that $F_R$ 
is projectively pseudocoherent  (since the building blocks $I
\mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$ for
projectively pseudocoherent functors $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R \to \mathrm{Sp}$ are independent of the base ring $R$).
nodes.statement_short: Restrict F to algebras over a prime field

nodes.name: Kan extension from free algebras where F vanishes
nodes.statement:
In particular, $F_R$ is left Kan extended from the subcategory
$(\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R)_{\Sigma}$. By assumption, $F_R$ annihilates $(\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R)_\Sigma$, so that
$F_R = 0$ on $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}_R$.
nodes.statement_short: Kan extension from free algebras where F vanishes

nodes.name: F kills henselian algebras over fields
nodes.statement:
It follows that $F$ annihilates 
any nonunital henselian algebra over a field.
nodes.statement_short: F kills henselian algebras over fields

nodes.name: F kills bounded-torsion I via nilpotent pI
nodes.statement:
Moreover, if $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$ is such that there exists $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$
with $NI = 0$, it follows that $F(I) = 0$: in fact, since $F$ preserves finite
products we reduce to the case where
$N  = p^r$ for some $r$, and then use the short exact sequence
$pI \to I \to I/p I$ where $pI$ is nilpotent. 
The resulting fiber sequence then shows that $F(I) \simeq F(I/pI) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: F kills bounded-torsion I via nilpotent pI

nodes.name: Take minimal d with pi_d F nonzero
nodes.statement:
Suppose $F$ is not the zero functor. 
Let $d$ be minimal such that $\pi_d F \neq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Take minimal d with pi_d F nonzero

nodes.name: pi_d F satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma 4.15
nodes.statement:
Then $\pi_d F$ is a
projectively finitely
generated functor $\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ which commutes with filtered
colimits; furthermore, $\pi_d F$ annihilates any $I \in \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$ which is either
of bounded torsion or a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space.
nodes.statement_short: pi_d F satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma 4.15

nodes.name: Lemma 4.15 gives a contradiction
nodes.statement:
Using 
Lemma~\ref{gabberlem} below, we find that $\pi_d F = 0$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.15 gives a contradiction

nodes.name: Homological stability with range independent of I
nodes.statement:
First, by the homological stability results of Maazen and van der Kallen
\cite{vdK}, we can approximate $C_*(BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I);
\mathbb{Z})$ by 
$C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I);
\mathbb{Z})$ in any given finite range. It is crucial for us that this stability range is independent of
the choice of $I$: namely, the stability range depends on the Krull dimension of
the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$, but since $I$ is contained
in the Jacobson radical this is the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Homological stability with range independent of I

nodes.name: Reduce to GL_n
nodes.statement:
Thus, it suffices to show that for any $n$, the functor $I \mapsto
C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to GL_n

nodes.name: Write C_*(BGL_n(Z semidirect I)) as homotopy orbits
nodes.statement:
We use the short
exact sequence of groups
\[ 1 \to GL_n(1 + I) \to GL_n( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I) \to GL_n(\mathbb{Z}) \to 1,  \]
where $GL_n(1 + I)$ is, by definition, the kernel of the second map in the above
sequence. It follows that 
there is a $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-action on 
$C_*(BGL_n(1 + I);
\mathbb{Z})$ and we have
\begin{equation} C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})
\simeq C_*(BGL_n(1 + I);
\mathbb{Z})_{h GL_n(\mathbb{Z})}.  \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write C_*(BGL_n(Z semidirect I)) as homotopy orbits

nodes.name: Bar construction on GL_n(1+I) = I^{n^2} is projectively pseudocoherent
nodes.statement:
We next argue that the functor 
$I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent. 
Note that as a set, $GL_n(1 + I)$ is naturally isomorphic to the
cartesian product  $I^{n^2}$ since $I$ is contained in
the radical of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$. 
Now we observe that using the classical bar construction and the
isomorphism (of sets) 
$GL_n(1 + I) \simeq I^{n^2}$, that 
$C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is a geometric realization of
functors of the form $I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}]$ for $i \geq 0$. Since 
the functor
$I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}] 
 \simeq H \mathbb{Z} \otimes \Sigma^\infty_+
 \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}}(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n^2i}\right\}^+, I)$ is clearly 
projectively pseudocoherent, it follows that 
$I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 +I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Bar construction on GL_n(1+I) = I^{n^2} is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Borel--Serre finiteness: homotopy orbits preserve pseudocoherence
nodes.statement:
Finally, the group $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ admits a finite index normal subgroup $N \leq
GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $BN$ has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex,
by the existence of the Borel-Serre compactification (see \cite{Serresurvey}
for a survey). Since $(-)_{hGL_n(\mathbb{Z})} \simeq ((-)_{hN})_{h(G/N)}$, we conclude by two applications of Proposition \ref{general:pscoh} that taking $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-homotopy orbits preserves projective
pseudocoherence. Therefore, 
we conclude in view of the previous paragraph and \eqref{glnZorbit}.
nodes.statement_short: Borel--Serre finiteness: homotopy orbits preserve pseudocoherence

nodes.name: Projective modules over R and R/I correspond
nodes.statement:
In fact, we claim that isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective $R$
modules and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective $R/I$-modules
agree.
nodes.statement_short: Projective modules over R and R/I correspond

nodes.name: Isomorphisms lift by Nakayama
nodes.statement:
For one direction, if $M, N$ are finitely generated projective $R$-modules, then any
isomorphism $M/IM \simeq N/IM$ can be lifted to a map $M \to N$, which is
necessarily an isomorphism by Nakayama's lemma applied to the kernel; we use
here that  $I$ is contained in the
Jacobson radical of $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Isomorphisms lift by Nakayama

nodes.name: Projectives lift by lifting idempotents
nodes.statement:
For the other direction, by lifting idempotents any
projective $R/I$-module lifts to $R$, cf. \cite[Tag 0D49]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: Projectives lift by lifting idempotents

nodes.name: HA as colimit of desuspended Eilenberg--MacLane spaces
nodes.statement:
We can write functorially $HA = \varinjlim_n \Sigma^{-n}\Sigma^\infty  K(A, n)$
for $K(A, n)$ the $n$th Eilenberg--MacLane space for $A$.
nodes.statement_short: HA as colimit of desuspended Eilenberg--MacLane spaces

nodes.name: Freudenthal reduces to Sigma^infty K(A,n)
nodes.statement:
This colimit stabilizes in any ranges of degrees by the Freudenthal suspension
theorem, so it suffices to show that the functor 
$A \mapsto \Sigma^\infty K(A, n)$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Freudenthal reduces to Sigma^infty K(A,n)

nodes.name: Iterated bar construction gives products of A
nodes.statement:
But this
follows from the iterated bar construction which gives a functorial model for
$K(A, n)$ as the colimit of an $n$-fold simplicial space each of whose terms is
a product of copies of $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterated bar construction gives products of A

nodes.name: Reduce to finite type by filtered colimits
nodes.statement: First we note that it suffices to prove this theorem in the case where $R$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{F}_p$, by extending using filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finite type by filtered colimits

nodes.name: Part (1) from Geisser--Levine
nodes.statement:
Then the first assertion follows from \cite[Thm.~8.3]{GL}, 
which shows that on smooth varieties over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the Zariski
sheafification of  
the presheaf
$\pi_n(K(\cdot)/p)$
is given by $\nu^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (1) from Geisser--Levine

nodes.name: Etale sheaves of TC/p are nu^n with descent spectral sequence (Geisser--Hesselho
nodes.statement:
The exact sequence describing $\pi_n( \mathrm{TC}(R)/p)$ actually follows from
\eqref{thisdiag}, though we will give a slightly different proof of the
stronger second claim. 
Namely, we use the results of Geisser--Hesselholt \cite[Thm.~4.2.6]{GH}
that on smooth quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over $\mathbb{F}_p$,
the homotopy group sheaves in the \emph{\'etale} topology of $\mathrm{TC}/p$ identify with those of $K/p$ via the cyclotomic trace, and hence identify with the $\nu^n$; and moreover one has an \'etale descent spectral
sequence starting from the \'etale cohomology of $\nu^n$ and converging to
$\pi_*( \mathrm{TC}/p)$.
nodes.statement_short: Etale sheaves of TC/p are nu^n with descent spectral sequence (Geisser--Hesselholt)

nodes.name: Artin--Schreier type sequence; quasi-coherent terms are acyclic
nodes.statement:
In the \'etale topology, there is a short exact sequence of sheaves $0 \to \nu^n \to
\Omega^n \xrightarrow{1 - C^{-1}} \Omega^n/d \Omega^{n-1} \to 0$, and the
second and third terms are quasi-coherent (either over the structure sheaf or
its Frobenius twist by Lemma~\ref{qcohomega}), so have no higher cohomology on affines.
nodes.statement_short: Artin--Schreier type sequence; quasi-coherent terms are acyclic

nodes.name: H^0 = nu^n and H^1 = nu~^n give part (2)
nodes.statement:
It follows that $H^0( (\mathrm{Spec} R)_{et}, 
u^n) = 
u^n(R), H^1( (\mathrm{Spec} R)_{et}, 
u^n) =
\widetilde{
u}^n(R)$, and the 'etale descent spectral sequence thus implies
the second claim.
nodes.statement_short: H^0 = nu^n and H^1 = nu~^n give part (2)

nodes.name: Part (3) from (1) and (2)
nodes.statement: The third claim follows from the first two.
nodes.statement_short: Part (3) from (1) and (2)

nodes.name: Kernels V_0, V_1 of reduction maps
nodes.statement_short: Kernels V_0, V_1 of reduction maps

nodes.name: Snake lemma reduces to surjectivity of V_0 -> V_1
nodes.statement:
We will show that the map $V_0 	o V_1$ is surjective. This easily implies 
the desired conclusions about the maps $
u^n(R) 	o 
u^{n}(R/I)$ and
$\widetilde{
u}^n(R) 	o \widetilde{
u}^n(R/I)$ thanks to the snake lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Snake lemma reduces to surjectivity of V_0 -> V_1

nodes.name: Generators of V_1: forms with a factor in I
nodes.statement:
Consider a differential form 
$\omega = a dx_1 dx_2 \dots dx_n \in \Omega^n_R$ such that one of $\left\{a, x_1, \dots,
x_n\right\}$ belongs 
to $I$ (here $n = 0$ is allowed). The image of such a class in 
$\Omega^n_R/d \Omega_R^{n-1}$ belongs to $V_1$, and $V_1$ is generated by such
classes.
nodes.statement_short: Generators of V_1: forms with a factor in I

nodes.name: Solve u - u^p c = 1 via Lemma 4.30
nodes.statement:
For $u \in R$, 
we have $$(1 - C^{-1}) ( u  \omega)  = (u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1})
\omega.$$ Since $(R, I)$ is a henselian pair and $a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots
x_n^{p-1}\in I$, we can
choose 
$u \in R$ such that $u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1} = 1$,
using Lemma~\ref{solveeq:hens}.
nodes.statement_short: Solve u - u^p c = 1 via Lemma 4.30

nodes.name: u omega lifts omega
nodes.statement_short: u omega lifts omega

nodes.name: Fibers F and FF; they agree in degrees >= 0
nodes.statement:
Let $F$ be the fiber of the top horizontal map and let $\mathbb{F}$ be the fiber
of the bottom horizontal map. Note that the maps $K(R) \to \mathbb{K}(R), K(R/I)
\to \mathbb{K}(R/I)$, etc.\ are equivalences in degrees $ \geq 0$; thus, taking
fibers, the maps $K(R, I) \to \mathbb{K}(R, I)$ and $K(S, J) \to \mathbb{K}(S,
J)$ are equivalences in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Fibers F and FF; they agree in degrees >= 0

nodes.name: F -> FF equivalence in degrees >= 0
nodes.statement:
Taking fibers again, we find that the
map $F \to \mathbb{F}$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: F -> FF equivalence in degrees >= 0

nodes.name: Bass excision: FF is connective; suffices F connective
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, $\mathbb{F}$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq 0$ (even
$\geq 1$) by the
excision theorem of Bass and Bass--Heller--Swan, \cite[Thm.~XII.8.3]{Bass}.  Thus it suffices to show that $F$ is also concentrated in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bass excision: FF is connective; suffices F connective

nodes.name: Lemma 4.20 and K_1 surjectivity give F connective
nodes.statement:
But since $(R, I)$ and $(S, J)$ are henselian pairs, it follows by
Lemma~\ref{K0invhenspair} that the maps
$K_0(R) \to K_0(R/I), K_0(S) \to K_0(S/J)$ are isomorphisms and the maps
$K_1(R) \to K_1(R/I), K_1(S) \to K_1(S/J)$ (which are the abelianizations of
$GL_\infty(R) \to GL_\infty(R/I), GL_\infty(S) \to GL_\infty(S/J)$)  are surjections; thus $K(R, I)$ and
$K(S, J)$ are concentrated in degrees $\geq 1$, so that $F$ is concentrated in
degrees $\geq 0$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.20 and K_1 surjectivity give F connective

nodes.name: Reduce to (Z semidirect I, I) by excision
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{replaceexcision}, it suffices to consider the case where
$(R, I) = (\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I, I)$ where $I$ is a nonunital henselian ring.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to (Z semidirect I, I) by excision

nodes.name: F(I) = K^inv(Z semidirect I, I)/p is projectively pseudocoherent
nodes.statement:
We now consider the functor 
\[ F: \mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}} \to \mathrm{Sp}, \quad 
F(I) = K^{\mathrm{inv}}(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I, I)/p.
\]
By Propositions~\ref{Kpscoh} and \ref{TCpscoh}, $F$ is a projectively
pseudocoherent functor.  Implicit here is the statement
(due to Quillen) that the
$K$-groups of $\mathbb{Z}$ are finitely generated, as are the mod $p$ homotopy
groups of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{Z})$ (both of which follow from evaluating the projectively
pseudocoherent functors $I \mapsto K(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I), \mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{Z}
\ltimes I)/p$ at $I = 0$).
nodes.statement_short: F(I) = K^inv(Z semidirect I, I)/p is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Verify the hypotheses of Proposition 4.16
nodes.statement:
The assertion of the theorem is that $F=0$.  We will show this by checking that $F$ satisfies the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{pseudoargument}.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the hypotheses of Proposition 4.16

nodes.name: F is exact
nodes.statement:
First observe that $F$ sends a short exact sequence $I' \to I
\twoheadrightarrow \overline{I}$ of nonunital henselian rings to a fiber sequence of spectra. 
To see this, 
we consider the diagram
\[ \xymatrix{ F(I') \ar[d]^{\mathrm{id}}   \ar[r] & F(I) \ar[d]  \ar[r] &  F(\overline{I})
\ar[d]   \\
F(I') \ar[r] &  K^{\mathrm{inv}}( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)/p \ar[r] &  K^{\mathrm{inv}}( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes 
\overline{I})/p . }\]
Note that the right-hand square is homotopy cartesian, so the top row is a
fiber sequence if and only if the bottom row is a fiber sequence. But the bottom
row is a fiber sequence by Corollary~\ref{replaceexcision} applied to the
homomorphism $(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I',I')\rightarrow (\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I, I')$.
nodes.statement_short: F is exact

nodes.name: Comparison diagram
nodes.statement:
To see this, 
we consider the diagram
\[ \xymatrix{ F(I') \ar[d]^{\mathrm{id}}   \ar[r] & F(I) \ar[d]  \ar[r] &  F(\overline{I})
\ar[d]   \\
F(I') \ar[r] &  K^{\mathrm{inv}}( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)/p \ar[r] &  K^{\mathrm{inv}}( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes 
\overline{I})/p . }\]
nodes.statement_short: Comparison diagram

nodes.name: Reduce to bottom row
nodes.statement:
Note that the right-hand square is homotopy cartesian, so the top row is a
fiber sequence if and only if the bottom row is a fiber sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bottom row

nodes.name: Bottom row exact by Corollary 4.35
nodes.statement:
But the bottom
row is a fiber sequence by Corollary~\ref{replaceexcision} applied to the
homomorphism $(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I',I')\rightarrow (\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I, I')$.
nodes.statement_short: Bottom row exact by Corollary 4.35

nodes.name: Nilpotent I: F vanishes by Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy
nodes.statement:
Next, we claim that if $I'  \in
\mathrm{Ring}^{\mathrm{nu,h}}$ is nilpotent, then $F(I') = 0$. This follows from  
Theorem~\ref{DGMthm}
which shows that $K^{\mathrm{inv}}( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I', I') = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Nilpotent I: F vanishes by Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy

nodes.name: Reduce to henselizations k{x_1..x_n} over prime fields
nodes.statement:
To complete the proof, i.e., to verify the conditions of
Proposition~\ref{pseudoargument}, we need to check that 
\[ F( k\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+) = 0,  \]
whenever $k$ is a prime field. 
We write $k\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}$ for the henselization of the
polynomial ring $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ at $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, so
$k\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \subset k\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}$ is the maximal ideal. 
Using Corollary~\ref{replaceexcision}, it suffices to show that
the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(k\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(k)$ is an equivalence
modulo $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to henselizations k{x_1..x_n} over prime fields

nodes.name: Two cases by characteristic
nodes.statement:
There are two cases for this. 
If $\mathrm{char}(k) \neq p$, this follows from Gabber rigidity. 
If $\mathrm{char}(k) = p$, 
this follows from Proposition~\ref{rigidity:henspaircharp}.
nodes.statement_short: Two cases by characteristic

nodes.name: char k != p: Gabber rigidity
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{char}(k) \neq p$, this follows from Gabber rigidity.
nodes.statement_short: char k != p: Gabber rigidity

nodes.name: char k = p: Proposition 4.32
nodes.statement:
If $\mathrm{char}(k) = p$, 
this follows from Proposition~\ref{rigidity:henspaircharp}.
nodes.statement_short: char k = p: Proposition 4.32

nodes.name: p-completion commutes with the I-adic tower for noetherian R
nodes.statement: First we note that $\widehat R_p = \varprojlim_s \widehat{R/I^s}_p$ and $\widehat{R/I^s}_p = \widehat R_p /I^s\widehat R_p$.  Indeed, $R$ being noetherian, we have that on finitely generated $R$-modules the $p$-adic completion identifies with the derived $p$-completion. It therefore preserves short exact sequences and sequential inverse limits along surjective transition maps, as these are examples of derived limits.
nodes.statement_short: p-completion commutes with the I-adic tower for noetherian R

nodes.name: Dundas--Morrow continuity for the p-completion
nodes.statement:
In particular, $\widehat R_p$ is $I\widehat
R_p$-adically complete. Therefore, the canonical map
\[ \mathrm{THH}(\widehat{R}_p)/p \longrightarrow \varprojlim_s \mathrm{THH}( \widehat{R}_p/I^s
\widehat{R}_p)/p\] is an equivalence by \cite[Thm.~4.5]{DundasMorrow}.
nodes.statement_short: Dundas--Morrow continuity for the p-completion

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 transfers back to R and R/I^s
nodes.statement:
But by the above, each quotient $\widehat R_p/I^s\widehat
R_p$ coincides with the $p$-adic completion of $R/I^s$, so that applying
Lemma~\ref{modplemma} to $R$ and to each $R/I^s $ completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.3 transfers back to R and R/I^s

nodes.name: Reduce to Milnor K_2 mod p
nodes.statement:
We begin with several straightforward reductions to Milnor $K$-theory. Firstly,
since $k[[t]]^\times$ is $p$-torsion-free, the canonical map $K_2(k[[t]])/p\to
\pi_2 (K(k[[t]])/p)$ is an isomorphism. The $p$-torsion in the
pro abelian group $\{k[t]/(t^s)^\times\}_s$ is also zero, since the transition
map $k[t]/(t^{ps})^\times\to k[t]/(t^s)^\times$ clearly kills all $p$-torsion in
the domain, and therefore $\{K_2(k[t]/(t^s))/p\}_s\to
\{\pi_2(K(k[t]/(t^s))/p) \}_s$ is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups. Secondly, $k[[t]]$ and
$k[t]/(t^s)$ are local rings with infinite residue field, whence a classical
result in algebraic $K$-theory \cite[\S8]{vanderKallen1977} states that  $K_2^M(k[[t]])\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} K_2(k[[t]])$
and $K_2^M(k[t]/(t^s))\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} K_2(k[t]/(t^s))$. Finally, the
canonical map $\pi_2 (\varprojlim_s K(k[t]/(t^s))/p)\to \varprojlim_s\pi_2(
K(k[t]/(t^s))/p)$ is surjective, by the Milnor sequence. In conclusion, to prove the theorem it is sufficient to show that the canonical map $K_2^M(k[[t]])/p\to\varprojlim_sK_2^M(k[t]/(t^s))/p$ is not surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Milnor K_2 mod p

nodes.name: K_2/p computes pi_2(K/p) for k[[t]]
nodes.statement:
Firstly,
since $k[[t]]^\times$ is $p$-torsion-free, the canonical map $K_2(k[[t]])/p\to
\pi_2 (K(k[[t]])/p)$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: K_2/p computes pi_2(K/p) for k[[t]]

nodes.name: Same for the pro system k[t]/t^s
nodes.statement:
The $p$-torsion in the
pro abelian group $\{k[t]/(t^s)^\times\}_s$ is also zero, since the transition
map $k[t]/(t^{ps})^\times\to k[t]/(t^s)^\times$ clearly kills all $p$-torsion in
the domain, and therefore $\{K_2(k[t]/(t^s))/p\}_s\to
\{\pi_2(K(k[t]/(t^s))/p) \}_s$ is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups.
nodes.statement_short: Same for the pro system k[t]/t^s

nodes.name: Milnor K_2 equals K_2 for local rings with infinite residue field
nodes.statement:
Secondly, $k[[t]]$ and
$k[t]/(t^s)$ are local rings with infinite residue field, whence a classical
result in algebraic $K$-theory \cite[\S8]{vanderKallen1977} states that  $K_2^M(k[[t]])\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} K_2(k[[t]])$
and $K_2^M(k[t]/(t^s))\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} K_2(k[t]/(t^s))$.
nodes.statement_short: Milnor K_2 equals K_2 for local rings with infinite residue field

nodes.name: Milnor sequence surjectivity
nodes.statement:
Finally, the
canonical map $\pi_2 (\varprojlim_s K(k[t]/(t^s))/p)\to \varprojlim_s\pi_2(
K(k[t]/(t^s))/p)$ is surjective, by the Milnor sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Milnor sequence surjectivity

nodes.name: Suffices: Milnor K_2 map not surjective
nodes.statement: In conclusion, to prove the theorem it is sufficient to show that the canonical map $K_2^M(k[[t]])/p\to\varprojlim_sK_2^M(k[t]/(t^s))/p$ is not surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: Milnor K_2 map not surjective

nodes.name: Detect symbols via dlog into Kahler 2-forms
nodes.statement_short: Detect symbols via dlog into Kahler 2-forms

nodes.name: Weight of 2-forms; p-basis elements have large weight
nodes.statement:
We now closely follow Bloch--Esnault--Kerz, with the necessary modifications to deal with the fact that we will eventually need to restrict to dlog forms. Given any map of rings $R\to S$ and differential form $\tau\in\Omega^2_{S/R}$, define its {\em weight} $w(\tau)$ to be the smallest integer $n$ for which it is possible to write $\tau=\sum_{i=1}^na_idb_i\wedge dc_i$ for some $a_i,b_i,c_i\in S$. 
If $\ell$ is a subfield of $k$ and $b_1,\dots,b_n,c_1,\dots,c_n\in k$ form part
of a $p$-basis for $k$ relative to $\ell$, then the elements $d b_1,\dots,d
b_n,d c_1,\dots,d c_n$ are linearly independent in the $k$-vector space
$\Omega^1_{k/\ell}$ and so this element $\sum_{i=1}^ndb_i\wedge dc_i$ has weight
$\ge n$ in $\Omega^2_{k/\ell}$ (Lemma~\ref{linalg} below).
nodes.statement_short: Weight of 2-forms; p-basis elements have large weight

nodes.name: Map e to t-adic coefficients; image of Omega^2_{k[[t]]} has bounded weight growt
nodes.statement:
Next consider the derivation
$$k[t]/(t^s) \rightarrow \Omega^1_k \otimes_k k[t]/(t^s)$$
which ``holds $t$ constant", so $\sum_n c_n t^n \mapsto \sum_n (dc_n)t^n$.  This extends by multiplicativity to a map
$$\Omega^\ast_{k[t]/(t^s)}\rightarrow \Omega^\ast_k \otimes_k k[t]/(t^s)$$
which splits the canonical map $\Omega^\ast_k\otimes_k k[t]/(t^s)\rightarrow
\Omega^\ast_{k[t]/(t^s)}$.   Restricting to degree $\ast=2$ and passing to the
limit as $s\to\infty$ defines \[e:\varprojlim_s\Omega^2_{k[t]/(t^s)}\longrightarrow
\varprojlim_s\Omega^2_k\otimes_kk[t]/(t^s),\] where each element on the right
may be expressed as $\sum_{j\ge 0}\tau_i t^i$ for some unique
$\tau_0,\tau_1,\dots\in \Omega^2_k$ (the {\em $t$-adic coefficients} of the
element). Bloch--Esnault--Kerz \cite[Lem.~B2]{BlochEsnaultKerz2013} show
(assuming $k = \mathbb{C}$, but the argument works in general) that the image of the composition \[\Omega^2_{k[[t]]}\longrightarrow \varprojlim_s\Omega^2_{k[t]/(t^s)}\longrightarrow \varprojlim_s\Omega^2_k\otimes_kk[t]/(t^s)\] lands inside the set of those elements $\sum_{j\ge 0}\tau_j t^j$ whose $t$-adic coefficients satisfy the following: there exists $N\ge0$ such that $w(\tau_j)\le N\binom{j+2}j$ for all $j\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: Map e to t-adic coefficients; image of Omega^2_{k[[t]]} has bounded weight growth

nodes.name: Construct compatible symbols f_s from relative p-bases
nodes.statement: We are now prepared to complete the proof by constructing a bad element of $\varprojlim_s K_2^M(k[t]/(t^s))/p$. First pick a sequence $0<w_1<w_2<\cdots$ of integers growing sufficiently fast such that no value of $N$ satisfies $w_j\le N\binom{2j}{2j-2}$ for all $j\ge1$. Then pick a sequence of subfields $\mathbb F_p=k_0\subset k_1\subset k_2\subset\cdots$ of $k$ such that any $p$-basis for $k_j$ relative to $k_{j-1}$ has $\ge2w_j$ elements; let $b_1^{(j)},\cdots,b_{w_j}^{(j)},c_1^{(j)},\cdots,c_{w_j}^{(j)}\in k_i$ be part of such a relative $p$-basis. Set \[f_s:=\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}\sum_{i=1}^{w_j}\{1+t^jb_i^{(j)},1+t^jc_i^{(j)}\}\in K_2^M(k[t]/(t^{s}))/p\] and note that the transition map $K_2^M(k[t]/(t^{s}))/p\to K_2^M(k[t]/(t^{s-1}))/p$ exactly kills the $j=s-1$ part of the sum and therefore sends $f_s$ to $f_{s-1}$; we therefore may define $f:=\varprojlim_s f_s\in\varprojlim_sK_2^M(k[t]/(t^{s}))/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct compatible symbols f_s from relative p-bases

nodes.name: Weights of coefficients of dlog f grow too fast: no lift
nodes.statement_short: Weights of coefficients of dlog f grow too fast: no lift

nodes.name: Interior product gives f_omega: V^dual -> V
nodes.statement:
Recall that we have an \emph{interior product} $V^{\vee} \otimes \bigwedge^2 V
\to V$ given  by $v \otimes (x \wedge y) \mapsto \left \langle v,
x\right\rangle y - \left \langle v, y\right\rangle x$. 
Given $\omega \in \bigwedge^2 V$, we obtain a map $f_\omega: V^{\vee} \to V$.
nodes.statement_short: Interior product gives f_omega: V^dual -> V

nodes.name: Weight w bounds rank by 2w
nodes.statement: If $\omega$ has weight $w$, then the rank of $f_{\omega}$ is at most $2w$.
nodes.statement_short: Weight w bounds rank by 2w

nodes.name: Rank of f_{omega_0} is 2n
nodes.statement:
Completing $\left\{u_1,\dots, u_n, v_1, \dots, v_n\right\}$ to a basis of $V$
and forming the dual basis, 
one now sees that the rank of $f_{\omega_0}$ for $\omega_0 = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i
\wedge v_i$ is $2n$; together, this implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Rank of f_{omega_0} is 2n

nodes.name: Forward direction from Mathew
nodes.statement:
It follows from \cite[Lemma 3.11]{Mthick} that if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is
quickly converging, then the towers of homotopy groups are 
quickly converging. 
Indeed, if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent or constant, then the tower of
homotopy groups is clearly quickly converging, and the referenced result shows
that the condition on homotopy groups is stable in cofiber sequences of towers.
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction from Mathew

nodes.name: Devissage to one degree; use generation by constant and nilpotent towers
nodes.statement:
For the converse direction, a d\'evissage reduces to the
case where $a= b$. In this case, it follows from the paragraph following 
Definition~\ref{quickconvab}: that is, quickly convergent towers of abelian
groups are built up from constant and nilpotent towers.
nodes.statement_short: Devissage to one degree; use generation by constant and nilpotent towers

nodes.name: Truncation of tensor depends on truncation of factor
nodes.statement:
Note that $\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i) \simeq \tau_{\leq m} ( \tau_{\leq m}
X_i \otimes Y_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Truncation of tensor depends on truncation of factor

nodes.name: Nilpotent factor gives nilpotent tensor
nodes.statement:
So if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, then so is 
$\left\{\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i)\right\}$, and the limit is zero.  Symmetrically, we get the same if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}Y_i\right\}$ is nilpotent.
nodes.statement_short: Nilpotent factor gives nilpotent tensor

nodes.name: Constant factors give constant tensor
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} Y_i\right\}$ are both constant, we see that $\tau_{\leq m} (X_i\otimes Y_i)$ is constant, and the map from $X\otimes Y$ to the limit is an isomorphism degrees $\leq m-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Constant factors give constant tensor

nodes.name: Thick subcategory argument
nodes.statement: A thick subcategory argument lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Thick subcategory argument

nodes.name: Mod p condition can be tested with S^0/p tensor S^0/p
nodes.statement: Note that a tower is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ if and only if it is almost quickly converging after smashing with $X$, for any choice of spectrum $X$ generating the same thick subcategory as $S^0/p$.  For example one can take $X=S^0/p\otimes S^0/p$.\footnote{This is the cone of multiplcation by $p$ on $S^0/p$, hence lies in the thick subcategory generated by $S^0/p$.  For the converse, note that $p^2$ kills $S^0/p$, so $S^0/p$ is a retract of $(S^0/p \otimes S^0/p)/p$.}
nodes.statement_short: Mod p condition can be tested with S^0/p tensor S^0/p

nodes.name: Tensor powers via Lemma 5.18
nodes.statement: Keeping this in mind, an inductive application of Lemma \ref{transfernilp} shows that $\left\{(HR_i)^{\otimes n}\right\}_i$ is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ for any $n\geq 0$, and has mod~$p$ limit $(HR)^{\otimes n}/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Tensor powers via Lemma 5.18

nodes.name: THH via Lemma 5.16
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma \ref{simplicialalmostquickconv} we deduce that $\left\{\mathrm{THH}(R_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with limit $\mathrm{THH}(R)/p$.
nodes.statement_short: THH via Lemma 5.16

nodes.name: TC via Lemma 5.17
nodes.statement: From this, Lemma \ref{TCalmostquickconv} lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: TC via Lemma 5.17

nodes.name: Fiber tower Sigma H(R[p^i]) with transition maps p
nodes.statement:
The map of towers $\{HR\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}\}\rightarrow
\{H(R/p^iR)\}$ has fiber $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ with transition maps multiplication by
$p$.
nodes.statement_short: Fiber tower Sigma H(R[p^i]) with transition maps p

nodes.name: Bounded torsion: fiber tower almost nilpotent mod p
nodes.statement:
Because of the bounded $p$-power torsion hypothesis, this tower
$\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ is almost nilpotent modulo $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded torsion: fiber tower almost nilpotent mod p

nodes.name: Argue as in Theorems 5.20 and 5.21
nodes.statement:
So we deduce $p$-adic
continuity for $\mathrm{TC}$ as in Proposition \ref{TCderpcontinuous}, and then $p$-adic
continuity for $K$-theory as in Proposition \ref{derivedpadiccont}.
nodes.statement_short: Argue as in Theorems 5.20 and 5.21

nodes.name: Combine the main theorem with relative TC calculations
nodes.statement:
Indeed, this follows from our main result (which identifies the relative
$K$-theory with relative $\mathrm{TC}$), 
together with the Geisser--Hesselholt calculations of relative $\mathrm{TC}$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the main theorem with relative TC calculations

nodes.name: Geisser--Hesselholt sequence for TC/p
nodes.statement:
We have
the short exact sequence
\[  0 \to \widetilde{\nu}^{n+1}(R) \to \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)  \to \nu^n(R) \to 0 
\]
as in Theorem~\ref{GHGL} (see also \eqref{thisdiag}).
nodes.statement_short: Geisser--Hesselholt sequence for TC/p

nodes.name: Rigidity of nu~ gives the claim
nodes.statement: Using Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}, the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Rigidity of nu~ gives the claim

nodes.name: Complete F-finite case is Morrow; reduce to it
nodes.statement:
If $R$ is $F$-finite, noetherian, and $I$-adically complete then this was proved
in \cite[Prop.~2.20]{Morrow-HW}, and we will reduce the general case to this
one.
nodes.statement_short: Complete F-finite case is Morrow; reduce to it

nodes.name: Reduce to henselizations of finite type algebras
nodes.statement:
Firstly, by taking a filtered colimit we may suppose that $R$ is the
henselization of a finite type $\mathbb F_p$-algebra along some ideal, and in
particular that $R$ is $F$-finite and excellent \cite[Tag 07QS]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to henselizations of finite type algebras

nodes.name: Neron--Popescu: completion is ind-smooth
nodes.statement: Then the $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is geometrically regular over $R$ by \cite[7.8.3(v)]{EGA_IV_2}, whence it is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras $A$ by N\'eron--Popescu.
nodes.statement_short: Neron--Popescu: completion is ind-smooth

nodes.name: Split injections give injective cokernel map
nodes.statement:
But each structure map $R\to A$ admits a splitting
as in Remark~\ref{henspairequivtocontinuity}. 
Therefore, taking a filtered colimit shows that \[\operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)})\] is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Split injections give injective cokernel map

nodes.name: Right side vanishes by the complete case
nodes.statement: Since the right side vanishes by the first sentence of the paragraph, the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Right side vanishes by the complete case

nodes.name: Etale sheaves W_r Omega on X and Y_s
nodes.statement: We will need to argue via the \'etale topology, so we begin by introducing the necessary sheaves. Let $X:=\mathrm{Spec} R$, with closed subschemes $Y_s:=\mathrm{Spec} R/I^s$ for $s\ge1$; let $W_r\Omega^n_X$, $W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s)}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_X\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s})$ be the corresponding \'etale sheaves on $X$. As explained in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, these sheaves have no higher \'etale cohomology (since $X$ is affine) and their global sections are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_R$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Etale sheaves W_r Omega on X and Y_s

nodes.name: Log subsheaves and relative log sheaves
nodes.statement: Next let $W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ be the image in the \'etale topology of $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,X}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{X}^n$, and similarly for each $Y_s$, and set $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}})$. As we already mentioned in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, the subgroup of dlog forms may be defined using either the Zariski or \'etale topology by \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}, and therefore the global sections of these sheaves are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Log subsheaves and relative log sheaves

nodes.name: Relative log sheaves have pro-zero H^1
nodes.statement:
We claim that $\{H^1_\sub{\'et}(X,W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}})\}_r=0$ for
each $s\ge 1$. After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian
ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$. Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective:
\[\xymatrix{
0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0
}\]
Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms
\begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0 \end{equation} Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}.
nodes.statement_short: Relative log sheaves have pro-zero H^1

nodes.name: Reduce to s = 1 using Remark 3.14
nodes.statement:
After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian
ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to s = 1 using Remark 3.14

nodes.name: R - F sequence for relative terms; surjectivity on global sections by Lemma 5.29
nodes.statement:
Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective:
\[\xymatrix{
0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0
}\]
Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms
\begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0 \end{equation} Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}.
nodes.statement_short: R - F sequence for relative terms; surjectivity on global sections by Lemma 5.29

nodes.name: Relative form of Illusie's sequence; global sections exact since H^1 vanishes
nodes.statement:
Finally, appealing to Illusie's result recalled immediately before the lemma (which has been extended to arbitrary regular $\mathbb F_p$-schemes by A.~Shiho \cite[Cor.~2.13]{Shiho2007}) and to an analogous pro version for the formal completion of $X$ along along $Y_1$ \cite[Cor.~4.8]{Morrow-HW} gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are again surjective:
\[\xymatrix{
0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}\ar[d]&\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\ar[d]&W_{r}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\
0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}&\{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}&\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]&0
}\]
Taking kernels gives a short exact sequence of relative terms
\[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow0.\] Taking global sections completes the proof since the previous paragraph showed that the left term has no $H^1_\sub{\'et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative form of Illusie's sequence; global sections exact since H^1 vanishes

nodes.name: Witt complex maps lambda: W_s Omega -> TR^s
nodes.statement:
The proof is similar to the techniques of \cite[\S5.1]{Morrow-HW}, but we repeat
the necessary details here. In particular, we begin with the same recollections
on Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg theorems for the spectra $\mathrm{TR}^s$. If $R$ is
any $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, then the pro graded ring $\{\mathrm{TR}^s_*(R;p)\}_s$ is a
$p$-typical Witt complex with respect to its operators $F,V,R$; by universality
of the de Rham--Witt complex, there are therefore natural maps of graded $W_s(R)$-algebras \cite[Prop.~1.5.8]{Hesselholt} $\lambda_{s,R}:W_s\Omega_R^*\to \mathrm{TR}_*^s(R;p)$ for $s\ge0$, which are compatible with the Frobenius,  Verschiebung, and Restriction maps (in other words, a morphism of $p$-typical Witt complexes).
nodes.statement_short: Witt complex maps lambda: W_s Omega -> TR^s

nodes.name: HKR and pro HKR identify relative TR with relative de Rham--Witt
nodes.statement:
From now on in the proof assume that $R$ is regular, noetherian, and $F$-finite, and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. Hesselholt's HKR theorem \cite[Thm.~B]{Hesselholt} implies that the resulting map of pro abelian groups \[\lambda_R:\{W_s\Omega_R^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R;p)\}_s\] is an isomorphism for each $n\ge 1$; similarly, the pro HKR theorem of Dundas--Morrow \cite[Cor.~4.15]{DundasMorrow} implies that \[\lambda_{R/I^\infty}: \{W_s\Omega_{R/I^s}^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s \tag{pro-HKR}\] is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups for each $n\ge0$. Since $W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_s\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$ is surjective for all $s,n\ge0$, it follows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exact sequences and there are therefore natural induced isomorphisms of relative theories
\[\{W_s\Omega_{(R,I^s)}^n\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\] for all $n\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: HKR and pro HKR identify relative TR with relative de Rham--Witt

nodes.name: Lemma 5.29 identifies relative TC^s with relative log forms; Lemma 5.30 for p^r
nodes.statement:
Now assume that $R$ is henselian along $I$. By Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}, the map
$R-F:W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$ is surjective for all
$n,s\ge0$, and therefore the previous isomorphism shows that the long exact
sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to
\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\xrightarrow{R-F}\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exacts and
thereby induces natural isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;p)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to}
\{\ker(W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)})\}_s\] The
right side of the previous line is precisely
$\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by applying \cite[Cor. 
4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} to $R$ and $R/I^s$ for each $s\ge1$ (in fact, we have
already made this argument: just take global sections in line
(\ref{equation_R-F}) for each $Y_s$ and then pass to the resulting diagonal of
the $\mathbb N^2$-indexed pro abelian group); moreover, this latter pro abelian
group is $p$-torsion-free by the injectivity in Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2} (this is
anyway easy: the pro abelian group is contained in $\{W_s\Omega^n_R\}_s$, which
is $p$-torsion-free thanks to the equality of the $p$- and canonical-filtrations
on the de Rham--Witt groups of any regular $\mathbb F_p$-algebra: see
\cite[Prop.~I.3.2 \& I.3.4]{illusie-derham-witt} for the case of a smooth algebra over a perfect field, then apply N\'eron--Popescu), so passing to finite coefficients gives us isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}/p^r\}_s\] for each fixed $r\ge1$. The right side is $\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by (the hard part of) Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.29 identifies relative TC^s with relative log forms; Lemma 5.30 for p^r

nodes.name: Pro-constancy and the main theorem pass to K
nodes.statement: Finally, pro-constancy of $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(-;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ (Proposition \ref{prop_pro_constant}) implies that the left side of the previous line is $\{\mathrm{TC}_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$, which by Theorem \ref{mainthm} identifies with $\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ via the trace map.
nodes.statement_short: Pro-constancy and the main theorem pass to K

nodes.name: Reduce to henselian local R and combine Theorem 5.31 with Geisser--Levine
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be as in the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}. Without loss of generality $R$ is henselian along $I$, whence $R$ is also local, and so the result follows by combining Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL_relative} with the isomorphism $K_n(R; \mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ of Geisser--Levine \cite{GL}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to henselian local R and combine Theorem 5.31 with Geisser--Levine

nodes.name: Compatibility via dlog on symbols
nodes.statement: Note that the two results are compatible since the trace map is given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols by \cite[Lem.~4.2.3 \& Cor.~6.4.1]{GH}.
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility via dlog on symbols

nodes.name: p-torsion-freeness deferred to Corollary 5.33
nodes.statement: We establish the $p$-torsion-freeness of $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ in the next corollary.
nodes.statement_short: p-torsion-freeness deferred to Corollary 5.33

nodes.name: Reduce to local R
nodes.statement: We can replace $R$ by its $I$-adic completion and thereby assume $R$ itself is local.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to local R

nodes.name: Part (1) from the diagram of Theorem 5.26
nodes.statement_short: Part (1) from the diagram of Theorem 5.26

nodes.name: Part (2): surjectivity mod p gives torsion-freeness
nodes.statement:
Part (1) clearly implies that $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s\to \{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)\}_s$
is surjective, whence the usual exact sequence implies it is an isomorphism and that $\{K_{n-1}(R/I^s)[p]\}_s=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (2): surjectivity mod p gives torsion-freeness

nodes.name: Symbolic pro K-groups and lifting units split the relative sequence
nodes.statement: As we have just seen in Corollary \ref{corollary_Milnor}, $\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is entirely symbolic; since $R\to R/I$ is surjective on units (using the assumption $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$), we deduce that $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\to \{K_n(R/I^s;p^r\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is surjective for all $n\ge0$. Therefore the long exact relative sequences breaks into the desired short exact sequences.
nodes.statement_short: Symbolic pro K-groups and lifting units split the relative sequence

nodes.name: Part (2) unravels pro surjectivity
nodes.statement: Part (2) is a consequence of the surjectivity arguments of the previous paragraph, unravelling what it means for a map of pro abelian groups to be surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Part (2) unravels pro surjectivity

nodes.name: Reduce to a separably closed field by the main theorem
nodes.statement:
By
Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we may assume that $R=k$ is a field itself, which is
then separably closed. 
Thus we need to show that if $k$ is a separably closed field of characteristic
$p > 0$, then the map $K(k) \to \mathrm{TC}(k)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a separably closed field by the main theorem

nodes.name: Suffices nu~^n(k) = 0 by Theorem 4.29
nodes.statement:
As $\mathbb{F}_p$ is perfect, $k$ is an ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra (e.g., choose
a transcendence basis for $k$).  Thus it suffices to show that the terms
$\widetilde{\nu}^n(k)$ vanish by Theorem~\ref{GHGL}. 
That is, we need to show that the map
\[ 1  - C^{-1}: \Omega^n_k \to \Omega^n_k/ d \Omega^{n-1}_k  \]
is surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices nu~^n(k) = 0 by Theorem 4.29

nodes.name: (1 - C^{-1})(u omega) formula
nodes.statement:
Given a form $\omega = a dx_1 \dots dx_n \in \Omega^n_k$, we have
$(1 - C^{-1})(u \omega) = (u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1}) \omega$.
nodes.statement_short: (1 - C^{-1})(u omega) formula

nodes.name: Solve separable equation in k
nodes.statement:
Since $k$ is separably closed, 
we can solve the equation $
u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1} = 1$ in $k$. This implies that $1 -
C^{-1}$ is surjective as desired and completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Solve separable equation in k

nodes.name: Suslin's key claim: pullbacks of a class along sections agree
nodes.statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field. 
The crux of Suslin's argument is to show that if
$q:X\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k)$ is a connected smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type, then
  for any class $\alpha \in F(X)$ and section $x: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$, the
 pullback $x^* \alpha \in F(k)$ is independent of the choice of $x$. 
It suffices to fix a section $x_0: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$,  
 and show (by connectedness, in view of the Zariski density of $k$-points in
 $X$, cf., e.g.,  \cite[Tag 04QM]{stacks-project}) that there exists a Zariski neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$ such that
 $x_0^\ast\alpha = x^\ast\alpha$ for all sections $x:\mathrm{Spec}(k)\rightarrow U$.
 Replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha-q^\ast x_0^\ast \alpha$, we can assume
 $x^\ast\alpha=0$.  Then by the assumption of rigidity,
 applied to the henselization of $X$ at $x_0$, and the commutation of $F$ with
 filtered colimits, we deduce that there is an \'etale neighborhood $Y\rightarrow
 X$ of $x_0$ such that $\alpha$ pulls back to $0$ on $Y$.  Then we can take $U$ to be the image of $Y\rightarrow X$: as $k$ is separably closed, every $k$-point of $U$ lifts to $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Suslin's key claim: pullbacks of a class along sections agree

nodes.name: Reduce to a Zariski neighborhood of x_0
nodes.statement:
It suffices to fix a section $x_0: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$,  
 and show (by connectedness, in view of the Zariski density of $k$-points in
 $X$, cf., e.g.,  \cite[Tag 04QM]{stacks-project}) that there exists a Zariski neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$ such that
 $x_0^\ast\alpha = x^\ast\alpha$ for all sections $x:\mathrm{Spec}(k)\rightarrow U$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a Zariski neighborhood of x_0

nodes.name: Assume x_0^* alpha = 0
nodes.statement:
Replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha-q^\ast x_0^\ast \alpha$, we can assume
 $x^\ast\alpha=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume x_0^* alpha = 0

nodes.name: Rigidity at the henselization gives an etale neighborhood killing alpha
nodes.statement:
Then by the assumption of rigidity,
 applied to the henselization of $X$ at $x_0$, and the commutation of $F$ with
 filtered colimits, we deduce that there is an \'etale neighborhood $Y\rightarrow
 X$ of $x_0$ such that $\alpha$ pulls back to $0$ on $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Rigidity at the henselization gives an etale neighborhood killing alpha

nodes.name: k-points of U lift to Y
nodes.statement: Then we can take $U$ to be the image of $Y\rightarrow X$: as $k$ is separably closed, every $k$-point of $U$ lifts to $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: k-points of U lift to Y

nodes.name: Injectivity
nodes.statement:
Now we prove the proposition. 
It suffices to consider the case where $K$ is the separable closure of a prime
field, and so is in particular perfect. 
Therefore, the extension $K \to L$ is ind-smooth, i.e., $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth
$K$-algebras $A_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ running over a filtered poset.  Then each map $K \to A_\alpha$ admits
a retraction, as $K$ is separably closed. 
It follows that $F(K) \to F(A_\alpha)$ is injective for each $\alpha$, so that
$F(K) \to F(L)$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity

nodes.name: Reduce to K separable closure of a prime field
nodes.statement:
It suffices to consider the case where $K$ is the separable closure of a prime
field, and so is in particular perfect.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to K separable closure of a prime field

nodes.name: L is a filtered colimit of smooth A_alpha
nodes.statement:
Therefore, the extension $K \to L$ is ind-smooth, i.e., $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth
$K$-algebras $A_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ running over a filtered poset.
nodes.statement_short: L is a filtered colimit of smooth A_alpha

nodes.name: Retractions exist since K separably closed
nodes.statement:
Then each map $K \to A_\alpha$ admits
a retraction, as $K$ is separably closed.
nodes.statement_short: Retractions exist since K separably closed

nodes.name: F(K) -> F(L) injective
nodes.statement:
It follows that $F(K) \to F(A_\alpha)$ is injective for each $\alpha$, so that
$F(K) \to F(L)$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: F(K) -> F(L) injective

nodes.name: Surjectivity
nodes.statement:
We now argue surjectivity. Let $u \in F(A_\alpha)$; we show that  the image of
$u$ in $F(L)$ belongs to the
image of $F(K)$.  Passing to a component if necessary, we can assume $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha)$ is connected.  Then $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha\otimes_K L)$ is connected as well, since $K$ is algebraically closed.  Now consider the two maps
\[ f_1, f_2:A_\alpha   \rightrightarrows L,  \]
where the first map is the colimit structure map and where
where the second map is $A_\alpha \stackrel{s}{\to} K \to L$. 
By the first paragraph of the argument applied to the $L$-algebra $A_\alpha
\otimes_K L$, we conclude that these two maps have the same effect on $u$, verifying the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Surjectivity

nodes.name: Fix u in F(A_alpha) with Spec A_alpha connected
nodes.statement:
Let $u \in F(A_\alpha)$; we show that  the image of
$u$ in $F(L)$ belongs to the
image of $F(K)$.  Passing to a component if necessary, we can assume $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha)$ is connected.  Then $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha\otimes_K L)$ is connected as well, since $K$ is algebraically closed.
nodes.statement_short: Fix u in F(A_alpha) with Spec A_alpha connected

nodes.name: Two maps A_alpha -> L
nodes.statement:
Now consider the two maps
\[ f_1, f_2:A_\alpha   \rightrightarrows L,  \]
where the first map is the colimit structure map and where
where the second map is $A_\alpha \stackrel{s}{\to} K \to L$.
nodes.statement_short: Two maps A_alpha -> L

nodes.name: Both maps agree on u
nodes.statement:
By the first paragraph of the argument applied to the $L$-algebra $A_\alpha
\otimes_K L$, we conclude that these two maps have the same effect on $u$, verifying the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Both maps agree on u

nodes.name: Trace induces the comparison since TC/p is an etale Postnikov sheaf
nodes.statement:
The comparison map is induced by the cyclotomic trace, given that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ is an \'etale Postnikov sheaf (see \cite[Thm 5.16]{CM18} in full generality; for
affines, see \cite[Sec.~3]{GH}; in the semi-separated case see \cite{BMloc} for
the conclusion of Nisnevich descent).
nodes.statement_short: Trace induces the comparison since TC/p is an etale Postnikov sheaf

nodes.name: Proper and affine proper base change reduce to the special fiber
nodes.statement:
Now assume $X$ is proper over $\mathrm{Spec}(R)$
henselian along $(p)$. Then the proper base change theorem together with
Gabber's affine analog of the proper base change theorem
\cite{Gabberaffine} combine to show $H^j_\sub{\'et}(X, \mathcal{F})\simeq
H^j_\sub{\'et}(X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR), i^*\mathcal{F})$
for all torsion abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_{et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proper and affine proper base change reduce to the special fiber

nodes.name: Finite cohomological dimension; compare homotopy sheaves
nodes.statement:
In particular,
$X_{et}$ has finite $p$-cohomological dimension by induction on an affine cover and the following Lemma~\ref{finiteetale}, so by comparing descent spectral sequences for $\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)$ and $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ it suffices to show that $\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ and $\pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$ have the same cohomology on $X_\sub{\'et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Finite cohomological dimension; compare homotopy sheaves

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaves agree on the special fiber
nodes.statement: But by the same base change results, this follows from the fact (see above) that they have the same restriction to $X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR)$.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy sheaves agree on the special fiber

nodes.name: Pullbacks preserve equivalences in degrees >= d
nodes.statement:
We use throughout the following basic observation: if $T \to T'$ is a map of
spectra which is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$, then for any spectrum $T''$
with a map $T'' \to T'$, the map $T \times_{T'} T'' \to T''$ is an equivalence
in degrees $\geq d$.
nodes.statement_short: Pullbacks preserve equivalences in degrees >= d

nodes.name: Reduce to F_p-algebras via the main theorem
nodes.statement:
Using the pullback square from Theorem~\ref{mainthm}
(involving the spectra $K(R)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r, K(R/p)/p^r,
\mathrm{TC}(R/p)/p^r$), we reduce to the case where $R$ is an
$\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. 
It now suffices to see that $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence
in degrees $\geq d$. 


Note also that the result is clearly equivalent if we replace $K(R)/p$ with
$\mathbb{K}(R)/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to F_p-algebras via the main theorem

nodes.name: Nisnevich descent for K and TC
nodes.statement:
By the theorems of Thomason--Trobaugh \cite{TT90} and
Blumberg--Mandell \cite{BMloc} respectively, 
$\mathbb{K}(-)/p^r$ and $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ 
are Nisnevich sheaves 
on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ with 
values in the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sp}$.
nodes.statement_short: Nisnevich descent for K and TC

nodes.name: Finite homotopy dimension: descent spectral sequence converges
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Th.~3.17]{CM18}, the finiteness of Krull dimension implies that
the Nisnevich topos of $\mathrm{Spec} R$ has \emph{finite homotopy dimension}  in the sense of \cite[Def. 7.2.2.1]{HTT}.
In the case where $R$ is noetherian, the finiteness of homotopy dimension
appears in \cite[Thm.~3.7.7.1]{SAG}. 
As a consequence, Postnikov towers in the $\infty$-category of Nisnevich sheaves of
spectra on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ are convergent and one has a descent spectral sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Finite homotopy dimension: descent spectral sequence converges

nodes.name: Reduce to henselian local stalks A
nodes.statement:
Therefore, it suffices to see that 
the maps on stalks induce isomorphisms in degrees $\geq d$. 
The maps on stalks are 
\[  \mathbb{K}(A)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p^r,  \]
as $A$ ranges over the connected finite \'etale algebras over henselizations of $R$ at prime ideals.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to henselian local stalks A

nodes.name: Main theorem reduces stalks to residue fields; p-bases bound degrees
nodes.statement:
Since the map $K(A)/p \to \mathbb{K}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq
1$, 
it suffices to see that $K(A)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p$ is an 
equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for each such $A$. This in turn follows from the fiber square 
of Theorem~\ref{mainthm}  (applied to the henselian local ring $A$) 
and the fact that if $k$ is a field of characteristic $p$, then the map $K(k)/p^r
\to \mathrm{TC}(k)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq \log_p [k: k^p]$ (which
follows from Theorem~\ref{GHGL} and the theory of $p$-bases, which implies $\dim
\Omega^1_k \leq d$ and so $\Omega^n_k  = 0$ for $n > d$ \cite[Thm.~26.5]{Matsumura}). 
Note also that the invariant $\log_p [k:k^p] = \dim \Omega^1_k$ is invariant under finite
separable extensions of fields of characteristic $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem reduces stalks to residue fields; p-bases bound degrees

nodes.name: Reduce to semiperfect F_p-algebras
nodes.statement:
Using Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we immediately reduce to the case where $R$ itself is a
semiperfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to semiperfect F_p-algebras

nodes.name: Nilradical gives a henselian pair with perfect quotient
nodes.statement:
In this case, let $I \subset R$ be the nilradical. It follows that $R/I$ is
perfect and that $I$ is locally nilpotent, so that $(R, I)$ is a henselian pair.
nodes.statement_short: Nilradical gives a henselian pair with perfect quotient

nodes.name: Main theorem plus perfect case
nodes.statement:
By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} and Example~\ref{perfex}, it follows that the map
$K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem plus perfect case

nodes.name: Functorial henselian ind-smooth cover R' -> R
nodes.statement: Recall that if $R$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra, we can make a functorial surjection to $R$ from a polynomial algebra, namely take the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{F}_p[x_a]_{a\in R}$ on variables indexed by the elements of $R$ with the map $x_a\mapsto a$.  Let $R'\rightarrow R$ denote the henselization of this surjection at its kernel; thus $R'$ is a functorial ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra surjecting onto $R$ with henselian kernel.  Moreover, $R\mapsto R'$ evidently commutes with filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: Functorial henselian ind-smooth cover R' -> R

nodes.name: nu~^m_r(R) := H^1_et(Spec R', TC homotopy sheaf); commutes with filtered colimit
nodes.statement:
Define
for $m \geq 0$
$$\widetilde{\nu^m_r}(R) := H^1(\operatorname{Spec}(R')_\sub{\'{e}t};\pi_{m}(\mathcal{TC}/p^r)).$$
Since the coefficient presheaf $\pi_{m}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r)$ commutes with filtered
colimits by Corollary \ref{TCring}, this \'etale cohomology group commutes with filtered colimits in $R'$ by standard cocontinuity arguments.  Combining with the previous, we find that $\widetilde{\nu^m_r}(-)$ commutes with filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: nu~^m_r(R) := H^1_et(Spec R', TC homotopy sheaf); commutes with filtered colimits

nodes.name: Descent spectral sequence gives the natural transformation
nodes.statement: Furthermore, since $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ has \'{e}tale $p$-cohomological dimension $\leq 1$, the descent spectral sequence for $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ gives a natural map $\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r)$ (compare with the proofs of Theorem \ref{GHGL} and Theorem \ref{padicetaleKthy}).  Composing with the map on $\mathrm{TC}$ induced by $R'\rightarrow R$ defines the desired natural transformation $\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)$.
nodes.statement_short: Descent spectral sequence gives the natural transformation

nodes.name: R' is ind-smooth local: splitting holds for R'
nodes.statement:
Now assume $R$ is local.  Then $R'$ is too, since a henselian ideal is radical, and it is moreover ind-smooth.  Thus the argument recalled before the statement of the theorem, based on the results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, shows that
$$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus \pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r).$$
nodes.statement_short: R' is ind-smooth local: splitting holds for R'

nodes.name: Main theorem gives a long exact sequence
nodes.statement:
On the other hand our main rigidity theorem, Theorem \ref{mainthm}, gives a long exact sequence
$$\ldots\rightarrow\pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r)\oplus \pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)\rightarrow\ldots.$$
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem gives a long exact sequence

nodes.name: Long exact sequence splits; decomposition for R
nodes.statement:
Combining shows both that this long exact sequence breaks up into short exact sequences and that 
$$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus\pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r),$$
as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence splits; decomposition for R

nodes.name: Two claims: etale-local surjectivity and rigidity of the cokernel
nodes.statement:
We claim that the map $\pi - \overline{F}$ is surjective locally in the \'etale topology 
and the cokernel satisfies rigidity for henselian pairs.
nodes.statement_short: Two claims: etale-local surjectivity and rigidity of the cokernel

nodes.name: Lifts to R - F, etale surjective by Morrow
nodes.statement:
The first claim follows because the composite map 
\[ W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \stackrel{R}{\to} W_r \Omega_R^{m}
\xrightarrow{\pi  - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \]
actually lifts to the map $W_{r+1}\Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{R - F} W_r
\Omega_R^{m}$, which is a surjection in the \'etale topology thanks to
\cite[Cor. 4.1(ii)]{Morrow-HW}.
nodes.statement_short: Lifts to R - F, etale surjective by Morrow

nodes.name: Diagram with kernel L as in Proposition 4.31
nodes.statement:
Second, 
let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. 
To see that $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ is rigid, we can imitate the
strategy of Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}. 
Namely, we 
let $L$ denote the kernel of the surjection
$W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_{R/I}^{m}/d
V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ and 
contemplate the commutative diagram
\[ \xymatrix{
 & & W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d]  \\
W_{r+1} \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \ar[rru]^{R - F} \ar[r]^R &   W_r
\Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d]  \ar[r]^{\psi} &  L \ar[d]  \\
W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \ar[d]  \ar[r]^R &  W_r \Omega_R^{m}\ar[d]
\ar[r]^-{\pi - \overline{F}} &  W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1}
\Omega_R^{m} \ar[d]  \\ 
W_{r+1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^R &  W_{r} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^-{\pi -
\overline{F}} &  W_r
\Omega_{R/I}^{m}/ d V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m}
}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Diagram with kernel L as in Proposition 4.31

nodes.name: Snake lemma: suffices psi surjective; relative forms surject onto L
nodes.statement:
To prove rigidity, it suffices by the snake lemma  to show that $\psi:W_r \Omega_{(R,
I)}^{m} \to L$ is a surjection. 
Note that the kernel $L$ is surjected upon by the relative forms $W_r
\Omega_{(R, I)}^{m}$; this follows easily from the fact that $\Omega_R^{m}
\to \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ is a surjection.
nodes.statement_short: Snake lemma: suffices psi surjective; relative forms surject onto L

nodes.name: psi surjective by Lemma 5.29
nodes.statement:
Thus, the surjectivity of $\psi$ now follows from the surjectivity of $R - F:
W_{r+1} \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)} \to W_r \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)}$ 
given by Lemma~\ref{lemma_drw1}.
nodes.statement_short: psi surjective by Lemma 5.29

nodes.name: Compute nu~ via the resolution on R', then pass to R by rigidity
nodes.statement:
Now we prove the proposition.  Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra and recall that, by definition,
$$\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R) = H^1( \mathrm{Spec}(R')_{\mathrm{et}}; \pi_m (
\mathcal{TC}/p^r)),$$
where $R'\rightarrow R$ is a surjective map from an ind-smooth
$\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra with henselian kernel. Since $\pi_m ( \mathcal{TC}/p^r)
\simeq W_r \Omega^{m}_{\mathrm{log}}$ (as
\'etale sheaves) over the ind-smooth $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ by the
results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, we can use the resolution of 
\eqref{piminusF2} in the \'etale topology and the fact that the two terms of
\eqref{piminusF2} have no higher cohomology on affines to calculate this etale cohomology group. It follows that 
$\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R)$ identifies with $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ on $R'$. Since we have just seen this cokernel satisfies
rigidity, we can replace $R'$ by $R$, whence the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Compute nu~ via the resolution on R', then pass to R by rigidity

nodes.name: Recall definition via R'
nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra and recall that, by definition,
$$\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R) = H^1( \mathrm{Spec}(R')_{\mathrm{et}}; \pi_m (
\mathcal{TC}/p^r)),$$
where $R'\rightarrow R$ is a surjective map from an ind-smooth
$\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra with henselian kernel.
nodes.statement_short: Recall definition via R'

nodes.name: Geisser--Levine/Hesselholt and the resolution compute H^1
nodes.statement:
Since $\pi_m ( \mathcal{TC}/p^r)
\simeq W_r \Omega^{m}_{\mathrm{log}}$ (as
\'etale sheaves) over the ind-smooth $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ by the
results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, we can use the resolution of 
\eqref{piminusF2} in the \'etale topology and the fact that the two terms of
\eqref{piminusF2} have no higher cohomology on affines to calculate this etale cohomology group.
nodes.statement_short: Geisser--Levine/Hesselholt and the resolution compute H^1

nodes.name: nu~ = coker(pi - Fbar) on R'
nodes.statement:
It follows that 
$\widetilde{\nu_r^{m}}(R)$ identifies with $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ on $R'$.
nodes.statement_short: nu~ = coker(pi - Fbar) on R'

nodes.name: Rigidity replaces R by R
nodes.statement:
Since we have just seen this cokernel satisfies
rigidity, we can replace $R'$ by $R$, whence the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Rigidity replaces R by R
